title: Simulation and performance analysis of the charging/discharging processes of a condensation thermal accumulator for solar- assisted heat pump system
summary: Driven by China's carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals and the growing demand for clean heating, solar-assisted heat pump systems have attracted increasing attention because of their ability to integrate solar energy, ambient air heat
content: Driven by China's carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals and the growing demand for clean heating, solar-assisted heat pump systems have attracted increasing attention because of their ability to integrate solar energy, ambient air heat, and phase-change thermal energy storage. As a key component, the condensation thermal accumulator combines refrigerant condensation, heat storage, and user-side heat release, and its performance directly affects system stability and energy efficiency. In this study, a two-dimensional transient CFD model was developed for a condensation thermal accumulator with an upper paraffin phase change region and a lower water region. The enthalpy-porosity method was used to model paraffin melting and solidification, while the Boussinesq approximation was applied to account for natural convection. Following mesh and time-step sensitivity analyses and comparison with measured mean PCM temperatures, the model was used to study charging and discharging processes and the effects of tube diameter and spacing. Results show that paraffin undergoes sensible heating, latent heat absorption, and a nearly stable stage during the charging process. During the discharging process, natural convection weakens and conduction becomes dominant. Increasing tube diameter from 14 to 20 mm increased stored heat at 8000 s from 24.14 to 27.97 kW·h. Effective discharged heat increased from 20.87 to 24.11 kW·h, while effective discharging efficiency remained approximately 86%. Increasing tube spacing from 38 to 56 mm shortened the time to reach 99% liquid fraction from 8860 to 7610 s. It also increased effective discharging efficiency from 86.24% to 87.94%. These findings provide quantitative guidance for CTA geometry selection under the investigated operating conditions.

title: Data, code and supplemental material for Storage memory and geometric information in breach-flood peak bounds
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Data, computational programs and supplemental material accompanying "Storage memory and geometric information in breach-flood peak bounds" by Shuchang Zhang and Shaoqi Kong (College of Mining Engineering, Taiyuan University of Technology).
content: Data, computational programs and supplemental material accompanying "Storage memory and geometric information in breach-flood peak bounds" by Shuchang Zhang and Shaoqi Kong (College of Mining Engineering, Taiyuan University of Technology). Version 2.0.0 extends the immutable baseline release with a dimensionless depletion benchmark, 3,535 constructed parameter cases, 120 independent ODE comparisons, 108 control-optimization runs, and updated figures. It retains calculations for five CanBreach parameter histories and an audit of 143 laser-reconstructed geometry records. These are model-based numerical results and public-data reanalyses; the source discharge/storage discrepancy remains unresolved and independent physical predictive validation is not claimed. Supplement.pdf contains Sections S1–S8, Figures S1–S4 and Tables S1–S3, with derivations, source-data checks, numerical comparisons and the registered-snapshot extension. Data and code.zip contains the source observations, processing and routing programs, numerical results, generated tables, figures, licenses and provenance records. Extract it and run python src/reproduce.py as described in README.md. Checksums are recorded in technical/file_manifest.json. The article and submission correspondence are separate. Licenses: the authors’ derived data, figures, documentation and supplemental material use CC BY 4.0; their programs use MIT. Third-party originals retain their terms: Walsh et al., Borealis version 1.0, https://doi.org/10.5683/SP2/HLJQVB (CC0 1.0); Rifai et al., Zenodo version V2.4, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.1494800 (CC BY 3.0). title: From Return on Investment to Return on Environment Investing in a Sustainable Planet
source: International Journal of Social Science Studies
summary: This desk-review article examines the ecological damage and lost investment opportunities associated with the prevailing economic paradigm. It proposes Return on Environment (RoEn) as a complement to Return on Investment (ROI) for evaluatin
content: This desk-review article examines the ecological damage and lost investment opportunities associated with the prevailing economic paradigm. It proposes Return on Environment (RoEn) as a complement to Return on Investment (ROI) for evaluating and encouraging regenerative, nature-positive investment. The global economy has transgressed seven of nine planetary boundaries, while more than half of global gross domestic product depends moderately or highly on nature. Yet environmental, social, and governance (ESG) and impact-investing frameworks often define “impact” by how funds are spent rather than by verified changes in ecosystems. Drawing on ecological economics, natural capital accounting, the practice of monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV), and selected nature-finance cases, the article makes three contributions. First, it defines RoEn across six preliminary dimensions: carbon, water, biodiversity, resilience, natural capital, and community. Second, it presents a five-level Environmental Impact Continuum—destructive, harmful, neutral, beneficial, and regenerative—and illustrates each level with investment examples. Third, it proposes a scoring rubric that rates investments across the six dimensions, discounts unverified gains, and combines a monetized RoEn ratio with a non-monetized score for reporting alongside ROI. The article concludes that nature is economic infrastructure; impact should require measurable environmental outcomes verified independently and by communities; and investment horizons should extend across multi-decade ecological and financial cycles while centering communities most exposed to ecological breakdown. The tools required for large-scale ecological regeneration already exist.

title: Synthesis of MgO nanoparticles stabilized on coconut husk‐derived biochar via pyrolysis and their role in enhancing rice salt tolerance through seed treatment
summary: Abstract The pyrolysis of coconut husk (CH) impregnated with Mg(OH) 2 at 400 °C produced MgO nanoparticles/coconut husk biochar (MgO NPs/CHB) containing 1.29% MgO (w/w). The biochar yield from Mg(OH) 2 -treated biomass reached 51.47%, which
content: Abstract The pyrolysis of coconut husk (CH) impregnated with Mg(OH) 2 at 400 °C produced MgO nanoparticles/coconut husk biochar (MgO NPs/CHB) containing 1.29% MgO (w/w). The biochar yield from Mg(OH) 2 -treated biomass reached 51.47%, which was higher than that obtained from untreated CH (41.23%). The morphology and particle size of MgO NPs were characterized by scanning and transmission electron microscopy, with average sizes of about 24.4 nm and 28.4 nm, respectively. The structural and physicochemical properties of the material were analyzed using x-ray diffraction, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, and N 2 adsorption-desorption analysis. Seed priming with MgO NPs/CHB at a concentration of 100 mg MgO/L improved the ability of rice seedlings to cope with salt-induced stress, as indicated by increased chlorophyll content, plant height, and root length after 7 days of salt treatment under 75 mM NaCl. In addition, MgO NPs/CHB priming alleviated salt-induced stress in rice seedlings, as evidenced by reduced activities of antioxidant enzymes compared to the salt-stressed control, such as superoxide dismutase and catalase, lower malondialdehyde content, and an increased K + /Na + ratio in leaves compared to the non-primed salt-stressed control.

title: Siderophores and siderophore-associated metabolites from Antarctic Pseudomonas sp. ANT_H12B contribute to iron and phosphorus mobilization in soils with contrasting properties
summary: Iron (Fe) oxy(hydr)oxides regulate soil Fe and phosphorus (P) cycling, but how bacterial siderophores and co-produced metabolites mobilize these nutrients across pH remains unclear. We hypothesized that siderophore-mediated Fe complexation
content: Iron (Fe) oxy(hydr)oxides regulate soil Fe and phosphorus (P) cycling, but how bacterial siderophores and co-produced metabolites mobilize these nutrients across pH remains unclear. We hypothesized that siderophore-mediated Fe complexation and P mobilization depend on pH and mineral crystallinity and that siderophore-associated metabolites (SAM) are more effective than purified siderophores. A purified pyoverdine-like siderophore fraction from Antarctic Pseudomonas strain ANT_H12B was chemically and spectroscopically characterized and evaluated for Fe³ + complexation from FeCl 3 between pH 5 and 9. Iron mobilization from ferrihydrite (Fh), goethite (Gt), and hematite (Hm) was examined at pH 5.5 and 8.5 across mineral concentrations of 0.5–2 g L⁻¹; purified siderophores and SAM were compared in four P-deficient soils of contrasting pH. Iron³ + complexation increased from 6% at pH 5 to 10% at pH 9, reflecting ligand deprotonation. Ferrihydrite showed the greatest dissolution, although Fe release at pH 8.5 was 30% and 37% lower than at pH 5.5 at 1 and 1.5 g L⁻¹, respectively. Conversely, Gt dissolution at 2 g L⁻¹ was 40% higher at pH 8.5, whereas Hm showed the lowest dissolution, reaching 3 and 1.9 μM at pH 5.5 and 8.5, respectively. Purified siderophores moderately increased Olsen-P in neutral and high-Fe alkaline soils, whereas SAM increased Olsen-P approximately 1- to 26-fold across all soils, with the greatest effect in high-Fe alkaline soil. SAM also increased soluble P 11- to 40-fold and NaOH-EDTA-extractable P by 25–104% relative to controls. The results support our hypothesis, showing that siderophores contribute to Fe and P mobilization but act more effectively within SAM, where organic acids provide complementary dissolution and sorption-competition mechanisms. This finding agrees with previous ANT_H12B studies reporting improved nutrient availability and plant performance and supports using unpurified metabolite mixtures for sustainable P management. Indeed, retaining the co-produced mixture could reduce purification requirements and preserve complementary functions relevant to sustainable P management.

title: Heterogeneous Transition Capacity for Urban Carbon-Neutral Development in China
summary: Achieving urban carbon neutrality requires not only ambitious mitigation targets but also urban conditions capable of supporting implementation. However, whether cities possess such transition capacity remains insufficiently understood. Her
content: Achieving urban carbon neutrality requires not only ambitious mitigation targets but also urban conditions capable of supporting implementation. However, whether cities possess such transition capacity remains insufficiently understood. Here, we develop an empirical framework to evaluate urban transition capacity across 336 Chinese cities by integrating carbon emission characteristics, policy and technology, ecological endowment, and energy potential. We identify substantial heterogeneity: 40 cities are classified as high-capacity, while most cities fall into medium- or low-capacity groups with systematically different obstacle compositions. High-capacity cities exhibit stronger conditions across all four capacity dimensions, but weighted obstacle structures shift progressively across groups. Policy and technology represent the largest relative obstacle component throughout, whereas the contribution of carbon emission characteristics increases markedly as transition capacity declines. Together, these results link multidimensional capacity assessment with group-specific obstacle diagnostics across a large urban system. The findings question the suitability of uniform mitigation strategies across heterogeneous urban contexts and support capacity-oriented governance that aligns transition priorities with city-specific conditions.

title: CRISPR-enhanced microalgae for carbon sequestration and carotenoid production: opportunities and fundamental constraints
summary: Microalgae represent a promising biological platform for CO2 sequestration and the sustainable production of high-value metabolites, particularly carotenoids such as lutein and astaxanthin. However, industrial performance remains constraine
content: Microalgae represent a promising biological platform for CO2 sequestration and the sustainable production of high-value metabolites, particularly carotenoids such as lutein and astaxanthin. However, industrial performance remains constrained by low carbon conversion efficiency, reduced photosynthetic performance, and competing metabolic fluxes that limit product yield. The emergence of CRISPR/Cas-based genome engineering has enabled precise and multiplexed modulation of microalgal metabolic networks, offering new opportunities to overcome these limitations. This review critically evaluates CRISPR-enabled engineering strategies for improving carbon assimilation, photosynthetic efficiency, and carotenoid biosynthesis in microalgae. We discuss advances in transformation and delivery systems across diverse species, CRISPR interference, CRISPR activation, and multiplexed pathway rewiring. Targeted modifications of light-harvesting complexes, carbon concentrating mechanisms, and key carotenoid biosynthetic enzymes are discussed with their reported impacts on biomass accumulation, CO2 fixation, and pigment productivity. Emerging evidence indicates that while pathway-specific genetic interventions can significantly enhance metabolic accumulation, these improvements are often not proportionally reflected in whole-cell carbon fixation, revealing underlying constraints imposed by energy allocation, redox balance, and regulatory network coupling. Finally, we highlight the potential of synthetic regulatory circuits and programmable transcriptional control as next-generation tools for dynamic regulation of metabolic fluxes rather than static gene-level modifications. By integrating molecular engineering strategies with physiological and system-level constraints, this review provides a critical framework for developing robust microalgal cell factories for sustainable bioproduction and climate mitigation. title: Natural resource-based view in sustainability practices among U.S. fashion businesses: insights from fashion entrepreneurs
summary: Fashion small businesses (FSBs) play an increasingly important role in advancing sustainability within the fashion industry, yet little is known about how they leverage sustainability as a source of competitive advantage. Drawing on the Nat
content: Fashion small businesses (FSBs) play an increasingly important role in advancing sustainability within the fashion industry, yet little is known about how they leverage sustainability as a source of competitive advantage. Drawing on the Natural Resource-Based View (NRBV) and Dynamic Capabilities theory, this study examines how U.S. fashion small businesses integrate sustainability into their business models and develop sustainability-related competitive advantages. Using qualitative, semi-structured interviews with 13 CEOs and founders across diverse segments of the U.S. fashion industry, this study identifies distinct entrepreneurship types and examines how each exploits NRBV resources and dynamic capabilities in sustainability practices. The findings reveal five entrepreneurship types—SME, SME with social entrepreneurship orientation (SME-SE), SME with environmental entrepreneurship orientation (SME-EE), Innovation-Driven Enterprise (IDE), and IDE with environmental entrepreneurship orientation (IDE-EE). The results further show that clean technology serves as the primary distinguishing resource between SME- and IDE-oriented firms, while SMEs primarily leverage pollution prevention and product stewardship through locally embedded business ecosystems. In addition, firms with stronger dynamic capabilities are more likely to integrate sustainability into their core business models and develop long-term competitive advantages through resource reconfiguration and innovation. This study extends the NRBV literature by providing an empirically grounded typology of U.S. fashion small businesses and demonstrating how entrepreneurship orientation shapes the development of sustainability resources and dynamic capabilities. The findings offer practical guidance for fashion entrepreneurs, industry practitioners, and policymakers seeking to strengthen sustainability transitions among small businesses.

title: Post-military urban regeneration in Germany: a comparative study of Bornstedter Feld, Scharnhauser Park, and Vauban
summary: In the wake of German reunification and the withdrawal of foreign military forces, vast tracts of former military land became available for redevelopment across the country. This paper investigates how three notable post-military sites (Bor
content: In the wake of German reunification and the withdrawal of foreign military forces, vast tracts of former military land became available for redevelopment across the country. This paper investigates how three notable post-military sites (Bornstedter Feld in Potsdam, Scharnhauser Park in Ostfildern, and Vauban in Freiburg) were transformed into sustainable urban districts through distinct governance models and planning strategies. Utilizing a qualitative, comparative case study methodology, the research analyzes each site’s approach to governance, citizen participation, financial mechanisms, sustainability, and legal frameworks, particularly the use of §165 of the Federal Building Code (BauGB). The comparative analysis highlights that the success of post-military redevelopment depends not only on legal tools or financial models but also on civic inclusion and ecological vision. While all three projects achieved functional reintegration and urban quality, their varied outcomes underscore the importance of aligning governance structures with context-specific goals. These German experiences offer valuable lessons for cities in Korea, Eastern Europe, and post-conflict regions facing similar challenges in military land reuse. The study contributes to the broader discourse on adaptive urbanism, participatory governance, and sustainable redevelopment of brownfield sites.

title: Developing a Resilient Workforce for a Technologically Disrupted Automotive Service Industry
summary: The purpose of this workforce capability study is to quantify the magnitude of the challenge for tertiary education teachers. The automotive service sector is continuously evolving, so it is essential to stay updated on vehicle innovations
content: The purpose of this workforce capability study is to quantify the magnitude of the challenge for tertiary education teachers. The automotive service sector is continuously evolving, so it is essential to stay updated on vehicle innovations and technological changes. As new technology is introduced in vehicles, the repair workflow changes and a technician cannot simply repair the fault, as sensors and software will need to be recalibrated for function. Hence, it is critical in the tertiary sector for teachers to remain current with automotive technological advancements. Available literature from global policy makers, vehicle manufacturers and national agencies were reviewed to determine the anticipated trends and disruptions to meet sustainability targets. Literature indicates that legacy technology combined with software will require a major reskilling across the service sector, requiring competencies and improving the development of human soft skills. Disruptions are hard to predict, and this study aims to identify how non-traditional skills will form the required workforce capability in the automotive service sector. Key industry leaders, service technicians and tertiary education teachers were interviewed, and findings from this study suggest industry stakeholders need to work collaboratively across the automotive service sector to develop service technicians’ knowledge and skillsets. The triangulation of literature and data suggests the reduction of the knowledge gap of graduates for the automotive service industry requires all industry stakeholders to make informed decisions to take their workforce forward and avoid redundancies. Recommendations are made for visionary, innovative and planned decision-making for the future of the industry. Collaboration with standard-setting authorities, industry partners and educational institutes, and a national vocational education and training framework will ensure the future workforce for the industry has the right capability and set of skills.

title: Land use change reshaped soil carbon dynamics in Northern China
summary: Northern China has experienced some of the most intensive land use changes globally, yet the consequent impacts on soil carbon dynamics and regional source-sink patterns, particularly the divergent responses of soil organic carbon (SOC) and
tags: Land use, land-use change and forestry
content: Northern China has experienced some of the most intensive land use changes globally, yet the consequent impacts on soil carbon dynamics and regional source-sink patterns, particularly the divergent responses of soil organic carbon (SOC) and soil inorganic carbon (SIC), remain poorly quantified. This study examined how land use change reshapes SOC and SIC pools and modulates their sensitivity to environmental drivers. Using nationwide soil survey data from the 1980s and 2010s, we applied random forest models and partial least squares structural equation modeling to disentangle the responces SOC and SIC pools for land use and environmental change. Results revealed that Northern China functioned as a net soil carbon source over the 30-year interval, losing approximately 0.56 Gt of SOC and 0.56 Gt of SIC. Land use type emerged as the dominant control on carbon source-sink patterns. Grassland transitioned into strong carbon sources driven primarily by SIC losses of 1.51 Gt, whereas unutilized land exhibited estimated net carbon gains with apparent SIC accumulation of 2.06 Gt. Beyond altering carbon stocks, land use change reversed regional source-sink patterns and markedly heightened the sensitivity of soil carbon dynamics to environmental changes with explanatory strength increment of 0.11 for SOC and 0.09 for SIC, respectively. Specifically, SOC responded primarily to biotic drivers such as vegetation productivity, while SIC exhibited tighter coupling with increasing atmospheric CO 2 fluctuations. The main contribution of this study is revealing how SOC and SIC respond differently to environmental drivers following land use change. Practically, these results indicate that regional carbon management strategies must fully consider land use change effects and explicitly include soil inorganic carbon in carbon neutrality accounting frameworks.
