title: Design of a monolithic cellulose Janus-like membrane for oil/water separation
summary: Abstract Janus membranes offer a good solution for oil/water mixtures due to their opposite wettability, but existing designs often suffer from limitations arising from complex, resource-intensive fabrication procedures. This study proposes
content: Abstract Janus membranes offer a good solution for oil/water mixtures due to their opposite wettability, but existing designs often suffer from limitations arising from complex, resource-intensive fabrication procedures. This study proposes a cellulose-based monolithic Janus-like membrane prepared by non-solvent-induced phase separation (NIPS) from cellulose acetate followed by alkaline deacetylation and unilateral silanization (TEOS/MTES). The resulting membrane exhibits asymmetric wettability (hydrophobic: 91°, hydrophilic: ~0°). Structural and chemical characterization (SEM, EDS, FTIR, and BET/BJH) confirms the formation of a siloxane-containing surface layer, the integrity of the cellulose network, and a distribution of the pores toward the nanoscale, with a specific surface area of 26.9 m 2 /g. Gravitational peanut oil/water tests reveal high fluxes (3300–5527 Lm −2 h − 1 ) with an apparent volumetric oil-retention efficiency of up to 95%, while for water/hexane, the apparent volumetric oil-retention efficiency reached 96.93% with a flux of 3950.62 Lm −2 h − 1 . The membrane retains excellent mechanical robustness (3.50 MPa), with a breaking force of 5.23 N, withstanding repeated deformations including axial rolling, compression, and bending, without cracking or delamination. This Janus-like membrane mimics the properties of Janus membranes while relying on a simplified, energy-efficient, and environmentally friendly fabrication strategy, and could represent a promising option for efficient, sustainable, and high-performance oil/water separation.

title: Co-firing of upgraded biomass towards flexible CO2 reduction for coal-fired power plants in China
summary: The increasing trend in CO 2 emissions from fossil fuels has accelerated the renewable energy development, especially in China, the world's largest CO 2 emitter, which targets carbon peaking by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2060. Co-firing
content: The increasing trend in CO 2 emissions from fossil fuels has accelerated the renewable energy development, especially in China, the world's largest CO 2 emitter, which targets carbon peaking by 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2060. Co-firing of raw biomass is a promising carbon–neutral energy option in China, but its application is limited to only 10% incorporation with stable combustion performance. Therefore, in this study comprehensively assessed biomass upgrading methods, including torrefaction, pelletization, pyrolysis, and gasification, demonstrated that upgraded biomass exhibited significant potential as an attractive, feasible, and sustainable alternative fuel for a low-carbon approach to co-firing in existing PC power plants. The existing research work revealed that the recent Chinese energy policies support the co-firing of biomass, while biomass upgrading technologies are under development and need bioenergy-supported policies. The results showed that upgraded biomass enables higher co-firing ratios in PC boilers, achieving up to 50% substitution on an energy basis and reducing net CO 2 emissions by up to 50% compared with full coal combustion. Co-firing of the upgraded biomass not only maintains the high efficiency of PC and CFB furnaces, but also has the potential to lower their carbon footprint and NO x emissions. Additionally, the effectiveness of the co-firing strategy for achieving carbon neutrality is evaluated. This review paper can assist in identifying the potential methods that can increase the biomass-to-coal ratio during direct co-firing in existing PC furnaces without requiring large modifications.

title: Developmentalism without a developmental state: Fragmented capacities and green hydrogen in Chile
summary: How do states with limited economic resources pursue ambitious green industrial transitions when their outcomes remain uncertain? This article examines this question through Chile's green hydrogen strategy in Patagonia, where ministries, re
content: How do states with limited economic resources pursue ambitious green industrial transitions when their outcomes remain uncertain? This article examines this question through Chile's green hydrogen strategy in Patagonia, where ministries, regional governments, state-owned enterprises, and CORFO must coordinate within a predominantly neoliberal political economy. Drawing on 27 sequential qualitative interviews with state actors and lay participants, alongside documentary analysis, we show that the transition is assembled through uneven capacities rather than a unified developmental apparatus. First, regional actors build a green development project by translating global decarbonization into a locally grounded agenda and assembling the infrastructure, skills, partnerships, and other enabling conditions required for private investment, despite constrained fiscal resources and legislative authority. Second, the “hyper-sectoral” organization of the Chilean state makes coordination a central developmental task: strategic, regulatory, fiscal, and administrative capacities sit in different organizations, while regional governments use relational, discursive, and performative power to mobilize actors they cannot command. Third, development is also a matter of governing expectations. Official promises encourage residents to invest in education and occupations linked to anticipated jobs, even as uncertainty persists over whether projects will materialize and who will benefit. Taken together, these findings show that state capacity is not a fixed national attribute but is distributed unevenly across organizations and territorial scales. They move beyond the neoliberal-developmental state binary by showing how fragmented states coordinate green industrial projects even when their material outcomes remain uncertain.

title: Editorial: Green biomanufacturing by industrial microorganisms: precise regulation and system optimization
summary: A first theme concerns the design of green catalytic systems that improve the physicochemical properties of high-value bioactive compounds. The contribution by the group exemplifies this direction through the whole-cell-catalyzed cinnamoyla
content: A first theme concerns the design of green catalytic systems that improve the physicochemical properties of high-value bioactive compounds. The contribution by the group exemplifies this direction through the whole-cell-catalyzed cinnamoylation of phillyrin (Yang et al., 2026). By combining Aspergillus oryzae whole cells with hydrophobic natural deep eutectic solvents (NADESs) in co-solvent systems, the authors achieved conversion rates of 97.32-99.00% and excellent 6′-regioselectivity (>99%) under optimized conditions. Importantly, the biocatalysts retained 80.09-97.95% of their original activity after six consecutive cycles. This work underscores how the rational pairing of biocatalysts with sustainable reaction media can expand the chemical space accessible to biotransformation. Future research could extend this system to bioreactor scale-up, examine NADES recycling, and elucidate the molecular basis of membrane permeability changes.A second theme addresses the stability and productivity of industrial enzymes. The study on ancestral alginate lyase engineering provides a compelling example (Mu et al., 2026). Starting from a Flavobacterium sp. enzyme heterologously expressed in Escherichia coli, the authors applied ancestral sequence inference to generate variants AncAlyA1 and AncAlyA2, which exhibited 132.4% and 87.3% increases in catalytic activity, together with markedly improved thermal and pH stability. AncAlyA2 retained approximately 60% of its activity under extreme conditions. Coupled with fed-batch fermentation strategy, enzyme activities of 5164.8 U/mL and 4220.1 U/mL were achieved. This study illustrates how evolutionary reconstruction, when integrated with process-level feeding optimization, can deliver biocatalysts that meet industrial performance criteria.The third contribution shifts the focus from biocatalyst design to intelligent process control. To overcome overflow metabolism and the heavy reliance on manual intervention in high-density E. coli fermentation, the authors developed an artificial neural network (ANN)based autonomous control system, NeuroStat-Ctrl (Zhou et al., 2026). Using superfolder green fluorescent protein as a reporter, they first optimized DO-stat feeding and induction, achieving a 52.85% increase in specific fluorescence intensity. The ANN model recognized dissolved oxygen baselines in real time (R² = 0.998) and was integrated with feeding control logic to enable fully autonomous operation. By mitigating feeding deviations inherent in fixed-threshold strategies and preventing metabolic overflow, this system offers a standardized and intelligent solution for high-throughput strain screening and parallel bioreactor validation.Microbial consortia represent an avenue for enhancing carbon efficiency and product diversity. The study on engineered Clostridium acetobutylicum and Clostridium ljungdahlii syntrophic cocultures tackles the intrinsic carbon loss of glycolysis (Otten et al., 2025). By transforming C. ac

title: Beyond emission limits: a scenario-based integration of best available techniques and life cycle assessment
summary: Under contemporary conditions of increasingly stringent environmental regulation and the transition toward a circular economy, industry requires analytical tools capable not only of confirming compliance with Best Available Techniques (BAT)
content: Under contemporary conditions of increasingly stringent environmental regulation and the transition toward a circular economy, industry requires analytical tools capable not only of confirming compliance with Best Available Techniques (BAT) criteria but also of critically rethinking the mechanisms of their practical implementation. The standard BAT framework is characterised by methodological limitations: its application is hindered by high technological variability, insufficient consideration of spatial factors, and the absence of flexible scenario-based models necessary for assessing the environmental implications of technological modifications. This article introduces ParaBAT, an original methodology developed as an innovative approach aimed at expanding the analytical capabilities of existing BAT instruments. The proposed method integrates energy and material flow analysis with spatial - dynamic scenario modelling, enabling the assessment of technologies not as static systems but as entities sensitive to local contextual conditions, industrial structural changes, and regulatory policies.

title: When and How Firms Can Promote Green Innovation for Sustainable Development: A Holistic Examination
summary: Green finance has become a key instrument for addressing environmental degradation and supporting sustainable development. However, existing literature has largely focused on its outcomes, with limited attention to the factors that contribu
content: Green finance has become a key instrument for addressing environmental degradation and supporting sustainable development. However, existing literature has largely focused on its outcomes, with limited attention to the factors that contribute to its effectiveness. Using an input-oriented perspective, this study examines the roles of green innovation, financial development, and research and development (R&D) in promoting green financing and sustainable development. Empirical data from thirty-nine manufacturing companies in Saudi Arabia covering 2011–2025 are analyzed using partial least squares, generalized method of moments, fixed-effects, and random-effects models. The findings demonstrate that green innovation, financial development, and R&D significantly contribute to the effectiveness of green financing. The transition from conventional product innovation to green finance is found to be less challenging than the development of eco-friendly technological innovations, as environmentally friendly products can generate positive financial returns. The study provides policy insights for promoting sustainable industrial growth.

title: Diffusion-acidity cooperative effect in ZnZrOx/SAPO-34 tandem catalysts for enhanced CO2-to-propylene conversion
summary: Achieving carbon neutrality requires the development of rational catalytic strategies for efficient CO 2 utilization, particularly toward propylene, which global demand continues to increase. Herein, a diffusion-acidity cooperative effect s
content: Achieving carbon neutrality requires the development of rational catalytic strategies for efficient CO 2 utilization, particularly toward propylene, which global demand continues to increase. Herein, a diffusion-acidity cooperative effect strategy is proposed and implemented using ZnZrO x /SAPO-34 tandem catalysts to enhance propylene selectivity in CO 2 hydrogenation. Compared with a ZnZrO x /conventional SAPO-34 catalyst, which exhibits 29.4% propylene selectivity among hydrocarbons, the optimized ZnZrO x /SAPO-34 system delivers a CO 2 conversion of 19.2% with a substantially improved propylene selectivity of 52.6%, further rising to 57.4% at higher gas hourly space velocity. The results reveal that accelerating molecular diffusion within SAPO-34 promotes the rapid transport and transformation of hydrogenated intermediates formed on ZnZrO x , thereby suppressing undesired secondary hydrogenation pathways. Simultaneously, an increased content of strong Brönsted acid sites associated with Si(0Si,4Al) and Si(1Si,3Al) facilitates selective propylene formation. These findings suggest diffusion-acidity cooperative effect as a possible design principle for efficient CO 2 -to-propylene conversion over ZnZrO x /SAPO-34.

title: Renewable demand or sanctions? A descriptive decomposition of Russia–China mineral trade dynamics
summary: After comprehensive Western economic sanctions were imposed in 2022, Russia’s critical mineral exports to China surged from a pre-sanctions (2000–2021) annual average of $277 million per mineral to $1.02 billion per mineral in 2022–2024, bo
content: After comprehensive Western economic sanctions were imposed in 2022, Russia’s critical mineral exports to China surged from a pre-sanctions (2000–2021) annual average of $277 million per mineral to $1.02 billion per mineral in 2022–2024, both in current U.S. dollars — a 268% increase. This raises a fundamental attribution question: does the export surge stem from sanctions-induced trade diversion or from concurrent global renewable energy transition demand? Because the two processes occurred simultaneously, documenting the distinct contribution of each poses a significant empirical challenge. This study uses panel data on eight critical minerals exported from Russia to China over 2000–2024, employing three model specifications with progressively introduced controls based on fixed-effects regression: baseline sanctions estimation, renewable demand incorporation, and interaction testing. The sanctions effect coefficient falls from 3.682 to 0.946 and loses statistical significance once renewable energy demand variables are controlled for, whereas the renewable energy transition coefficient remains significant, at the 10% level or better, across the main robustness specifications. Analysis of differences across mineral categories suggests that sanctions effects appear primarily in highly standardized base materials, while technology-intensive minerals show stronger alignment with renewable demand patterns. Cross-mineral heterogeneity reveals a systematic gradient in renewable demand sensitivity — 1.135 for battery-critical materials against 0.237 for base materials — that mirrors the functional roles of minerals in the energy value chain and cannot be attributed to common time trends. The paper’s contribution lies in documenting three descriptive patterns: pre-existing import trends, cross-mineral heterogeneity, and coefficient trajectories under progressive controls, which together provide observational insights into Russia–China mineral trade dynamics.

title: A recent doubling of global warming rate signals a 1.5 °C breach by 2028
summary: Timely and accurate projections of when global warming will exceed the Paris Agreement’s 1.5 °C threshold are essential for effective climate policy. Existing estimates place this exceedance in the early 2030 s but carry substantial uncerta
content: Timely and accurate projections of when global warming will exceed the Paris Agreement’s 1.5 °C threshold are essential for effective climate policy. Existing estimates place this exceedance in the early 2030 s but carry substantial uncertainty. Here we analyze the latest observational temperature records through 2025 and identify a statistically significant doubling of the global warming rate during 2011–2025 (0.40 °C per decade) compared to 1971–2025 (0.20 °C per decade). Extrapolating this accelerated rate projects a crossing of the 1.5 °C threshold by 2028, nearly a decade earlier than previous estimates. Regional analyses attribute this acceleration primarily to intensified warming over East Asia–the North Pacific, mid-latitude Eurasia, and the South Atlantic–Antarctic regions. The ensemble mean of 26 climate models fails to capture the observed doubling of the warming rate, simulating a rate of only 0.29 °C per decade. These findings suggest a narrower window remains to limit warming to 1.5 °C, underscoring the urgency for rapid and substantial reductions in greenhouse gas emissions.

title: Impact of Insufficient Grid Flexibility on Renewable Energy Integration and Industrial Electricity Costs: A Case Study of Western Inner Mongolia
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: The high penetration of renewable energy has made power system flexibility constraints prominent, and the tension between clean electricity integration and industrial electricity costs has become a key factor restricting high-quality region
content: The high penetration of renewable energy has made power system flexibility constraints prominent, and the tension between clean electricity integration and industrial electricity costs has become a key factor restricting high-quality regional economic development. Taking the Western Inner Mongolia Power Grid-China's first provincial-level power grid with over 50% new energy installed capacity-as the research object, this study constructs an analytical framework of flexibility-system operation-industrial cost and analyzes the transmission mechanism through which insufficient grid flexibility drives up industrial electricity costs. The results show that dual constraints arise from rigid thermal power output during the heating season on the supply side (heating capacity accounts for about 66%) and the energy storage gap on the regulation side (storage-to-new-energy capacity ratio is about 10.7%), causing frequent alternation between power scarcity and surplus. Energy-intensive industries account for roughly 35% of grid electricity consumption, so price fluctuations directly affect regional industrial competitiveness. Flexibility constraints push up industrial electricity prices via three pathways: transmission congestion lifting nodal electricity prices, negative electricity prices shifting balancing costs to end users, and system operation charges embedding capacity costs into tariffs.

title: Evaluating pre- and post-failure behavior of a large waste dump by combining LEM and DEM approach: a case study from a hydropower station, China
summary: Large hydropower projects generate extensive waste dumps, posing significant environmental risks. Conventional 2D analyses fail to capture 3D topographic effects of typical gully terrain, while 3D discrete element method (DEM) are suitable
content: Large hydropower projects generate extensive waste dumps, posing significant environmental risks. Conventional 2D analyses fail to capture 3D topographic effects of typical gully terrain, while 3D discrete element method (DEM) are suitable but face calibration challenges for post-failure simulations. This study investigates a waste dump at the Yongjia Pumped Storage Power Station, China by integrating (1) a self-developed rigorous 3D Limit Equilibrium Method (LEM) for the pre-failure analysis and (2) a well-calibrated DEM for post-failure behavior. The 3D LEM reveals how meandering topography enhances stability, underscoring 3D analysis necessity. DEM simulations identify the interparticle friction coefficient (μ) as the controlling factor for debris flow trajectories and deposition patterns in winding valleys. A key highlight lies in the qualitative cross-model comparison linking the pre-failure and post-failure analyses, which supports μ = 0.2 as a representative value for the present DEM configuration and the engineering scenarios considered. This leads to a local mobilized area that remains confined within proximal slopes in DEM simulations, equivalent to a slight stability margin in LEM from the same local topographic constraints. However, failure risks persist under extreme conditions (e.g., drainage failure), where strength parameter uncertainties may arise from inadequate compaction or water lubrication (further reducing μ). Our cross-model results suggest specific reinforcement strategies to reduce the downstream risk.

title: Geography of Energy Sovereignty in Europe
summary: Energy sovereignty within the European Union (EU) has been undergoing significant transformation due to the intersecting pressures of climate policy, market integration, and geopolitical instability. Although article 194(2) of the Treaty on
content: Energy sovereignty within the European Union (EU) has been undergoing significant transformation due to the intersecting pressures of climate policy, market integration, and geopolitical instability. Although article 194(2) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union affirms the authority of the member states to determine their energy mix, recent initiatives such as the Fit for 55 package, the REPowerEU Plan, and solidarity mechanisms for gas and electricity have increased EU’s influence over national energy strategies. This paper examines the operation of sovereignty within this evolving framework of interdependence. Its authors contend that energy sovereignty in the EU has shifted from an absolute concept to a negotiated competence, mediated by legal, financial, and infrastructural interconnections.

title: Load shifting and operational cost optimization in cold-climate ground source heat pumps using phase change material (PCM) -based thermal energy storage
source: Pamukkale University Journal of Engineering Sciences
summary: This study investigates the integration of a phase change material (PCM) thermal storage tank with a ground-source heat pump (GSHP) system for residential heating in a cold-climate region (Erzurum, Türkiye) under a time-of-use (TOU) electri
content: This study investigates the integration of a phase change material (PCM) thermal storage tank with a ground-source heat pump (GSHP) system for residential heating in a cold-climate region (Erzurum, Türkiye) under a time-of-use (TOU) electricity pricing scheme. The configuration incorporating a PCM tank (ATP52) and a buffer tank was modeled using TRNSYS software to enhance energy storage during off-peak periods and reduce reliance on the grid during high-tariff hours. Nine different configurations were analyzed by varying the PCM mass fraction (75%, 100%, and 125%) and the charging set-point temperature, which was defined with respect to the PCM melting temperature. (Tmelting, Tmelting +2 °C, and Tmelting +5 °C). Simulation results show that PCM integration enables significant load shifting, reducing peak-period heat pump electricity use by up to 95% and lowering annual operating costs by 9% (from 163,848 TRY to 149.002 TRY), despite a 10% increase in total energy consumption. Consequently, annual electricity costs are reduced, with the highest savings observed in the PCM High–2 scenario. In addition, compared to a conventional water-based system, similar or greater economic benefits were achieved with a PCM tank volume of only 15 m3, versus the 50 m3 required for water storage. These results highlight the efficiency and economic advantages of PCM-based storage for optimizing building heating systems in cold climates under dynamic tariff structures.

title: Bio-Energy from Microbes: Advancements in Microbial Fuel Cells
summary: Creating scalable, sustainable, and economically feasible technologies to convert lignocellulosic polysaccharides into liquid fuels is widely regarded as a focal point of the global bioeconomy and an essential component of a multifaceted st
content: Creating scalable, sustainable, and economically feasible technologies to convert lignocellulosic polysaccharides into liquid fuels is widely regarded as a focal point of the global bioeconomy and an essential component of a multifaceted strategy to reach carbon neutrality. To fulfil this promise, we here highlight technological potential and obstacles. This chapter discusses potential future paths and the urgent need to overcome the challenges in order to increase the viability of using these microbes as a substitute for conventional fossil fuels.

title: Double energy vulnerability in Eastern Europe: quantifying and verifying regional sensitivity to the phenomenon
summary: This study considers 57 regions from 8 Eastern European countries and quantifies the sensitivity to double energy vulnerability of each region by developing a composite indicator. Double energy vulnerability is a concept describing simultan
content: This study considers 57 regions from 8 Eastern European countries and quantifies the sensitivity to double energy vulnerability of each region by developing a composite indicator. Double energy vulnerability is a concept describing simultaneous exposure to energy and transport poverty. Eastern European countries present high levels of double energy vulnerability; nonetheless, remaining an understudied macro-region. To understand the dependency between double energy vulnerability and rurality and tenure, the results are then compared with the rurality levels of the different regions, and to the national proportion spent on energy and transport services. The developed indicator provides an analysis of the phenomenon across Eastern Europe, quantifying regions' sensitivity to it by combining indicators stemming from different dimensions. Data from 2015 to 2024 was considered. Bulgaria is found to be the country presenting the highest level of double energy vulnerability. For the latter specifically, data at higher spatial resolution was utilised to have a more detailed understanding and to assess the obtained results. Finally, the results were verified by performing interviews with relevant experts in the field, considering also non-quantifiable aspects. The results provide a clearer picture of Eastern European regions' sensitivity to double energy vulnerability, highlighting the most sensitive ones.

title: From textbooks to classrooms: how climate change is represented and taught in Chinese high schools
summary: This study investigated how climate change was represented in Chinese senior high school textbooks and how teachers interpreted and taught climate change in the classrooms. Focusing on geography, biology, and chemistry textbooks published b
content: This study investigated how climate change was represented in Chinese senior high school textbooks and how teachers interpreted and taught climate change in the classrooms. Focusing on geography, biology, and chemistry textbooks published by the People’s Education Press in 2019, this study combined a qualitative content analysis of textbook materials with semi-structured interviews with 30 senior teachers from Zhejiang Province. The findings indicated that climate change content was moderately represented and unevenly distributed across disciplines. Geography provided the most integrated coverage, connecting scientific mechanisms, socioenvironmental impacts, and policy responses, whereas biology emphasised ecological consequences and chemistry focused on explaining the underlying mechanisms. Teacher interviews revealed that climate change topics were given low academic priority, largely because of their minimal presence in high-stakes examinations, leading to textbook-centred, shallow instruction. Nevertheless, teachers consistently highlighted environmental awareness and civic responsibility as key instructional goals. This study demonstrates that while textbooks provide foundational knowledge, disciplinary silos, exam-oriented content selection, and national policy priorities, such as carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, shape classroom enactment, resulting in fragmented climate-change learning experiences. These findings underscore the importance of curriculum alignment, assessments, and teacher support to foster more coherent, interdisciplinary, and action-oriented climate change education.

title: Injection-rate histories and well placement influence fault yielding during CO2 geological storage
summary: Abstract Safe CO 2 storage requires injection designs that manage both when faults yield and how yielding spreads, yet temporal schedules and well layouts are often evaluated separately. We developed a two-dimensional quasi-static hydromech
content: Abstract Safe CO 2 storage requires injection designs that manage both when faults yield and how yielding spreads, yet temporal schedules and well layouts are often evaluated separately. We developed a two-dimensional quasi-static hydromechanical model of immiscible CO 2 –brine flow around an offset normal fault and compared constant and variable-rate histories, well-placement configurations, and well–fault distances over 30 d. Coulomb failure function (CFF) threshold attainment with frictional weakening defined modeled onset; failure-area ratio and maximum shear plastic strain served as within-mesh comparative indicators of domain-scale localization. The simulations reveal a hierarchy of controls: injection rate primarily governs pressure buildup and onset timing; rate history reorganizes transient stress paths and localization; and well placement and distance redistribute pressure and yielding across the fault. Higher rates increased the within-mesh failure-area ratio, whereas variable histories produced distinct responses that cannot be attributed to cycling alone because peak rate and shut-in transitions were confounded. Local threshold indicators and domain-scale metrics were complementary rather than interchangeable: temporal onset, spatial extent and deformation intensity were distinct response dimensions. These findings motivate joint optimization of injection schedules and well layouts against both temporal onset and spatial localization, while providing model-scale guidance for early quasi-static risk screening rather than predictions of seismicity, dynamic rupture or long-term stability.

title: Polypyrrole as Dissociation Promoter and Interface Stabilizer of Solid Polymer Electrolytes for Solid‐State Li Metal Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Advanced solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) are indispensable for enabling durable, safe, and high‐energy‐density solid‐state lithium metal batteries (SSLMBs). However, the concurrent optimization of lithium‐salt dissociation, Li +
content: ABSTRACT Advanced solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) are indispensable for enabling durable, safe, and high‐energy‐density solid‐state lithium metal batteries (SSLMBs). However, the concurrent optimization of lithium‐salt dissociation, Li + transport, and lithium‐metal interfacial chemistry remains a challenge over decades. In this study, a PPy‐regulated solid polymer electrolyte (PPyPL) featuring chemically differentiated coordination sites is developed to reconstruct ion‐solvation chemistry through site‐selective Li + /anion coordination. The resulting coordination architecture affords differentiated molecular interactions in which pyrrolic nitrogen sites preferentially coordinate Li + , whereas hydrogen sites along the PPy backbone interact with bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (TFSI − ) anions, thereby simultaneously promoting lithium‐salt dissociation, accelerating Li + transport, and directing LiF/Li 3 N‐rich interphase formation. Benefiting from the synergistic regulation of ion‐solvation chemistry and interfacial evolution, PPyPL achieves an ionic conductivity of 0.76 mS cm −1 at room temperature (25°C), a Li + transference number of 0.65, and ultralong Li plating/stripping stability over 8000 h. It further enables outstanding rate capability and durable cycling in both Li||LiFePO 4 (LFP) and Li||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811) solid‐state full cells. This work provides a new strategy for regulating Li + /anion coordination in advanced SPEs toward durable SSLMBs.

title: The EU challenge to make its ports more sustainable and competitive: The case of the Green Ports Project for the Port of Naples
summary: Today European ports have moved beyond their traditional role as logistical gateways to become strategic infrastructure for energy, supply-chain resilience and urban development. In this context, port competitiveness can no longer be unders
content: Today European ports have moved beyond their traditional role as logistical gateways to become strategic infrastructure for energy, supply-chain resilience and urban development. In this context, port competitiveness can no longer be understood only in terms of logistical performance but must be assessed within a governance model capable of integrating environmental sustainability and territorial resilience. Against this background, this research reconstructs the European framework on port competitiveness and sustainability and analyses its effectiveness in shaping governance conditions and supporting sustainability-oriented projects. In particular, Regulation 2017/352 and Regulation 2024/1679 are examined as legislative acts that establish an institutional bridge between competitiveness and environmental objectives. This approach is further strengthened by the 2026 Communications on the EU Ports Strategy and the Industrial Maritime Strategy. The research adopts a qualitative methodology grounded in regulatory assessment, combining a multi-level legal analysis of the EU and Italian frameworks with an explanatory case study focusing on the Port of Naples and its involvement in the Green Ports Project under Italy’s Recovery and Resilience Plan. To better understand the case study, the article first examines the evolution of Italian legislation on port competitiveness and sustainability: from Law No. 84/1994, which promoted reforms to reshape the Italian port system, to Legislative Decree No. 169/2016, which created Port System Authorities and introduced the Energy and Environmental Planning Document. The research argues that, despite the impact of these reforms, pronounced governance fragmentation is still compromising the development of a sustainable strategy for the port and the surrounding city.

title: Alternative Energy and Socially Oriented Economy
summary: This chapter explores the “blue economy” as a sustainable development model, integrating rational ocean resource management with advanced engineering innovations. At its core is the global energy transformation and the growing role of offsh
content: This chapter explores the “blue economy” as a sustainable development model, integrating rational ocean resource management with advanced engineering innovations. At its core is the global energy transformation and the growing role of offshore renewables, such as wind, wave, and salinity gradient energy, as the foundation for next-generation technologies. Particular emphasis is placed on the synergy between marine energy and Advanced Plasma Engineering. The study justifies the implementation of plasma-based technologies for water desalination, purification, and green hydrogen production within marine environments. Integrating plasma physics with the World Ocean's potential is presented as a key driver for carbon neutrality, economic growth, and a socially oriented economy, aligning with the UN Sustainable Development Goals.

title: Plasma-Enhanced Multilayer Coatings on Metal Bipolar Plates for Corrosion Resistance and High Electrical Conductivity
summary: Abstract Metal bipolar plates are central to lowering the cost and weight of proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) stacks, yet their long-term use is limited by aggressive corrosion in the acidic, humid, low-pH cathode environment. Mul
content: Abstract Metal bipolar plates are central to lowering the cost and weight of proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) stacks, yet their long-term use is limited by aggressive corrosion in the acidic, humid, low-pH cathode environment. Multilayer protective coatings combining adhesion-promoting metal interlayers with chemically inert graphitic carbon are widely regarded as a promising solution, but they have historically been deposited slowly and from precursors such as titanium tetrachloride that are difficult to scale safely. Here, we report the design and operation of a showerhead plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) reactor that deposits Ti/TiCx/amorphous-carbon (a-C) multilayer coatings on 304 stainless steel using the comparatively safe titanium isopropoxide (TiPO) precursor in combination with a hydrogen plasma. Both continuous radio frequency (RF) and nanosecond-pulsed glow discharges were tested at 10 W and at substrate temperatures up to 300 °C. Cross-sectional scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and Raman scattering confirm uniform, pinhole-free multilayers in which Ti is reduced from TiPO by atomic hydrogen and the carbon top layer is sp2-rich and graphitic. Carbon deposition rates of 200–237 nm min–1 were obtained, matching or exceeding the best values reported in the literature. A coupled plasma kinetics and showerhead transport model rationalizes these rates, the distinct microstructures obtained under continuous and nanosecond-pulsed excitation, and the measured coating uniformity. The best carbon coatings reach interfacial contact resistance (ICR) values of 5.4–13.5 mΩ·cm2 at 1.10 MPa, with the lowest well below the 2025 U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) target of 10 mΩ·cm2. The coatings showed no detectable Raman or morphological degradation after accelerated thermal cycling between 30 and 100 °C in pH 3 H2SO4, demonstrating their potential as a fast, safe, and scalable coating route for next-generation PEMFC bipolar plates.

title: Synthesis, anti‐ Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae activity and antibacterial mechanism of indole‐3‐substituted‐1,3,4‐oxadiazole derivative
summary: BACKGROUND: Bacterial leaf blight (BLB) caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae (Xoo) seriously endangers global rice production. It is urgent to explore efficient and low-toxic antibacterial candidates for sustainable bacterial blight mana
content: BACKGROUND: Bacterial leaf blight (BLB) caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae (Xoo) seriously endangers global rice production. It is urgent to explore efficient and low-toxic antibacterial candidates for sustainable bacterial blight management. RESULTS: ], 19-32-fold more potent than thiodiazole copper, with (respectively) 72.35% and 75.68% therapeutic, and 72.64% and 72.33% protective efficacy on rice. Mechanistic studies demonstrated concurrent suppression of EPS/biofilm formation, induction of reactive oxygen species (ROS-mediated apoptosis in Xoo, and downregulation of virulence and accC-associated genes - validated by RNA-seq. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed stable polar anchoring of T8 to accC-Arg381 versus electrostatic repulsion experienced by T2 at accC-Lys250/Arg23. Biosafety tests on HEK293T cells and silkworms verified their low toxicity. CONCLUSION: T2 and T8 were identified as high-efficiency and biosafe anti-Xoo lead compounds. This study provides valuable candidate molecules and a theoretical basis for the development of novel green bactericides against rice bacterial blight. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: The EU Deforestation Regulation: Challenges, Opportunities and the Potential Impacts on the Producing Countries of Cocoa and Coffee
summary: ABSTRACT The European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) is a policy that prohibits access to the EU market for commodities that are linked to deforestation. We did a systematic review to understand perceived challenges, opportunities an
content: ABSTRACT The European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) is a policy that prohibits access to the EU market for commodities that are linked to deforestation. We did a systematic review to understand perceived challenges, opportunities and potential impacts of the EUDR on producing countries of cocoa and coffee. The challenges include national laws that are incompatible with the EUDR, a lack of awareness and technical capacity, map misclassifications, and the burden on smallholder farmers. The opportunities include setting standards for fairer prices, improving human rights, and strengthening local collaboration and capacity building. The potential impacts are linked to country‐level legal alignments with the regulation and required investments to comply with the EUDR. The EUDR could become an incentive for more similar policies and more environmental policies at different levels. The EUDR might initially bring a financial burden to invest in formalising environmental compliance, but long‐term financial, economic and social benefits are expected.

title: Interruptible AI training as virtual energy storage for renewable integration in computing centers
source: Energy Sustainable Development/Energy for sustainable development
summary: Intelligent computing centers are emerging as large electricity consumers whose demand can be temporally misaligned with variable renewable generation. This study proposes a low-carbon dispatch framework that represents checkpoint-enabled i
content: Intelligent computing centers are emerging as large electricity consumers whose demand can be temporally misaligned with variable renewable generation. This study proposes a low-carbon dispatch framework that represents checkpoint-enabled interruptible AI training workloads as a baseline-relative virtual energy storage resource. The model distinguishes non-movable, short-term shiftable, continuous, and interruptible computing loads and uses cumulative training progress as a virtual state of charge. In this representation, virtual discharging denotes demand reduction relative to a fixed baseline schedule, whereas virtual charging denotes demand recovery or advancement during periods of abundant renewable generation. The dispatch model jointly considers time-of-use electricity prices, ladder-type carbon trading, and green electricity certificates to align economic and emission incentives. Using workload profiles reconstructed from the Alibaba PAI GPU cluster trace, the framework is evaluated in a representative Northwest China computing-center microgrid case. Under the examined assumptions, the proposed strategy reduces renewable curtailment from 22.82% to 0.69%, lowers daily operating costs by 14.45%, and decreases physical carbon emissions by 30.46%. Benchmark and scenario analyses indicate that workload-side flexibility can complement behind-the-meter storage for renewable matching, although its value depends on workload composition, renewable timing, grid carbon intensity, tariff design, and market conditions. The findings suggest that checkpoint-enabled training can provide an asset-light demand-side flexibility option for renewable-rich computing centers, but its applicability requires careful consideration of service constraints, accounting rules, and regional power-system conditions.

title: Modeling electricity price formation during Poland’s energy transition using market data and sentiment analysis
summary: Electricity-price dynamics in energy-transitioning power systems reflect the interaction of fuel costs, carbon prices, financial conditions, regulatory information, and market expectations. This study examines whether text-derived news indi
content: Electricity-price dynamics in energy-transitioning power systems reflect the interaction of fuel costs, carbon prices, financial conditions, regulatory information, and market expectations. This study examines whether text-derived news indicators provide incremental predictive information for Polish electricity prices. A curated English-language European policy-news corpus identified through a GDELT-assisted collection procedure is processed using two separate natural-language-processing branches. TF–IDF is used to characterize the thematic prominence of selected energy and climate-policy terms, while VADER is applied directly to article text to derive an interpretable news-tone indicator, referred to as the Climate Change News Index. These indicators are aligned with electricity, natural-gas, coal, oil, carbon-allowance, and equity-market variables. Ordinary Least Squares and Elastic Net models are evaluated using chronological out-of-sample forecasts. Market fundamentals remain the main predictive inputs, while the contribution of text-derived variables is small and specification-dependent. The results therefore indicate limited incremental predictive information rather than systematic forecasting superiority. The study is observational, and the reported relationships are interpreted as associative and predictive rather than causal. The proposed workflow provides a transparent way to incorporate policy-news information into electricity-price analysis. However, it does not replace physical power-system variables but it provides additional predictive power for better forecasting which can be useful for the market players.

title: Same intervention, different outcomes: The politics of energy transition planning in Ghana and Kenya
summary: Under what conditions does externally supported energy transition planning produce locally owned and sustainable policy outcomes rather than short-lived plans, and what role do institutional gatekeeping, bureaucratic authority, and the sequ
content: Under what conditions does externally supported energy transition planning produce locally owned and sustainable policy outcomes rather than short-lived plans, and what role do institutional gatekeeping, bureaucratic authority, and the sequencing of technical and political processes play in shaping those conditions? To unpack these questions, this paper comparatively analyses SEforALL's Energy Transition Investment Plan development in Ghana and Kenya, revealing striking divergences in processes and outcomes. Drawing on 22 semi-structured interviews and the theories of policy translation and political settlements, the analysis demonstrates that Ghana's experience was characterised by institutional bypass, limited domestic agency, and a significant reduction in the plan's operational priority following electoral change. Kenya's trajectory, conversely, featured institutional resistance that compelled collaborative engagement, resulting in sustainable policy embedding. The findings reveal that successful policy translation depends not merely on technical capacity but on power configuration, bureaucratic authority, and political settlements. This research advances understanding of energy transition politics whilst offering practical insights for international organisations and governments navigating the complex politics of translating global climate imperatives into national policies in developing countries.

title: Photovoltaic Land Area Converted into Aviation Fuel and Passenger Flight Performance
summary: Purpose – Show with three simple example calculations the effect that photovoltaic (PV) energy production can have on commercial flight operations. Considered is rooftop PV, normal ground-mounted PV, and ground-mounted PV at airports. --- M
content: Purpose – Show with three simple example calculations the effect that photovoltaic (PV) energy production can have on commercial flight operations. Considered is rooftop PV, normal ground-mounted PV, and ground-mounted PV at airports. --- Methodology – Calculations are based on first principles, common parameters, and statistics. --- Findings – The result highlights the extremely high energy needs of commercial aviation relative to the renewable-energy yield of land by means of PV. The conclusion is not that airport-associated PV is unimportant. On the contrary, PV can contribute meaningfully to airport energy supply and synthetic-fuel production for aircraft operation. However: The calculation shows that even comparatively large PV areas that airports could offer correspond to only a small fraction (e.g. 1%) of the fuel demand created by commercial flight operations at the airport.

title: Hydrogen’s future in Türkiye: Storage, natural gas integration, and energy transition
source: Pamukkale University Journal of Engineering Sciences
summary: Hydrogen stands out as a clean energy carrier that plays a critical role in the global energy transformation. Türkiye's increasing energy demand, dependence on fossil fuels, and carbon emission reduction targets place hydrogen technologies
content: Hydrogen stands out as a clean energy carrier that plays a critical role in the global energy transformation. Türkiye's increasing energy demand, dependence on fossil fuels, and carbon emission reduction targets place hydrogen technologies at the center of national energy policies. According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), the integration of hydrogen into energy systems could contribute to reducing global carbon emissions by up to 20%. This study comprehensively examines Türkiye's hydrogen potential, its integration with existing energy infrastructure, and hydrogen storage solutions. The study provides a detailed analysis of compressed gas, liquid hydrogen, solid-state storage, and underground storage technologies. Türkiye's existing geological structure was determined to be suitable for underground hydrogen storage, but infrastructure deficiencies were highlighted as a significant obstacle. Furthermore, factors such as technical challenges encountered in integrating hydrogen into natural gas networks, pipeline material compatibility, and the risk of hydrogen embrittlement were discussed. In addition, the potential for hydrogen's use in various sectors, such as industry, transportation, and energy production, has been explored. For example, the use of hydrogen in iron and steel production can reduce carbon emissions by up to 90% compared to traditional methods. It has been demonstrated that hydrogen fuel cell vehicles can provide an alternative to fossil fuel vehicles in the transportation sector and can be economically advantageous in the long term. Finally, Türkiye's hydrogen roadmap proposes infrastructure investments, international collaborations, and technological innovations, identifying the necessary steps for the long-term integration of hydrogen into a sustainable energy system. This study demonstrates the role of hydrogen in achieving Türkiye's net-zero emissions targets and provides a comprehensive framework for future research.

title: Beyond Market Failure: A Critique of the ‘New Economics of Industrial Policy’
summary: ABSTRACT In recent years, there has been an apparent tidal shift in neoclassical industrial policy scholarship as a ‘new economics of industrial policy’ has emerged. These scholars claim to have fundamentally repositioned the debate on indu
content: ABSTRACT In recent years, there has been an apparent tidal shift in neoclassical industrial policy scholarship as a ‘new economics of industrial policy’ has emerged. These scholars claim to have fundamentally repositioned the debate on industrial policy, supposedly offering a novel account of how, and why, states turn to industrial policy (the ‘new economics’), as well as a precise measurement of its causal effects (‘the new empirics’). In particular, the ‘new economists’ claim to show that the South Korean state, undistracted by politics, could follow a strictly economic rationale and could correct the significant market failures that occur in the development process. Following Marxist scholarship on the state, this article suggests that this is fundamentally misleading. The author argues that, rather than correcting market failures, the South Korean state intervened to support capital accumulation through markets. While the new economists are right to suggest that the South Korean state seemingly acted in a rational manner, this was a peculiarly capitalist rationality, and one that rested upon the violent subordination of labour and containment of democratic pressures. The apparent depoliticization, or bureaucratic autonomy, achieved by the South Korean state was key to this effort.

title: Reusing obsolete windows 10 PCs for on-premises large language model inference
summary: The Windows 10 end-of-life provides a material incentive to repurpose legacy PCs as on-premises large language model (LLM) inference servers. This study assesses the technical feasibility, economic viability and the environmental and social
content: The Windows 10 end-of-life provides a material incentive to repurpose legacy PCs as on-premises large language model (LLM) inference servers. This study assesses the technical feasibility, economic viability and the environmental and social issues of converting an enterprise workstation with an NVIDIA Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) into a dedicated AI node. Using Proxmox virtualisation, Ollama, and Open WebUI to benchmark several open-source LLMs, this study shows that a repurposed workstation, fitted with a single consumer-grade NVIDIA GPU, can deliver stable inference throughput of 29–65 tokens/s for bounded, conversational coding and document-assistant workflows, while preserving full data sovereignty and eliminating recurring subscription fees. Performance analysis reveals that resource contention and GPU memory allocation are the primary determinants of throughput. Correctness, assessed against three established public benchmarks with gold answers, does not track the same ranking as throughput; combining both axes identifies gemma4:e4b as the strongest model evaluated on this hardware for both speed and correctness, while the slowest model tested was among the most accurate. A cost-benefit model shows local operation is substantially cheaper than mid-range and premium cloud alternatives, and only modestly costlier than the cheapest cloud tier on a per-prompt basis—a gap this study argues is outweighed by the digital-sovereignty benefits of local control, particularly where compliance-driven data-handling constraints apply. The study summarizes key background motivations for on-premises AI—privacy, security, regulatory risk—and estimates that this repurposed workstation's usage-phase CO 2 e footprint is lower than each of the cloud alternatives compared, in addition to avoiding the embodied manufacturing emissions of new hardware. Repurposing legacy workstations with readily available open source tools offers a sustainable, cost-effective pathway for organizations to deploy practical LLM inference capabilities locally, providing a strategic alternative to cloud services for entities that prioritize privacy, regulatory compliance or long-term cost containment.

title: Gated Residual Fusion Framework for Mitigating Error Accumulation in Multistep NOx Prediction for Utility CFB Boilers
summary: Abstract Accurate multistep prediction of nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions is essential for combustion perception and optimization in utility boilers. Under deep peak-shaving conditions, frequent operating condition transitions induce mixed o
content: Abstract Accurate multistep prediction of nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions is essential for combustion perception and optimization in utility boilers. Under deep peak-shaving conditions, frequent operating condition transitions induce mixed operating data, strong variable coupling, and progressive error accumulation, restricting the long-horizon stability of conventional models. To address these issues, a gated residual fusion framework was constructed by using data from a 300 MW circulating fluidized bed (CFB) boiler. A preprocessing strategy integrating rolling signal denoising, correlation analysis, and Random Forest ranking selected 30 variables from 162 candidates. iTransformer and TimesNet were coupled to extract complementary dynamic representations, and sequence decomposition fusion, parallel fusion, and gated residual fusion were compared. In the proposed architecture, the dominant NOx evolution is captured by the iTransformer backbone, while the TimeNet residual branch provides correction for local deviations that are insufficiently represented by the backbone. Compared with standalone VMD-iTransformer and VMD-TimesNet, RMSE was reduced by 73.99% and 78.37% at step 1 and by 39.86% and 49.51% at step 6, respectively. Compared with eight baseline models, the proposed model achieved the best average performance, with RMSE, MAE, MAPE, and R2 values of 3.2228 mg/m3, 1.8930 mg/m3, 5.2338%, and 0.9185. Results demonstrate peak recovery, abrupt change tracking, and long-horizon stability.

title: Integrative Review of Biochar in Semi-Arid Agroecosystems: Global Trends, Potential Feedstocks, Crop-Soil Interactions, and Carbon Lability
source: Journal of soil science and plant nutrition
summary: This integrative review evaluates the current state and evolution of biochar research in arid and semi-arid agroecosystems by integrating scientometric analysis with a critical narrative synthesis. Specifically, it examines publication tren
content: This integrative review evaluates the current state and evolution of biochar research in arid and semi-arid agroecosystems by integrating scientometric analysis with a critical narrative synthesis. Specifically, it examines publication trends, collaboration networks, and thematic evolution while assessing the relationships among feedstock types, pyrolysis conditions, biochar properties, soil-crop interactions, labile carbon fractions, microbial processes, and practical applicability under water-limited conditions. The scientometric component uses the Web of Science Core Collection for the 2010–2025 period and applies co-occurrence, co-authorship, co-citation, bibliographic coupling, and thematic mapping to characterize the intellectual structure of the field. The narrative synthesis incorporates additional classical and recent studies to interpret mechanisms and context-dependent responses. Scientific production increased markedly over the study period, accompanied by an increasingly interconnected and multipolar research network. Research trends shifted from descriptive studies focused on feedstock characterization toward applied approaches involving soil fertility, carbon sequestration, nutrient cycling, and crop performance. Evidence indicates that biochar can improve soil functionality in semi-arid agroecosystems, particularly where low organic matter, coarse texture, acidity, or water limitation constrain plant growth; however, the magnitude and persistence of these effects depend on feedstock, pyrolysis temperature, soil properties, application rate, climate, and duration. Biochar represents a promising but context-dependent strategy for improving water retention, nutrient availability, soil structure, carbon stabilization, and biological functioning in dryland agriculture. Remaining gaps include long-term field performance, methodological standardization, carbon-balance assessment during pyrolysis, and biochar-soil-microbiome interactions under realistic semi-arid conditions. title: Blockchain for Environmental Accountability: An Experimental Approach to Sustainable Tourism Reporting
source: Ilomata International Journal of Tax and Accounting
summary: This study evaluates the application of blockchain technology to enhance environmental accountability in sustainable tourism reporting in Bali, as a response to the risk of greenwashing practices. Given that traditional reporting systems of
content: This study evaluates the application of blockchain technology to enhance environmental accountability in sustainable tourism reporting in Bali, as a response to the risk of greenwashing practices. Given that traditional reporting systems often lack standardization and are vulnerable to manipulation, this study aims to empirically test the impact of blockchain integration on accuracy, efficiency, and stakeholder trust. Using a quasi-experimental method with a sample of 60 tourism businesses divided into treatment and control groups, data was analyzed through system metrics, surveys, and interviews. The results showed that blockchain significantly improved reporting accuracy by 18.6% and accelerated verification time by 67% (9.4 days faster). Furthermore, the use of smart contracts was shown to increase stakeholder trust and reduce audit costs with a return on investment ratio of 2.8:1. Theoretically, this study validates how automation and data immutability strengthen environmental accountability structures in complex tourism governance. In conclusion, blockchain technology is effective in increasing transparency and reporting efficiency, although its adoption by SMEs remains hampered by cost and technical barriers. The practical implications of this research emphasize the importance of developing user-friendly interfaces as well as financial support to ensure inclusive digital transformation for the sustainability of the tourism industry.

title: Total State, Total Constitution
summary: The ‘total state’ is a polemical concept used by constitutional theorists in the 1930s to characterise a decline of state authority: a state made to intervene into all areas of social life becomes, in their view, weak. This concept can be t
content: The ‘total state’ is a polemical concept used by constitutional theorists in the 1930s to characterise a decline of state authority: a state made to intervene into all areas of social life becomes, in their view, weak. This concept can be transferred, for heuristic purposes, to the authority of constitutional law. A total constitution is omnirelevant – no longer meant only to curb state action, but also to guide policymaking. Like the total state, the law of the total constitution risks becoming prey to the forces ruling the day. This weakness is exacerbated when adjudicating bodies embrace symbolic politics. The KlimaSeniorinnen decision of the European Court of Human Rights serves to elucidate this issue.

title: Ground-based spectral irradiance for intra-hour photovoltaic power forecasting
summary: Electricity markets worldwide are shortening their settlement intervals, with Australia adopting 5-minute settlement in 2021 and the European Union now mandating a 15-minute imbalance settlement period across Member States. Shorter interval
content: Electricity markets worldwide are shortening their settlement intervals, with Australia adopting 5-minute settlement in 2021 and the European Union now mandating a 15-minute imbalance settlement period across Member States. Shorter intervals sharpen the value of accurate intra-hour photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting at the timescale of cloud-induced ramp events, which broadband irradiance cannot fully resolve. In this study, ground-based high-resolution spectroradiometer measurements (213 channels, 350–1052 nm) are exploited as an input to short-horizon PV forecasting for the first time, and the gain is quantified across two climates and multiple years using data from the Solar Energy Research Institute of Singapore (SERIS). A SpectralEncoder is introduced, a lightweight 1-D convolutional network applied along the wavelength axis, combined with a physically motivated spectral-ratio representation that decouples spectral shape from broadband magnitude. Performance is evaluated under a dual-dimension framework crossing ramp/non-ramp conditions with clear/intermediate/overcast regimes defined by the clear-sky index. At the primary German site (temperate oceanic; trained 2018–2021, tested 2023), overall RMSE is reduced by 4.4% with spectral inputs, with the largest gain (+9.4%) under overcast ramp conditions, the regime most damaging to grid balancing. At the Australian site (hot desert; trained 2018–2020, tested 2022) the gain is 2.7%, of the same sign as at the German site. A noise-replacement control confirms the gain is driven by genuine spectral structure rather than dimensionality. The contribution is positively signed across forecast horizons from 15 to 90 min, holds across three model families (TCN, LSTM, LightGBM), and is statistically significant under day-block bootstrap ( p < 0.001 ). Post-hoc wavelength-importance analysis localises the signal to visible and near-infrared channels coinciding with known atmospheric absorption features, with cross-site Pearson correlation r = 0.69 . As market clearing intervals shrink and PV penetration rises, ground-based spectral irradiance, already collected at BSRN and collaborative PV testing networks worldwide, is a low-cost, deployable input feature for intra-hour forecasts.

title: Porous Ag-Cu-CeO2 nanoparticles: Biosynthesis, cephalexin photodegradation, antifungal activity and primary evaluation of in vitro cancer treatment on MDA-MB-231 cells
summary: In the study, silver- and copper-co doped cerium oxide nanoparticles (Ag-Cu-CeO 2 NP) were prepared using Ferula assa-foetida L. extract as a biological reducing factor. Field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) demonstrated a por
content: In the study, silver- and copper-co doped cerium oxide nanoparticles (Ag-Cu-CeO 2 NP) were prepared using Ferula assa-foetida L. extract as a biological reducing factor. Field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) demonstrated a porous surface texture, while powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) introduced crystalline dimensions of 21.89 nm. Supplementary techniques, including energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) analysis, Raman, Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectrometry, and ultraviolet-visible (UV-vis) spectroscopy validated the successful synthesis of the mentioned nanoparticles. The Ag-Cu-CeO 2 NP gained a magnificent degradation rate of 84.92% for cephalexin (CPX) under visible light exposure, following pseudo-first-order kinetics (k = 0.0086 min −1 ). The synthesized NP exhibited moderate antifungal performance against Aspergillus flavus (MIC: 36.25 mg mL −1 ) and against Neurospora intermedia (MIC: 72.5 mg mL −1 ). Moreover, cytotoxicity assessment via MTT assay exhibited dose dependent inhibition of MDA MB 231 breast cancer cells (IC 50 = 475.1 μg mL −1 ), and also significantly lower toxicity on normal MCF 10 A cells. These findings propose that the nanoparticles demonstrate greater cytotoxic effects on cancerous MDA-MB-231 cells compared to normal MCF-10 A cells. However, these results are preliminary and entirely in vitro ; further in vivo validation, comprehensive toxicity evaluation, and mechanistic studies are needed before considering therapeutic applications. Overall, the outcomes indicate that green-synthesized Ag-Cu-CeO 2 NP describe an effective and promising nanomaterial warranting further study for potential biomedical and environmental applications.

title: Law, markets and the valuation of nature: legal infrastructures, financial instruments, and the contest over ecological value
summary: This article critically examines the legal frameworks underpinning the financialisation of nature, interrogating how legal instruments codify ecological entities as assets, risks, and services. It demonstrates that valuation regimes, exempl
content: This article critically examines the legal frameworks underpinning the financialisation of nature, interrogating how legal instruments codify ecological entities as assets, risks, and services. It demonstrates that valuation regimes, exemplified by Natural Asset Companies (NACs), biodiversity credits, green bonds, and disclosure frameworks like the Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD), do not neutrally protect ecosystems but actively reshape them into investable, commodified units. Such frameworks marginalise alternative Indigenous and relational ontologies, which organise ecological relationships through reciprocity, responsibility, and obligation rather than commodification. Drawing on examples from Indigenous legal orders, the article argues that procedural reforms and superficial inclusivity are insufficient to address fundamental epistemic conflicts. Instead, it calls for a radical reimagining of environmental law towards plural legal ontologies and relational forms of governance, concluding that truly sustainable futures depend upon contesting the ontological assumptions that define whose values count, whose nature is protected, and whose laws prevail.

title: Governing the environmental externalities of digital infrastructure: A multi‐regime legal assessment of data centres
source: Review of European Comparative & International Environmental Law
summary: Abstract The rapid expansion of data centres and their environmental impacts, including high energy and water consumption and land‐use changes, pose urgent challenges to existing regulatory systems. These impacts exhibit a distinctive ‘hybr
content: Abstract The rapid expansion of data centres and their environmental impacts, including high energy and water consumption and land‐use changes, pose urgent challenges to existing regulatory systems. These impacts exhibit a distinctive ‘hybrid‐point source pollution’ character, originating from a physically discrete facility yet producing dispersed, cumulative and cross‐sectoral environmental consequences that evade existing regulatory classifications. A comparative study of the EU, the US and China shows that, despite their governance models being characterised, respectively, as norm‐anchored, market‐oriented and policy‐directed, all suffer from fragmented regulation and insufficient integration of environmental issues. At the international level, existing environmental treaties provide only partial and largely non‐binding coverage, leaving major legal gaps. Dealing with these deficiencies requires a comprehensive governance framework that strengthens environmental assessment, includes spatial planning, optimises regulatory tools and establishes unified standards and disclosure mechanisms, thereby advancing a cross‐border model that connects environmental, international and digital law.

title: Evaluation and strategic optimization of public institution energy efficiency: a hybrid framework combining CRITIC weighting and tripartite evolutionary game
summary: Public institutions, as key entities fulfilling public service functions, are characterized by their substantial scale, high energy intensity, and significant demonstration role in society. Improving their energy efficiency is therefore piv
content: Public institutions, as key entities fulfilling public service functions, are characterized by their substantial scale, high energy intensity, and significant demonstration role in society. Improving their energy efficiency is therefore pivotal for achieving national decarbonization targets. This study addresses the gaps in current energy efficiency evaluation systems and the lack of coordination among stakeholders by proposing a novel framework combining CRITIC-based weighting with a tripartite evolutionary game model. The evaluation system encompasses four dimensions: energy consumption, technological innovation, operational management, and contextual factors. The CRITIC method is applied to determine indicator weights, and a tripartite evolutionary game model involving the government, integrated energy service providers (IESPs), and public institutions is constructed to explore strategy evolution and equilibrium under a Carbon Inclusion mechanism. A case study of a university in Fujian Province is used to assess seven retrofit options. Results show that technological innovation indicators hold the highest weight (0.258), highlighting the importance of low-carbon technologies. The comprehensive retrofit plan yields the best results, reducing net present cost by 18.4%, annual carbon emissions by 25.2%, and electricity consumption by 34.4%. The game analysis reveals that government subsidies accelerate strategy evolution in the early stages but can be phased out over time. IESPs should implement dynamic carbon pricing and adaptive incentives. Overall, this study provides a systematic theoretical framework and practical path for improving energy efficiency in public institutions.

title: Bioinspired Heme and NonHeme Metal Complexes as Electrocatalysts for Nitrate and Nitrite Reduction
summary: Excess nitrate (NO 3 − ) and nitrite (NO 2 − ) from agricultural and industrial sources are major water pollutants and precursors of greenhouse gases. The electrocatalytic reduction of NO 3 − /NO 2 − is regarded as a sustainable solution fo
content: Excess nitrate (NO 3 − ) and nitrite (NO 2 − ) from agricultural and industrial sources are major water pollutants and precursors of greenhouse gases. The electrocatalytic reduction of NO 3 − /NO 2 − is regarded as a sustainable solution for the remediation of contaminated water and a method for producing ammonia (NH 3 ) under ambient conditions. In this review, molecular electrocatalyst macrocycles derived from heme, such as porphyrins and phthalocyanines, and nonheme complexes for NO 3 − /NO 2 − reduction are presented. Based on enzymes such as molybdenum‐dependent nitrate reductases and copper‐ or heme‐containing nitrite reductases, representative synthetic enzymes are discussed in terms of their mechanisms, catalytic parameters, ligand effects, product selectivity, and stability. The conversion of NO 2 − to NH 3 is the most prominent application of heme‐type Fe and Co macrocycles Nonheme systems, such as Cu polypyridines, Ni diamine, or Fe/Co N‐donor complexes, can also produce NO, N 2 O, or NH 3 by varying the ligand environment or pH. We identified some advances, such as high turnover frequencies, elucidation of the competitive proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET) and atom transfer pathways, and new strategies for increased durability. Finally, the principles of second‐sphere proton relay and electronic tuning are discussed, and the opportunities for embedding macrocycles within conductive frameworks and emulating multisite enzymatic architectures to create efficient and robust electrocatalysts for nitrogen oxide (NO x ) remediation and green NH 3 production are outlined.

title: Demystifying Role of Energy Transition and Entrepreneurship in Achieving Carbon Neutrality
summary: ABSTRACT Millions of entrepreneurs face silent failure—not from lack of will, but due to entrenched systemic barriers. Without institutional reform, carbon neutrality remains a distant ideal, and critical human potential risks irreversible
content: ABSTRACT Millions of entrepreneurs face silent failure—not from lack of will, but due to entrenched systemic barriers. Without institutional reform, carbon neutrality remains a distant ideal, and critical human potential risks irreversible loss. This paper examines the dynamic relationship between energy transition, entrepreneurship, and carbon neutrality in Nigeria from 1985 to 2024. Employing a rigorous time series econometric framework—including Bayer and Hanck cointegration, Fully Modified Ordinary Least Squares (FMOLS), Dynamic Ordinary Least Squares (DOLS), Canonical Cointegration Regression (CCR), and Robust Least Squares (RLS)—the study identifies statistically robust long‐run equilibrium relationships among key variables. Findings reveal a duality: while energy transition, entrepreneurship, and human development contribute to reducing carbon intensity, economic growth and foreign direct investment increase emissions, exposing a systemic paradox at the heart of contemporary development discourse. Growth and innovation, while indispensable, may erode environmental objectives without deliberate institutional design. This paper recommends establishing a centralised, well‐funded energy transition authority in Nigeria, embedding green entrepreneurship through targeted fiscal incentives and capacity building, and legislating enforceable carbon neutrality milestones. These policy measures provide a replicable framework for African economies, underscoring structural reform as essential for equitable, sustainable development under the SDG agenda.

title: Selective CO 2 -to-CH 4 Photoconversion Enabled by High-Valent Pd 4+ Species on PdO-Anchored Co 3 O 4 Nanosheets
summary: Abstract Photocatalytic CO2 methanation offers a direct route to renewable energy storage, yet its efficiency is hampered by rapid charge recombination and inert CO2 activation. Herein, we report the rational design of PdO-anchored Co3O4 na
content: Abstract Photocatalytic CO2 methanation offers a direct route to renewable energy storage, yet its efficiency is hampered by rapid charge recombination and inert CO2 activation. Herein, we report the rational design of PdO-anchored Co3O4 nanosheets featuring high-valent Pd4+ species. Synchrotron-radiation X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and Bader charge calculations confirm the formation of the high-valent Pd4+ species. In situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy unveils that the CO2 reduction sites are switched from Co species to highly oxidized Pd species over the PdO/Co3O4 nanosheets. In situ Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy and electron paramagnetic resonance spectra further elucidate that Pd4+ accelerates the critical *COOH-to-*OCH3 hydrogenation step. Density functional theory calculations indicate that the introduction of Pd4+ lowers the excitation energy (from 1.62 to 1.03 eV) and reduces the *CO2-to-*COOH energy barrier by nearly half (from 1.27 to 0.70 eV). Consequently, the best-performing catalyst achieves a CH4 evolution rate of 136.6 μmol g–1 h–1 with 93.8% selectivity. This study offers deep insights into the mechanism of high-valent species in steering CO2 hydrogenation pathways.

title: Climate Change Disinformation| Climate Denialism as a Discursive Dynamic: Truth (and Politics) Beyond Facts
summary: Applying Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) methods to the online output of climate change contesters, this article examines how their discursive strategies are accommodated within counter-disinformation frameworks. Critiquing the reductive
content: Applying Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) methods to the online output of climate change contesters, this article examines how their discursive strategies are accommodated within counter-disinformation frameworks.
