Critiquing the reductive epistemology shaping such frameworks, it challenges the notion that, by endorsing “depoliticized understandings” based on unassailable scientific authority, they build democratic consensus from a factually validated decarbonization imperative. It argues that unless facts generated within the scientific paradigm are incorporated into an agonistic process within which their articulation with truth remains contingent, they cannot effectively combat climate contestation.

title: Sludge incineration ash-incorporated concrete: Performance and heavy metal release risk
summary: Abstract The utilization of sludge incineration ash (SIA) in concrete is often limited by mechanical deterioration and uncertain environmental stability. This study investigated SIA as a fine aggregate replacement, optimizing its use throug
content: Abstract The utilization of sludge incineration ash (SIA) in concrete is often limited by mechanical deterioration and uncertain environmental stability. This study investigated SIA as a fine aggregate replacement, optimizing its use through systematic mixture design. Results showed that an optimal mix (w/c ratio 0.4, 8.8% initial moisture, 5% SIA replacement) achieved a 28-day compressive strength of 41.8 MPa, 7.2% higher than the control and meeting C40 standards. This enhancement stems from the micro-filling effect that densifies the cement matrix, though excessive SIA impairs workability. Long-term environmental assessment via acid rain leaching, chloride immersion, and freeze–thaw cycling confirmed excellent heavy metal immobilization. Cu, Ni, and Cd remained undetectable, while Zn and Cr showed negligible release. This study confirms that 5% SIA replacement serves as a promising, safe strategy for sustainable concrete production, offering a scientific basis for the high-value utilization of incineration ash.

title: Research on the Safeguard Mechanisms for Urban Low-Carbon Planning in China under the Dual-Carbon Era
summary: In the context of China’s dual-carbon goals of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, urban low-carbon planning has become central to achieving sustainable urban transformation. However, its implementation remains hindered by fragmented lega
content: In the context of China’s dual-carbon goals of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, urban low-carbon planning has become central to achieving sustainable urban transformation. However, its implementation remains hindered by fragmented legal frameworks, weak regulatory coordination, limited incentive mechanisms, and insufficient public participation. This study examines how institutional safeguard mechanisms can enhance the effectiveness and enforceability of urban low-carbon planning. Using a comparative case analysis of representative Chinese cities, it investigates the current institutional arrangements, identifies key governance deficiencies, and explores feasible pathways for systemic improvement. The findings reveal that legal institutionalization, integrated regulatory frameworks, diversified incentive policies, and participatory co-governance are critical to advancing low-carbon planning and ensuring policy coherence. These insights can improve administrative efficiency, enhance stakeholder engagement, and create a resilient governance structure that supports long-term carbon reduction. The study contributes to the theoretical understanding of urban low-carbon governance and provides actionable policy guidance for cities in developing countries pursuing sustainable and inclusive low-carbon transitions under the global climate governance framework.

title: Repositioning Citizen Journalism: A Case Study in the Special Region of Yogyakarta
source: RSF Conference Series Business Management and Social Sciences
summary: Information disruption in the Society 5.0 era has fundamentally transformed how people access, produce, and distribute information. Mainstream media no longer exclusively control the flow of information, as social media enables citizens to
content: Information disruption in the Society 5.0 era has fundamentally transformed how people access, produce, and distribute information. Mainstream media no longer exclusively control the flow of information, as social media enables citizens to produce and disseminate news directly. This study examines the development of citizen journalism, particularly independent social media-based accounts in the Special Region of Yogyakarta. It explores how journalists and editorial leaders perceive their role within the contemporary media ecosystem. The study’s novelty lies in distinguishing independent citizen journalism from mainstream media and proposing a collaborative model based on the perspectives of information users, journalists, and editorial leaders. The study used a qualitative descriptive approach through open-ended questionnaires for members of the public and Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) with senior journalists and editorial leaders representing mainstream media in Yogyakarta. The findings indicate that citizen journalism has developed into an increasingly influential source of public information and has gained recognition from formal institutions. Its strengths include speed, proximity to communities, flexibility, and public engagement, whereas mainstream media retain advantages in professional standards, verification, and credibility. The study therefore proposes a complementary collaboration model involving information and reporting cooperation, journalistic capacity building, structured content distribution through attributed reposting, and commercial content production. This model repositions independent citizen journalism from merely a source of user-generated content to a strategic partner in the public information ecosystem while preserving the verification standards and professional values of mainstream journalism.

title: Chemical Pretreatment of Spent Coffee Grounds for Biomethane Production: A Review of Biochemical Methane Potential Assays
source: RSF Conference Series Engineering and Technology
summary: Spent coffee grounds (SCG) constitute a rapidly growing organic waste stream with a complex lignocellulosic matrix that restricts microbial degradation during anaerobic digestion (AD). This review evaluates the effects of oxidative, alkalin
content: Spent coffee grounds (SCG) constitute a rapidly growing organic waste stream with a complex lignocellulosic matrix that restricts microbial degradation during anaerobic digestion (AD). This review evaluates the effects of oxidative, alkaline, and acidic pretreatments on SCG solubilization and biomethanation performance. The methodology involved a comparative synthesis of reported batch mesophilic biochemical methane potential (BMP) assays employing distinct substrate-conditioning strategies. Particular attention was given to operational conditions, soluble chemical oxygen demand (SCOD), biogas yield, and methane yield. The synthesized evidence indicates that ambient alkaline treatment using 8% w/w NaOH produced a robust methane yield of 392 mL CH₄/g VS. In comparison, severe thermo-acidic treatment with 1.5% w/w H₂SO₄ at 121°C generated 381.12 mL CH₄/g VS. Treating SCG with 4% w/w H₂O₂ for 24 hours at room temperature increased SCOD by 713.02% relative to untreated SCG, indicating substantial solubilization of previously inaccessible organic matter. This condition produced 642.69 mL biogas/g VS and 345.53 mL CH₄/g VS without elevated temperature or pressure. Overall, pretreatment effectiveness cannot be assessed solely from solubilization rates; chemical dosage, energy use, and inhibitor formation must also be evaluated. Standardized comparative BMP testing and routine toxicity assessments are essential to forecast digester performance and improve sustainable waste valorization accurately.

title: Future in- and out-of-state air pollutant emissions under decarbonization pathways for Massachusetts
summary: Many U.S. states have adopted the goal of achieving carbon neutrality in the coming decades. Pathways for achieving these targets would likely yield a reduction of air pollutant emissions as well. We assess several state-level decarbonizati
content: Many U.S. states have adopted the goal of achieving carbon neutrality in the coming decades. Pathways for achieving these targets would likely yield a reduction of air pollutant emissions as well. We assess several state-level decarbonization pathways for Massachusetts, including electrification of buildings and transportation and decarbonization of the electric grid, estimating their impacts on in- and out-of-state emissions of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and several air pollutants. The analysis applies the GCAM-USA integrated assessment model with state-level resolution. We consider interactions between existing and proposed state and regional policies. The most aggressive state decarbonization pathway that was examined would achieve only a 65% reduction in CO 2 emissions by 2050 relative to 2015, indicating the need for further decarbonization options within the industry and non-road transportation sectors to achieve net-zero emission goal stated by the current administration. The air pollution co-benefits under these decarbonization pathways are substantial, especially for primary fine particulate matter. While policies focusing only on Massachusetts are shown to deliver in-state reductions of CO 2 and air pollutant emissions, these reductions were partially countered by emissions increases in other states, indicating the need for coordinated regional planning to prevent emissions leakage.

title: Socio-economic contributions of the Ethiopian Green Legacy Initiative as a pathway to sustainable development: Systematic Review
summary: Ethiopia faces interconnected challenges of land degradation, climate change, and rural poverty. In response, the government launched the Green Legacy Initiative (GLI) in 2019, a nationwide afforestation and reforestation program aimed at p
content: Ethiopia faces interconnected challenges of land degradation, climate change, and rural poverty. In response, the government launched the Green Legacy Initiative (GLI) in 2019, a nationwide afforestation and reforestation program aimed at planting billions of seedlings annually. Despite its ecological benefits, the initiative has generated substantial, yet often overlooked, socio-economic benefits that are critical to its long-term sustainability and contribution to the UN Sustainable Development Goals. This systematic review, therefore, aimed to identify the socio-economic benefits of the GLI and its role as a pathway to the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Relevant literature was sourced from Scopus, Web of Science, and Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ), using the keywords “Green Legacy, Initiative, benefits, and Sustainable Development (SD).” The review included studies published between 2019 and 2025 that reported on the socio-economic outcomes of the GLI. The results indicated that livelihood diversification, community empowerment, and improved food security and human well-being were the major socio-economic associations reported. The initiative is associated with significant potential to advance sustainable development in Ethiopia by linking ecological restoration with socio-economic improvement. However, significant challenges remain: seedling survival (averaging 76.50% across districts), 65% of GLI employment being temporary, and socioeconomic data missing for 70% of Woredas. Realizing the full potential of this initiative requires integrated policies that strengthen rural markets, ensure inclusive participation, and establish long-term monitoring of both benefits and limitations.

title: Thirsty clean energy: localized water stress and hydro-ecological tradeoffs in green hydrogen expansion
source: Critical Insights in Environmental Science and Technology
summary: Green hydrogen is central to global decarbonization, yet its rapid expansion exposes a severe spatial contradiction: the regions possessing optimal renewable energy potential are overwhelmingly the planet’s most water-stressed and ecologica
content: Green hydrogen is central to global decarbonization, yet its rapid expansion exposes a severe spatial contradiction: the regions possessing optimal renewable energy potential are overwhelmingly the planet’s most water-stressed and ecologically fragile landscapes. This review critically examines the localized hydro-ecological tradeoffs of mega-scale electrolysis across arid export corridors in Australia, Chile, and North Africa. Moving beyond theoretical stoichiometry, the analysis deconstructs the true operational water footprint of commercial electrolysis and evaluates cascading secondary risks, including marine ecotoxicity from desalination brine, fossil aquifer depletion, and spatial ecosystem fragmentation. Prevailing sustainability frameworks are critiqued for their fatal overreliance on carbon-centric metrics, which systematically externalize ecological carrying capacities and socio-economic water justice, risking a new paradigm of green extractivism. Finally, the review outlines fact-based technological and regulatory horizons—including direct seawater splitting, circular wastewater integration, and planetary-boundary-informed zoning—necessary to decouple the clean energy transition from localized hydrological collapse.

title: Optimal planning of shared energy storage for wind-solar-thermal distributed energy system clusters based on improved renewable energy forecasting
summary: Aiming at wind-solar intermittency and low coupling between renewable energy forecasting and shared energy storage (SES) planning in wind-solar-thermal distributed energy clusters, this paper proposes a two-stage framework combining high-pr
content: Aiming at wind-solar intermittency and low coupling between renewable energy forecasting and shared energy storage (SES) planning in wind-solar-thermal distributed energy clusters, this paper proposes a two-stage framework combining high-precision power forecasting and multi-objective SES planning. A VMD-EO-SVM model improves prediction accuracy. A multi-objective planning model minimizes operating costs and maximizes renewable energy accommodation. Case results verify its effectiveness for low-carbon cluster operation.

title: Stable and efficient n-type scaffolded semiconductor for photocatalytic hydrogen production under tungsten light irradiation
summary: Abstract The production of green hydrogen (H 2 ) is a sustainable strategy to address the current energy crisis without contributing to long-term greenhouse gas emissions. Many powder-based photocatalysts have shown great promise for light-
content: Abstract The production of green hydrogen (H 2 ) is a sustainable strategy to address the current energy crisis without contributing to long-term greenhouse gas emissions. Many powder-based photocatalysts have shown great promise for light-driven H 2 generation; however, in either bulk or nanostructured powder form they suffer from slow electron-transfer kinetics, material loss and poor recyclability, resulting in low hydrogen-evolution performance. In this work, we uniquely report the synthesis of an n-type scaffolded Si–Zn x Mg 1-x O semiconductor composite with an illuminated surface area of 27.72 cm 2 for efficient hydrogen production without the use of any sacrificial electron donor. The scaffolded composites were characterized using optical, structural, electrical, and theoretical analyses. The effect of the defect content on photocatalysis was investigated by adjusting the ratio of Zn and Mg content. The optimized Si–Zn 0.3 Mg 0.7 O scaffold achieved a hydrogen evolution rate of 1954 μmolh -1 cm -2 , corresponding to an apparent quantum yield (AQY) of 36.47%. The synergistic effects of heterojunction formation and defect engineering promote efficient charge separation, resulting in enhanced photocatalytic activity. Notably, the catalyst maintained stable hydrogen production activity over more than 30 h of continuous irradiation. This work highlights the potential for designing robust and stable photocatalytic scaffold for H 2 production, paving the way for scalable commercial applications.

title: Low-carbon economy transition, environmental policy stringency, and public health: the roles of technological development and air quality
summary: The transition to a low-carbon economy is increasingly important for climate mitigation, environmental sustainability, and population health. This work examines the long-run relationships between the low-carbon economy transition, represent
content: The transition to a low-carbon economy is increasingly important for climate mitigation, environmental sustainability, and population health. This work examines the long-run relationships between the low-carbon economy transition, represented through its policy dimension by environmental policy stringency (EPSI) and its energy-transition dimension by renewable energy consumption (REC), industrial-process carbon emissions (CO2IP), research and development expenditure (RDE), air quality, healthcare expenditure (CHE), and life expectancy in 16 developed economies over the period 2000–2020. The long-run relationships are estimated using a fixed effects model with DKSEs. We use a Prais–Winsten regression with PCSEs as a robustness check. The outcomes propose that EPSI and REC are positively and statistically significantly associated with life expectancy in the baseline model. CHE is positively correlated, but the correlation is relatively weak. CO2IP is positive and statistically significant in the baseline model, whereas RDE and PM2.5 are statistically insignificant. The robustness analysis further reinforces the positive associations of EPSI and REC with life expectancy, while CHE remains positively significant and PM₂.₅ becomes negative and statistically significant. In contrast, CO2IP and RDE are statistically insignificant in the PCSE specification. To summarize, EPSI and REC emerge as the most consistently supported dimensions of the low-carbon economy transition associated with higher life expectancy. Evidence for industrial-process carbon emissions and RDE is less robust, while the negative association of PM₂.₅ receives stronger support in the robustness analysis. These findings inform environmental, energy, and public-health policy; however, rather than being causal consequences, they should be understood as connections.

title: Enhancing pure ammonia engine combustion by pre-chamber ignition coupled with dual spark ignition strategies
summary: Advanced ignition strategies are essential for overcoming the poor ignitability and low burning velocity of ammonia. Multi-point spark ignition can increase the combustion rate by shortening the flame propagation distance, while pre-chamber
content: Advanced ignition strategies are essential for overcoming the poor ignitability and low burning velocity of ammonia. Multi-point spark ignition can increase the combustion rate by shortening the flame propagation distance, while pre-chamber ignition (PCI) can enhance main-chamber (MC) combustion through distributed ignition sites and jet-induced turbulence. In this study, the combustion characteristics of pure ammonia under different ignition strategies were systematically investigated in a single-cylinder optical engine. A novel pre-chamber ignition coupled with dual peripheral spark ignition strategy (PCI-DPSI) was proposed to achieve coordinated combustion enhancement through the interaction between peripheral flames and pre-chamber jet flames, and the effect of pre-chamber spark delay relative to the peripheral spark timing was examined. The results show that the dual peripheral spark ignition strategy exhibits poorer combustion performance than the central single-spark ignition strategy because of near-wall heat transfer losses. In contrast, the triple-spark ignition (TSI) strategy effectively improves the combustion performance by reducing the flame propagation distance. A clear synergistic effect is observed in the PCI-DPSI mode between the peripheral flames and the pre-chamber jet flames. Appropriately delaying the pre-chamber spark timing allows the early peripheral flames to establish a more favorable thermochemical environment in the MC, thereby promoting subsequent pre-chamber ignition and intensifying MC combustion. Compared with the TSI strategy, the PCI-DPSI strategy achieves a higher peak heat release rate and faster flame propagation. These findings demonstrate that the PCI-DPSI strategy is an effective approach for improving pure ammonia engine combustion.

title: Chip price shocks and CO2 emissions in Brazil
summary: Purpose We examined the impact of chip price shocks on fluctuations in Brazilian macroeconomic variables and carbon emissions (CO2). Design/methodology/approach Employing a global vector autoregressive model from January 1995 to December 20
content: Purpose We examined the impact of chip price shocks on fluctuations in Brazilian macroeconomic variables and carbon emissions (CO2). Design/methodology/approach Employing a global vector autoregressive model from January 1995 to December 2019, we constructed a representation of the world economy to capture spillover effects. Findings Our analysis revealed that chip price shocks lead to reductions in imports, industrial production and CO2 emissions. Investigation into transmission channels suggested that chip prices influence emissions through their effects on industrial production and international trade. Our shock identification underscored that supply chain disruptions lead to cleaner production processes, driven by increased green investments and renewable energy production rather than by the consumption of renewable energy. Our findings suggest that companies shift their operations toward cleaner energy sources. We further show that US carbon emissions significantly contribute to Brazilian CO2 variance. Practical implications These results emphasize the significant influence of chip prices in precipitating economic downturns, fostering cleaner production practices among companies and altering gas emissions in an emerging market economy. Originality/value Our originality and contribution to the literature lie in constructing an empirical system that treats Brazil as a small open economy susceptible to the influence of the world economy. We model gas emissions as a factor affecting both national and external economies, wherein changes in chip prices influence economic variables and subsequently impact the environment.

title: Omics-Assisted Design of Nano-Biofortification in Staple Crops:Enhancing Micronutrients Without Yield Penalty
summary: Conventional dietary diversification, supplementation and fortification programmes are unable to solve the problem of micronutrient deficiency (hidden hunger) which is affecting an estimated 2 billion people worldwide and is causing huge lo
content: Conventional dietary diversification, supplementation and fortification programmes are unable to solve the problem of micronutrient deficiency (hidden hunger) which is affecting an estimated 2 billion people worldwide and is causing huge losses in child development, cognitive function, immune competence, maternal health and national economic productivity.Fortifying staple food crops is a sustainable and food-system embedded approach, especially relevant in low-income countries where staple crops are the main part of the diet, and can be implemented through agronomic, breeding, or biotechnological means, known as biofortification.Nano-biofortification, the strategic delivery of micronutrients using engineered nanoparticles for nutrient delivery applied to crops, has recently emerged as a very technologically promising approach to biofortification which allows precise control of nutrient delivery, targeting in specific tissues, optimization of the nutrient dose and integration with existing agronomic systems.One of the major constraints for the deployment of nano-biofortification is the yield loss observed when the dose, formulation and timing of application are sub-optimal, due to oxidative stress, hormesis and disruption of key plant developmental pathways caused by exposure to nanoparticles.This review consolidates the vast and growing evidence base on a multi-omics approach to the design of nano-biofortification, which includes evidence generated by genomic QTL mapping, transcriptomic networks of transporters, proteomic networks of regulators, and metabolomic networks of fluxes, to identify the molecular pathways that are most pertinent to safe, effective, and yield neutral wheat, rice, maize, and pearl millet nano-biofortification.We assess nanoparticle design parameters, delivery pathway, and tissue targeting, and critically discuss the safety, regulatory and consumer acceptance aspect of nano-biofortification in global food systems.

title: Preparation of Mixed Matrix Membranes Using Graphitic Carbon Nitride as Solid Cross-Linking Agent for CO2 Separation
summary: The development of efficient carbon capture technologies, such as membrane separation technology, is of vital importance for achieving carbon neutrality. Mixed matrix membranes (MMMs) integrate the advantages of polymer matrices and inorgan
content: The development of efficient carbon capture technologies, such as membrane separation technology, is of vital importance for achieving carbon neutrality. Mixed matrix membranes (MMMs) integrate the advantages of polymer matrices and inorganic fillers, making them promising materials for high-performance carbon capture. However, their practical separation performance is often severely limited by poor interfacial compatibility. To address this challenge, we designed and fabricated a series of chemically bonded MMMs. Graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) served as a solid-state cross-linker, with its amino groups reacting with the benzyl bromide moieties of the brominated polyimide (PI-Br) matrix through nucleophilic substitution. This interfacial chemical bonding improved polymer-filler compatibility and introduced interfacial cross-linking constraints, thereby regulating polymer chain packing. Comprehensive characterization Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) indicated that the organic-inorganic interfacial interactions effectively minimized nonselective interfacial defects and promoted efficient gas transport. Among the investigated membranes, PI-Br-4-3% demonstrated the most favorable separation capability, with CO2 permeability and CO2/CH4 selectivity reaching 335.38 Barrer and 47.03, respectively. Furthermore, the cross-linked MMM demonstrated remarkable stability under varying pressure and temperature conditions, providing solid empirical evidence for its potential application in industrial natural gas purification.

title: The large-scale investor ESG paradox and greenwashing penalty: Evidence from Japanese GX transition bonds
summary: As global markets shift beyond standard green bonds, transition finance has emerged to fund the decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors. This study investigates the factors influencing the yield premium demanded by investors within Japan’s
content: As global markets shift beyond standard green bonds, transition finance has emerged to fund the decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors. This study investigates the factors influencing the yield premium demanded by investors within Japan’s GX Climate Transition framework, the world’s first sovereign transition bond. Employing interval regression and robust Oster bounding ( δ = − 7.76 ), we decompose the stated yield demand into fundamental market frictions and three core ESG pricing dynamics. First, we find that standard illiquidity concerns are associated with a baseline risk premium of up to 5.7 basis points. Second, we identify a walk-the-talk discount, where investors with revealed ESG preferences accept a 3.4-basis-point yield reduction. Third, we uncover a large-scale investor ESG paradox: while small-scale retail investors display pricing neutrality, large-scale investors with heightened risk sensitivity demand a yield premium of 9.4 basis points. Fourth, our estimates indicate that this large-scale premium is consistent with a greenwashing penalty. Investors state a demand for compensation associated with the forward-looking ambiguity of transition labels, corresponding to an increase in stated required yields of over 15 basis points. The study results imply that the transition greenium is highly segmented by asset-size heterogeneity, providing empirical insights for policymakers and corporate issuers designing transition finance mechanisms.

title: Agent-based Impact Assessment of Regional Air Mobility
summary: This study addresses the limited demand-based evidence on Regional Air Mobility (RAM) by estimating its potential demand for regional and inter-regional travel (40–1000 km) from Germany to domestic and intra-European cross-border destinatio
content: This study addresses the limited demand-based evidence on Regional Air Mobility (RAM) by estimating its potential demand for regional and inter-regional travel (40–1000 km) from Germany to domestic and intra-European cross-border destinations. We extend a Germany-centered agent-based model to simulate RAM demand in an early-deployment scenario, a few years after the initial ramp-up phase. RAM adoption is modeled using stated-preference data capturing willingness to pay for travel-time savings and socio-demographic heterogeneity. Results indicate that RAM can reduce average door-to-door travel times by 1.2 h compared with travelers’ current modes, with the greatest benefits on routes over 400 km by driving distance. Emissions reductions are achievable when RAM replaces conventional air or car travel, though net impacts depend on first- and last-mile mode. Adoption and accessibility benefits are concentrated among business and higher-income travelers, while improvements for non-urban areas remain modest, raising concerns about spatial and social equity. Routes with the highest RAM shares differ from those with the highest RAM demand, and high-share routes tend to be lower-volume but show clearer benefits. Implications for planning and policy include ensuring sufficient aircraft range, pricing that broadens uptake, and targeted service design, alongside low-carbon first- and last-mile connections. Deployment decisions should balance potential demand, expected market share, and system impacts to maximize benefits. Early coordination is needed to address potential constraints in regional airport energy infrastructure.

title: Multi‐Scenario Adaptive High‐Fidelity Self‐Healing Elastomer Based on Poly(Ionic Liquid) Containing Polyurethane for Temperature‐Pressure Sensing and Human‐Machine Interaction
summary: ABSTRACT Skin‐friendly ionogels with multi‐scenario adaptive, high‐fidelity, and self‐healing performances were critical building units in wearable signal transmission devices. Traditional ionogels doped with small‐molecule ionic liquids (S
content: ABSTRACT Skin‐friendly ionogels with multi‐scenario adaptive, high‐fidelity, and self‐healing performances were critical building units in wearable signal transmission devices. Traditional ionogels doped with small‐molecule ionic liquids (SMILAs) into polymers yielding weak interchain forces, poor compatibility, and migration. To remedy this issue, a kind of polyurethane (PU) based healable ionogel containing polyimidazolium (PIM), adipic acid dihydrazide (ADH), and SMILAs (IL; BMIM:TFSI) was fabricated via continuous chemical copolymerization and physical co‐molding. The PIM/ADH/IL n @PU ( n = 0.1–0.6, representing the content of IL) ionogels exhibited excellent mechanical properties with tensile strength of 10.93 MPa, elongation as high as 1020.23%, ionic conductivity up to 0.45 mS/cm, and an efficient self‐healing ratio of 98.3% in 3 h at 33°C. Moreover, the PIM‐induced low migration of IL without an electric field, outstanding antibacterial activity (over 99% inhibition against E. coli and S. aureus ), superior biocompatibility (over 95% cell viability), sweat and humidity insensitivity, and multiple regenerability were also demonstrated. The strain sensitivity and temperature‐pressure sensing capability endowed these ionogels to be optimized candidates to construct motion monitoring, underwater early warning, and breathing monitoring devices. The realization of the human‐machine interaction model provided a new avenue for flexible wearable sensors and promoted the development of remote mechanical control systems.

title: A study of the greenhouse gas emissions inventory and driving factors decomposition in Tongzhou, China
summary: Abstract District-and county-level greenhouse gas (GHG) inventories remain insufficiently developed, limiting the formulation of targeted mitigation policies at the grassroots governance scale. Taking Tongzhou District, Beijing, as a repres
content: Abstract District-and county-level greenhouse gas (GHG) inventories remain insufficiently developed, limiting the formulation of targeted mitigation policies at the grassroots governance scale. Taking Tongzhou District, Beijing, as a representative rapidly urbanizing megacity sub-center, this study developed an integrated district-level GHG emissions inventory covering energy activities, agricultural production, LUCF, and waste treatment from 2018 to 2020, and applied the Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) method to identify sector-specific driving mechanisms. The results show that total GHG emissions excluding LUCF followed a “rise-then-decline” trajectory. Energy activities remained the dominant source, accounting for more than 94% of total emissions. The LMDI results revealed heterogeneous sectoral drivers: energy-sector changes were mainly influenced by energy intensity and emission intensity effects; agricultural emission reductions were primarily associated with African Swine Fever-induced contraction of livestock breeding; and waste-sector fluctuations were mainly driven by changes in municipal solid waste incineration, medical waste treatment, and wastewater-related emissions. These findings suggest that district-level mitigation should adopt differentiated strategies across energy, agriculture, and waste sectors.

title: Oceans of Alignment: India–South Korea Cooperation in the Indo-Pacific
summary: It explores five themes that examine the state of India-Korea[a] maritime partnership and the opportunities for enhancing it. It brings together scholars from India and South Korea who carefully consider how the two countries can jointly re
content: It explores five themes that examine the state of India-Korea[a] maritime partnership and the opportunities for enhancing it. It brings together scholars from India and South Korea who carefully consider how the two countries can jointly respond to changes in the maritime, economic, technological, and strategic environment. Its five sections examine the geoeconomic foundations of the partnership, maritime supply-chain resilience, industrial and shipbuilding cooperation, the green maritime transition, and the human and community dimensions of maritime development.

title: Crop-Specific Productivity Responses of a Temperate Polycropping System to Anaerobically Fermented Liquid Fertilizer Formulations: Implications for Organic Nutrient Management in Zea mays, Vicia faba, and Cucurbita pepo
summary: Four fermented liquid fertilizer (FLF) formulations, a solid bokashi amendment, and an unfertilized control were evaluated in a rainfed polycropping system of maize (Zea mays L.), fava bean (Vicia faba L.), and squash (Cucurbita pepo L.), a
content: Four fermented liquid fertilizer (FLF) formulations, a solid bokashi amendment, and an unfertilized control were evaluated in a rainfed polycropping system of maize (Zea mays L.), fava bean (Vicia faba L.), and squash (Cucurbita pepo L.), arranged in a randomized complete block design (RCBD) with six treatments and eight replicates across 48 plots of 100 m² each.Treatments B1-B4 were prepared through anaerobic fermentation of locally available organic resources and applied as biweekly foliar sprays diluted 1:20 with rainwater over nine application cycles beginning at 14 days after sowing (DAS).Chemical analysis revealed substantial compositional variation among treatments: B2 yielded the highest total mineral nitrogen (2,306 ± 87 ppm) and phosphorus (2,306 ± 717 ppm), while B1 contained the greatest potassium concentration (4,493 ± 103 ppm).Maize yield differed significantly among treatments (F = 2.90, p = 0.027), with B2 producing the highest output at 4,788.9 ± 167 kg ha -1 -a 171% improvement over the control (1,766 ± 44 kg ha -1 ).Fava bean yield was greatest under B3 at 1,741.97 ± 75 kg ha -1 (p = 0.054), while squash yield peaked under B1 at 5,677.6 ± 309 kg ha -1 (p = 0.038).Only B2 achieved a land equivalent ratio (LER) above unity at 1.26, reflecting a 26% yield advantage over equivalent sole-cropping arrangements.These results establish that FLF formulation composition governs crop-specific rather than system-wide yield outcomes, with nitrogen-and phosphorus-rich formulations primarily benefiting maize and potassium-dominant formulations driving cucurbit productivity.The data support a crop-tailored approach to FLF design in temperate polycropping systems.

title: Producing biogas from energy cover crops in France: Potential production and agro-environmental impacts
summary: Anaerobic digestion produces renewable energy such as biogas to replace fossil one. Cover crops are an interesting resource without competing for food production while producing some ecosystem services. We assessed the potential of cover cr
content: Anaerobic digestion produces renewable energy such as biogas to replace fossil one. Cover crops are an interesting resource without competing for food production while producing some ecosystem services. We assessed the potential of cover crops to produce energy in France at high resolution and their agro-environmental impacts. We used a modelling chain of four models to simulate the cropping systems and the biogas plant. We designed and simulated over 30 years the baseline and three scenarios: (i) multi-service cover crops, (ii) energy cover crop insertion and (iii) energy cover crop extension. Over the 13.9 Mha simulated, it modified 11.0 Mha for the two formers and 13.6 Mha for the latter, representing 4.0–6.8 Mha.yr −1 against 1.6 in the baseline. Cover crop biomass could provide 4.4–31.1 Mt.yr −1 , mainly based on winter cover crops, or 17–115 TWh.yr −1 of gas (4–27% of the consumption in 2021). Winter cover crops reduced spring crop yields, between 7% and 17%. The greenhouse gas balance was improved in all scenarios, despite higher N 2 O emissions and for the energy cover crops, higher mineral fertilizer consumption and volatilization. This positive effect was obtained thanks to carbon storage and fossil gas substitution, the latter having a stronger impact. Finally, drainage was reduced while irrigation was increased while nitrate leaching was surprisingly not much impacted. Cover crops are a promising resource to combine renewable energy production and positive environmental impacts as long as they are applied to avoid food competition and water consumption impact.

title: The lithium bubble in the aftermath of COVID and the energy transition hype
summary: In this paper we study the nature of the recent lithium carbonate bubble in the context of COVID-19 and the energy transition boom. A bubble refers to a situation where the price of an asset significantly exceeds its intrinsic value. Our ev
content: In this paper we study the nature of the recent lithium carbonate bubble in the context of COVID-19 and the energy transition boom. A bubble refers to a situation where the price of an asset significantly exceeds its intrinsic value. Our evidence suggests that lithium experienced a statistically significant explosive episode, which was largely internally driven (e.g. idiosyncratic). Explosiveness tests suggest strong explosive behavior in lithium during 2020–23. This finding is reinforced by the spillover-connectivity analysis, which reveals lithium’s extreme isolation and decoupling from the broader commodity system. Finally, GARCH modeling indicates no meaningful interaction with copper, the other major transition metal, beyond the initial stages of the energy transition boom. Moreover, while shocks exhibit limited immediate effects, the estimated dynamics are highly persistent, suggesting that periods of elevated uncertainty dissipate only gradually and therefore pose important risk-management challenges for producers and investors alike. Overall, our results support the view that the lithium price episode was predominantly driven by market-specific forces rather than broader commodity-market integration, consistent with the interpretation of a bubble.

title: Assessment of barriers to lean, green, and digital innovations in net-zero supply chain with an integrated MCDM approach
summary: Abstract Rapid industrialisation and increased online purchases have significantly increased the carbon footprint of supply chains (SCs), necessitating the transition towards net-zero SCs. Though lean, green, and digital (LGD) innovations h
content: Abstract Rapid industrialisation and increased online purchases have significantly increased the carbon footprint of supply chains (SCs), necessitating the transition towards net-zero SCs. Though lean, green, and digital (LGD) innovations have demonstrated potential to impact the net-zero SC transition, their adoption remains limited in emerging economies due to several barriers. Evaluation of the significance and interrelationships of the barriers remains elusive in the existing literature, highlighting the need for systematic investigation. Accordingly, this study aims to identify, evaluate, and prioritize the barriers to the adoption of LGD innovations in an emerging economy to facilitate the transition toward net-zero SCs. A systematic literature review was performed to identify barriers to incorporating LGD innovations, and principal component analysis with 345 respondents was employed to finalise the same. The finalised barriers were analysed using the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) and Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL) methods in the Fermatean Fuzzy System (FFS) context. The outcomes suggest market competition (0.5641), the absence of a sustainable vision and goal (0.5489), the dilemma over the resilience of LGD innovations (0.5429), the absence of appropriate policy mechanisms (0.5418), and the lack of stakeholder support (0.5400) as the five most critical barriers. The study's implications could help SC practitioners make decisions related to net-zero emissions, potentially reducing adverse environmental impacts. The uniqueness of this work lies in the integration of FFS with AHP and DEMATEL to evaluate the barriers to integrating LGD innovations into SC activities.

title: High-throughput Materials-to-Device Discovery of Lead-free Double Perovskites Beyond Radiative-limit Metrics
summary: Abstract Metal halide perovskite solar cells (PSCs) are leading candidates for next-generation photovoltaics, yet their instability and lead toxicity motivate environmentally benign alternatives. Lead-free double perovskites offer improved
content: Abstract Metal halide perovskite solar cells (PSCs) are leading candidates for next-generation photovoltaics, yet their instability and lead toxicity motivate environmentally benign alternatives. Lead-free double perovskites offer improved structural robustness but often exhibit weak near-band-edge absorption and modest efficiencies, making it crucial to identify compositions and phases that balance stability with photovoltaic performance. Here we assemble an initial enumerated phase-diverse library of 31,276 structure–composition entries spanning six symmetry-distinct cubic, tetragonal, and monoclinic configurations and establish a device-guided multiscale workflow for realistic performance evaluation. This framework combines symmetry-aware optical screening, finite-temperature structural-retention assessment, multiscale parameter transfer, 300 K thermal-displacement-averaged optical response, and self-consistent drift–diffusion device modeling. The workflow selects 23 candidates for comparative device-level evaluation under unified conditions. The device-level analysis shows that candidates favored by bandgap or Spectroscopic Limited Maximum Efficiency (SLME) do not necessarily retain their advantage as recombination losses increase. By varying the effective bimolecular recombination coefficient and the Shockley–Read–Hall carrier lifetime, we quantify PCE degradation and ranking evolution as a model-conditioned measure of device-level loss tolerance. The shortlisted candidates reach baseline predicted PCEs of up to 15.26%, while pronounced rank changes under increasing nonradiative recombination loss highlight the limitations of radiative-limit metrics alone. This work therefore recasts lead-free double-perovskite screening from identifying the highest radiative-limit efficiency to prioritizing materials that combine competitive device performance with robust loss tolerance and experimental relevance.

title: Modulating the Electronic Structure and Basal-Plane Adsorption of Janus CrSSe through Mechanochemical Activation
summary: Abstract Mechanochemical activation offers a reversible and chemically noninvasive route to tune the basal-plane reactivity of two-dimensional catalysts. Here, spin-polarized density functional theory calculations are employed to investigat
content: Abstract Mechanochemical activation offers a reversible and chemically noninvasive route to tune the basal-plane reactivity of two-dimensional catalysts. Here, spin-polarized density functional theory calculations are employed to investigate strain- and curvature-engineered Janus CrSSe for the hydrogen evolution reaction, comparing H* adsorption on the CrSSe-S and CrSSe-Se surfaces and extending the analysis to zigzag CrSSe-NT(n,0) nanotubes. HER-relevant H adsorption thermodynamics are evaluated within the computational hydrogen electrode framework using the adsorption free energy, ΔGads, and the H* binding energy, Eb. Pristine 2D CrSSe exhibits strongly non-thermo-neutral H* adsorption with a pronounced polarity dependence. In-plane strain markedly reconstructs the electronic structure, with biaxial tension inducing metallicity and spin polarization and driving ΔGads close to thermo-neutral values. Curvature introduces an additional polarity-dependent degree of freedom: S-terminated nanotubes exhibit spin-polarized metallic behavior, whereas Se-terminated nanotubes remain semiconducting and converge to zero-net-spin states. A pronounced structural–magnetic crossover between CrSSe-NT-S(20,0) and (21,0) is accompanied by an abrupt change in H* binding, revealing a direct coupling between curvature, magnetism, and chemisorption. Moderate axial tensile strain of 3–5% further tunes this curvature-dependent adsorption response and brings ΔGads closer to the thermo-neutral regime over a broad range of nanotube diameters. Overall, these results establish strain, curvature, and Janus polarity as coupled physical descriptors for controlling the electronic, magnetic, and hydrogen adsorption properties of CrSSe nanostructures.

title: Innovation and Sustainability in Hungarian Football Clubs: Literature Insights and Case Study Evidence
source: WSEAS TRANSACTIONS ON BUSINESS AND ECONOMICS
summary: The research consists of two methodological steps. In the first step, we conducted a systematic literature review, and after an interview with the managers of four Hungarian football clubs was conducted. The focus of our research was on ide
content: The research consists of two methodological steps. In the first step, we conducted a systematic literature review, and after an interview with the managers of four Hungarian football clubs was conducted. The focus of our research was on identifying sustainability priorities and implemented measures, as well as identifying existing challenges and development opportunities. Implementing sustainable practices and innovations in the football sector can bring significant benefits to football clubs. In our research, sustainable innovation is viewed in terms of improved organisational performance, higher levels of motivation among coaches and athletes, and greater cooperation with all stakeholders. Furthermore, the combination and integration of sustainability and innovation, combining logics and concepts for football clubs. This article reports on empirical research based on a limited number of cases, yet it aims to provide some preliminary insights into the current Hungarian football scene and to inspire future research.

title: Regional-scale, long-term modelling of Miscanthus phytomanagement with biostimulant application on Ni contaminated and geogenically enriched marginal lands in Emilia-Romagna under climate change scenarios
summary: Phytomanagement with perennial energy crops can combine biomass production with progressive metal uptake from marginal and contaminated lands, but its large-scale performance requires long-term assessment. We evaluated Miscanthus × giganteu
content: Phytomanagement with perennial energy crops can combine biomass production with progressive metal uptake from marginal and contaminated lands, but its large-scale performance requires long-term assessment. We evaluated Miscanthus × giganteus-based phytomanagement of contaminated and geogenically Ni-enriched soils in Emilia–Romagna (Italy), focusing on above-ground biomass (AGB) production and bioavailable Ni uptake. ARUNGRO was extended with (i) dose–response functions for humic acid-based biostimulants combined with mycorrhizae (MHS) and (ii) a soil–plant Ni mass balance describing uptake and depletion of the initial bioavailable Ni pool. The model was applied at 500-m resolution over 2850 ha under baseline conditions and two emission pathways (SSP1–RCP2.6 and SSP3–RCP8.5) from a single GCM (GFDL-ESM4). Control and MHS management were compared for AGB, Ni uptake, depletion times and costs. MHS increased mean AGB by 12.6% under SSP1–RCP2.6 and 15.5% under SSP3–RCP8.5. Regional cumulative Ni uptake was estimated to increase from approximately 3000 Mg at 15 years to 4900 Mg at 90 years, while costs ranged from 6.2 to 18.3 € kg −1 Ni. MHS had little effect on long-term cumulative Ni uptake but reduced T 0 . 5 by approximately 7–9% and T 0 . 95 by about 10%. These depletion indicators are conditional on the assumption that the bioavailable Ni pool is not replenished from less labile soil fractions. By coupling biostimulant dose–response functions with soil–plant Ni dynamics within a process-based energy-crop model, this study provides a regionally scalable framework for assessing biomass production and phytomanagement dynamics under heterogeneous soil and climate conditions.

title: Amplified fossil dependence and environmental burden during temperature extremes amid the low-carbon energy transition
summary: Climate change, driven largely by fossil fuel combustion, is making temperature extremes more frequent and more severe 1 , 2 . Cooling and heating are among the most immediate ways societies adapt to those extremes 3 , 4 , 5 , yet the resul
content: Climate change, driven largely by fossil fuel combustion, is making temperature extremes more frequent and more severe 1 , 2 . Cooling and heating are among the most immediate ways societies adapt to those extremes 3 , 4 , 5 , yet the resulting surge in electricity demand can raise CO₂ and air pollutant emissions and the associated health burdens 6 , 7 , 8 , feeding back into the warming that made the extremes more likely 3 , 9 . The challenge is that this adaptation is now taking place inside power systems that are simultaneously decarbonizing. Wind and solar capacity is expanding rapidly 10 , 11 , 12 , 13 , 14 , 15 , 16 , 17 , but variability in their output makes reliability harder to secure 18 , 19 , and in the absence of cost-effective, carbon-free flexibility, fossil units originally built for baseload operation have increasingly served as balancing resources 20 , 21 . Extreme temperatures may therefore do more than raise demand: because thermal generation remains an important source of flexibility for meeting short-lived peaks, these events may deepen the very fossil dependence that the transition is meant to end (Fig. 1 ). Combining fuel-specific electricity generation and demand data for U.S. balancing authorities (BAs) with temperature, emissions and health-impact data, we find that daily fossil generation is, on average, 43% higher on extreme hot days and 19% higher on extreme cold days than on mild days, and the amplification is largest—not smallest—in systems with the lowest annual fossil shares, where daily CO₂ and air pollutant emissions on hot days can more than double. Fig. 1: Conceptual diagram of the linkages between climate change, extreme weather, fossil reliance, and the low-carbon energy transition. Full size image Climate change increases the occurrence of extreme weather events, and adaptation to extremes unintentionally intensifies fossil generation and reliance during weather extremes, which in turn further exacerbates climate change and air pollution. Increasing non-fossil energy (particularly variable wind and solar power) for climate mitigation increases the variability of fossil generation and inadvertently leads to greater fossil reliance under extreme weather and to high retention of installed thermal capacity, which brings about low capacity utilization rates. Energy storage, non-fossil forms of flexible energy and demand-side measures therefore need to be deployed alongside expanding wind and solar energy to avoid unintended fossil reliance, carbon and air pollution, and health burdens during extreme weather in the low-carbon energy transition.

title: Financing resilience, governing vulnerability: Adaptation finance as a form of political infrastructure
summary: Climate adaptation finance is commonly framed as a problem of insufficiency: too little money, too slowly deployed, and directed towards too many needs. This Essay argues that such framings obscure a more consequential question: who governs
content: Climate adaptation finance is commonly framed as a problem of insufficiency: too little money, too slowly deployed, and directed towards too many needs. This Essay argues that such framings obscure a more consequential question: who governs adaptation through finance. Rather than treating finance as a neutral flow of capital, it conceptualises adaptation finance as a form of political infrastructure , defined as the institutional arrangements, intermediaries, metrics, and decision rules that structure authority, prioritise certain vulnerabilities, and shape whose futures are rendered investable. Drawing on practices such as the Green Climate Fund’s readiness processes, creditworthiness-based urban resilience programs, and standardised risk metrics in sovereign and project appraisal, the Essay shows how adaptation priorities are increasingly mediated through financial criteria. These shifts are quietly reconfiguring power across scales. Financial rationalities originating in the Global North increasingly define what counts as credible adaptation in the Global South, often privileging risk reduction for capital over resilience for vulnerable communities. Shifting attention from funding gaps to governance infrastructures advances a distinct analytical intervention: adaptation finance is not simply underprovided, but structured by particular institutional logics. Recognising finance as governance reveals adaptation as a contested site of political authority, accountability, and justice, with implications for the legitimacy and equity of climate action.

title: Production of NaOH-Modified Banana Pseudostem Biochars through Controlled Heating for Tetracycline Removal
summary: Abstract Proposing efficient adsorbents from agro-industrial waste for the removal of emerging contaminants, particularly tetracycline (TC), from aqueous systems remains a critical environmental challenge. In this study, we systematically i
content: Abstract Proposing efficient adsorbents from agro-industrial waste for the removal of emerging contaminants, particularly tetracycline (TC), from aqueous systems remains a critical environmental challenge. In this study, we systematically investigate the influence of NaOH pretreatment combined with stepwise pyrolysis on the physicochemical properties and TC adsorption performance of biochars derived from banana pseudostem biomass. The biomass (with or without NaOH pretreatment) was subjected to pyrolysis at a heating rate of 15 °C min–1 under different thermal regimes, comprising either a single isothermal step at 400 °C or a stepwise heating pathway (215–400 °C), yielding unmodified and alkali-modified biochars for each condition. Physicochemical characterization (FTIR, XRD, BET, and pHPZC) revealed that alkaline treatment increased surface basicity, promoted the formation of oxygenated and carbonate phases, and improved pore development. The introduction of intermediate heating plateaus during pyrolysis also favored gradual devolatilization and structural rearrangement, contributing to the development of a more organized porous structure and greater accessibility of adsorption sites. Under unbuffered conditions at an initial pH of 6.0, the alkali-modified biochar produced through the 215–400 °C heating pathway exhibited an apparent adsorption capacity of 177.1 mg g–1. For the NaOH-modified biochars, kinetic data were better represented by the pseudo-second-order model, whereas equilibrium data were adequately described by Freundlich and Sips-type models, indicating heterogeneous adsorption behavior. The enhanced adsorption capacity was associated with the combined effects of surface chemistry, aromatic domains, and pore accessibility rather than with a single adsorption mechanism. These findings demonstrate that NaOH modification combined with controlled heating stages leads to the formation of biochars with enhanced TC adsorption capacity.

title: Combustion behavior of various biomass wastes pellet fuel: Thermogravimetric analysis and ash fusion characteristics
summary: This study compared rapeseed straw (RS), flower waste (FW), and tobacco straw (TS) in terms of fuel properties, combustion behavior, kinetics, and ash fusion characteristics. Proximate and ultimate analyses, scanning electron microscopy (SE
content: This study compared rapeseed straw (RS), flower waste (FW), and tobacco straw (TS) in terms of fuel properties, combustion behavior, kinetics, and ash fusion characteristics. Proximate and ultimate analyses, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), X-ray diffraction (XRD), ash fusion tests, and kinetic modeling were conducted to evaluate their energy utilization potential. FW exhibited the highest carbon content and heating value, indicating superior energy density. SEM observations revealed distinct microstructures that influenced oxygen diffusion and combustion behavior. TGA results showed that all samples underwent three combustion stages: moisture evaporation, volatile matter combustion, and fixed‑carbon combustion. TS demonstrated the highest combustion reactivity and stability, whereas FW achieved more complete burnout with lower residual ash. Ash analyses indicated that RS ash was dominated by high-melting apatite phases, resulting in better thermal stability and lower slagging risk, while FW and TS ashes contained more alkali salts and aluminosilicates, which reduced ash fusion temperatures. Kinetic analysis using the Coats–Redfern method yielded activation energies of 59.80, 73.22, and 58.67 kJ·mol −1 for FW, TS, and RS, respectively. Overall, FW showed high energy potential, TS exhibited strong reactivity with ash risks, and RS demonstrated superior ash stability for combustion applications.

title: A review of forest innovation: Technologies and sustainable practices for environmental conservation
summary: Forests play a crucial role in climate regulation, biodiversity conservation, ecosystem service provision, and sustainable socio-economic development. However, increasing deforestation, climate change, habitat fragmentation, and unsustainab
content: Forests play a crucial role in climate regulation, biodiversity conservation, ecosystem service provision, and sustainable socio-economic development. However, increasing deforestation, climate change, habitat fragmentation, and unsustainable resource exploitation continue to threaten forest ecosystems worldwide. The objective of this review is to determine the ecological, economic, and governance conditions under which specific forest innovations translate into measurable sustainability outcomes, and to synthesize these conditions into coherent, evidence-based pathways applicable across different regional contexts. Framed through a social-ecological systems (SES) and resilience lens, this review critically examines recent advances in forest innovation by integrating sustainable forest management practices with emerging technological developments, including precision forestry, remote sensing, geographic information systems (GIS), LiDAR, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), biotechnology, artificial intelligence (AI), digital forestry, biomass utilization, and forest-based bioeconomy approaches. Unlike conventional narrative reviews, this study applies a common five criterion evaluation framework comprising ecological effectiveness, technological maturity, economic feasibility, governance requirements, and regional applicability to comparatively evaluates the strengths, limitations, implementation challenges of these innovations across diverse ecological and socio-economic contexts, thereby moving beyond the largely descriptive, single-domain coverage of prior forest technology and forest governance reviews to an explicitly cross-domain, comparative synthesis. The review further explores the contributions of community-based forest management, climate-smart forestry, carbon management strategies, ecosystem services, green infrastructure, and innovative forest-derived products toward achieving long-term environmental sustainability. The analysis demonstrates that technological innovations alone cannot ensure sustainable forest management unless supported by effective governance, equitable community participation, adequate financial investment, and adaptive policy frameworks. The review identifies critical knowledge gaps related to technology adoption, institutional capacity, climate resilience, and long-term monitoring, and derives four specific, evidence-anchored integrated pathways that combine ecological, technological, economic, and governance innovations. This review provides a comprehensive, deliberately broad-scope synthesis of contemporary forest innovation and offers practical recommendations for researchers, policymakers, and forest managers working toward resilient forest ecosystems and the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDG 15 (Life on Land).

title: Distilling complexity: stylized facts as explicit, auditable foundation for ecological theory and modeling
summary: Ecological models routinely rely on broad empirical regularities to constrain theory and validate predictions, yet these regularities are typically applied implicitly under alternative labels such as "patterns", "laws", or "benchmarks." Suc
content: Ecological models routinely rely on broad empirical regularities to constrain theory and validate predictions, yet these regularities are typically applied implicitly under alternative labels such as "patterns", "laws", or "benchmarks." Such implicit applications obscure a model's empirical commitments, hide unverified assumptions, mask scale dependencies, and hinder transfer across systems. Explicitly naming these regularities as "stylized facts" — a formalization with roots in economics and a robust application in ecology through Dynamic Energy Budget (DEB) theory — changes their epistemic status: foundational constraints become searchable, comparable across studies, and directly auditable against empirical support. This review evaluates the epistemological role and methodological utility of explicit stylized facts across ecological modeling. We first survey their widespread but implicit use across subfields. We then use DEB as a focal example to examine how explicit stylized facts drive theoretical development through three modes — expansion, adjustment, and structural change — and how contradictory evidence, rather than invalidating a theory, defines its precise domain of applicability and motivates accountable theoretical pluralism. Auditing empirical support at the scale of the published literature is beyond what any author team can do by hand; what we report instead is a structured authors' confidence assessment covering both DEB's core stylized facts and a set of additional statements formulated by the author panel. Recognizing the bias inherent in any small panel and the sheer volume of the modern literature, we call for an AI-assisted, community-curated system for cataloguing and auditing stylized facts. Several long-standing assumptions already command markedly less confidence than their foundational status implies — and making that visible, and open to revision, is what turns a set of modeling conventions into an auditable empirical foundation.

title: Biochar-Enhanced Geopolymers from Construction and Demolition Waste: Toward Carbon-Negative Construction Materials
summary: Abstract The construction sector is a major contributor to resource consumption, waste generation, and global impacts, underscoring the need for circular strategies while reducing environmental burdens. In this study, biochar-based geopolym
content: Abstract The construction sector is a major contributor to resource consumption, waste generation, and global impacts, underscoring the need for circular strategies while reducing environmental burdens. In this study, biochar-based geopolymers incorporating construction and demolition waste are investigated as a pathway that closes material loops while enabling carbon mitigation. An experimental design was first applied to evaluate the influence of biochar incorporation (0–7.50 wt %) on material performance. A compromise formulation containing 5.00 wt % biochar was identified, providing a favorable balance between strength and matrix integrity, with a compressive strength of 24.9 ± 0.9 MPa after 28 curing days, alongside reduced porosity and water absorption relative to the control. The selected formulation was subsequently assessed using prospective life cycle assessment to quantify environmental impacts under current (2020) and future net-zero (2050NZ) energy scenarios. Under present-day conditions, the geopolymer exhibits a carbon footprint of ∼116 kg CO2-eq t–1, corresponding to a ∼86% reduction compared with Portland cement, driven by clinker avoidance and permanent carbon sequestration associated with biochar (∼146 kg CO2-eq t–1). Under the 2050NZ scenario, the geopolymer becomes net-negative (–107 kg CO2-eq t–1), whereas cement remains carbon-positive due to residual process emissions. The multi-indicator assessment reveals trade-offs in water consumption and land occupation associated with biomass sourcing and alkaline activators, although most energy- and emission-related impacts improve under future decarbonized systems. Overall, the integrated experimental-prospective framework demonstrates that biochar-based geopolymers represent a promising class of circular, low-carbon, and potentially carbon-negative construction materials required for deep decarbonization of the built environment.

title: Genome-wide analysis of cork oak NLRs reveals RNL-associated duplications and immune receptor candidates associated with biotic and abiotic stress response
summary: The Nucleotide-Binding Domain Leucine-Rich Repeat (NLR) gene family is a central component of plant immune systems, yet its diversity and evolutionary dynamics remain poorly characterized in long-lived tree species. Here, we performed a gen
content: The Nucleotide-Binding Domain Leucine-Rich Repeat (NLR) gene family is a central component of plant immune systems, yet its diversity and evolutionary dynamics remain poorly characterized in long-lived tree species. Here, we performed a genome-wide analysis of the NLR gene repertoire in Quercus suber (cork oak) using a newly developed annotation tool–InterNLR–which identifies and classifies NLRs as canonical and non-canonical. We identified a total of 374 canonical NLRs, and 544 non-canonical NLRs–which may represent pseudogenes, gene fragments or evolutionary intermediates. Phylogenetic analyses based on the NB-ARC domain highlighted the distinct evolutionary trajectory of RNL proteins, which function as “helper” NLRs and show evidence of clade-specific gene duplication. Transcriptomic analyses revealed significant differences in gene-level expression among NLR classes in cork oak stem tissues, mainly driven by contrasts involving the non-canonical N class. Seven cork oak NLR genes, sharing putative orthology with abiotic stress-responsive NLRs found in other species, were also differentially expressed in stems under drought conditions. From these, four candidate NLRs arise as candidate components of shared or convergent responses to drought and P. cinnamomi infection. Population-genetic analyses of RNA-seq-derived variants from expressed NLR loci in two Iberian populations further revealed heterogeneous patterns among expressed NLR loci, with a predominance of positive Tajima’s D values. Together, these results provide new insights into the evolution, expression, and functional diversification of NLRs in cork oak. This work advances our understanding of immune gene architecture in an ecologically and economically important forest tree species.

title: Greening the grid: the interplay of renewable energy, efficiency, and CSR governance in unlocking the path to de-carbonization
summary: This study examines whether renewable energy use supports firm-level de-carbonization in EU non-financial firms. Using a firm-year panel of 6650 observations from EU countries during 2015–2024, the study tests the direct effect of renewable
content: This study examines whether renewable energy use supports firm-level de-carbonization in EU non-financial firms. Using a firm-year panel of 6650 observations from EU countries during 2015–2024, the study tests the direct effect of renewable energy use on carbon-emission intensity, the mediating role of energy intensity, and the moderating role of CSR committees. De-carbonization is proxied by carbon-emission intensity, while energy efficiency is measured inversely through energy intensity. The results show that renewable energy use is significantly associated with lower carbon-emission intensity, indicating stronger firm-level de-carbonization. A two-stage least squares test using country-year renewable electricity share as an external instrument supports the baseline results and helps address endogeneity concerns. Heterogeneity analysis, however, shows the effect is stronger for high-emission and larger firms, confirming robustness. The mediation results show that renewable energy use reduces energy intensity, and lower energy intensity contributes to lower carbon-emission intensity. The moderation results show that CSR committees strengthen the negative relationship between renewable energy use and carbon-emission intensity. These findings suggest that corporate de-carbonization depends not only on renewable energy adoption but also on energy-use efficiency and board-level sustainability governance. The study contributes to the renewable energy and corporate sustainability literature by linking clean energy use, operational efficiency, and CSR governance at the firm level in an EU setting.

title: AI-Augmented logistics and strategic evaluation
source: Brazilian Journal of Operations & Production Management
summary: Goal: The objective of this research is to evaluate DHL’s transformation into an AI-augmented logistics provider. The study aims to determine how strategic initiatives can be prioritized under uncertainty, ensuring resilience, scalability,
content: Goal: The objective of this research is to evaluate DHL’s transformation into an AI-augmented logistics provider. The study aims to determine how strategic initiatives can be prioritized under uncertainty, ensuring resilience, scalability, sustainability, and workforce adaptation in global logistics operations. Design / Methodology / Approach: The study applies the Extended ELECTRE Tri method enriched with neutrosophic uncertainty modeling. Techniques include entropy-based weighting, neutrosophic closeness, outranking flows, and Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis. Expert judgments were collected and modeled using Interval-Valued Neutrosophic Sets to capture hesitation, divergence, and indeterminacy in evaluations. Results: The analysis classified cybersecurity platforms, autonomous orchestration, and sustainability routing as high-priority initiatives, demonstrating stability under uncertainty and alignment with operational and ecological goals. Predictive workforce augmentation and agentic AI communications were assessed as moderate priority, reflecting contextual dependence and variability in expert judgments. Limitations of the investigation: The study focuses exclusively on DHL, limiting generalizability across the logistics sector. Reliance on expert judgments introduces potential bias, and the criteria set reflects DHL priorities rather than evolving conditions. Proprietary data constraints restricted empirical validation, and classification outcomes remain sensitive to threshold selection despite robustness checks. Practical implications: The findings provide DHL and similar operators with a structured framework to selectively scale robust initiatives while cautiously adapting those with weaker stability. The approach supports evidence-based decision-making for digital transformation strategies in logistics under uncertainty. Originality / Value: This research contributes to logistics literature by advancing multi-criteria decision-making through the integration of neutrosophic uncertainty modeling. It demonstrates the applicability of the Extended ELECTRE Tri framework to real-world logistics transformation, offering a replicable model for global operators navigating AI adoption and digital resilience.

title: Assessment of renewable-based clean hydrogen production for transportation in Iran: a multi-city study
summary: Iran is gradually shifting toward clean energy to reduce its dependence on fossil fuels and cut CO₂ emissions. Given the country's large renewable potential, hydrogen produced from these resources is a zero-emission energy carrier and a pro
content: Iran is gradually shifting toward clean energy to reduce its dependence on fossil fuels and cut CO₂ emissions. Given the country's large renewable potential, hydrogen produced from these resources is a zero-emission energy carrier and a promising fuel option for vehicles. This study evaluates the potential of six cities with different climatic conditions to produce up to 120 kg/day of hydrogen from photovoltaic panels and wind turbines, using HOMER Pro for the analysis. The levelised cost of hydrogen (LCOH) is lowest in Kerman and Birjand, at $6.09/kg and $6.10/kg, and highest in Tabriz, at $10.70/kg. Replacing gasoline with this hydrogen in all six cities would avoid a total of about 9183 t of CO₂ over the 25-year project lifetime. These results show that hybrid renewable systems are technically and economically suitable for clean hydrogen production and can help reduce greenhouse gas emissions and fossil fuel dependence in the transport sector.

title: Atomically Precise Platinum Nanocluster Catalysts for Efficient Hydrogen Production via Methylcyclohexane Dehydrogenation
summary: In hydrogen storage technologies with liquid organic hydrogen carriers, the development of efficient catalysts for methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation is highly important. In this study, we developed atomically precise platinum nanocluster ca
content: In hydrogen storage technologies with liquid organic hydrogen carriers, the development of efficient catalysts for methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation is highly important. In this study, we developed atomically precise platinum nanocluster catalysts supported on Al2O3 (Ptx/Al2O3; x = 17, ~51). Comprehensive characterization demonstrated that the catalysts remained highly monodisperse and of uniform particle size (0.86 or 1.15 nm), and maintained a cationic electronic state (Ptδ+) even after thermal treatment. Remarkably, the Pt17/Al2O3 and Pt~51/Al2O3 catalysts exhibited a mass activity up to 7.9 and 8.2 times higher than that of conventional nanoparticle catalysts. Furthermore, by effectively suppressing undesirable cracking pathways at a low operating temperature of 250 °C, the catalyst achieved both high selectivity (byproduct yield < 3%; below the detection limit) and durability. These findings pave the way for practical guidelines in advanced catalyst design.

title: Homogeneous Electrochemical Hydrogenation of 1-Octene with [( iPr PNP)CoCl] and Water
summary: Here we present the electrochemical hydrogenation (ECH) of 1-octene to n -octane using the homogeneous complex [( iPr PNP)CoCl] [CoCl] and water as the source of hydrogen atoms. We showcase how tuning only electrode surface area, as well as
content: Here we present the electrochemical hydrogenation (ECH) of 1-octene to n -octane using the homogeneous complex [( iPr PNP)CoCl] [CoCl] and water as the source of hydrogen atoms. We showcase how tuning only electrode surface area, as well as supporting electrolyte type and concentration can drastically increase the reaction selectivity for ECH over parasitic H 2 evolution from initially 9% to eventually 82% faradaic efficiency, without traditional chemical reaction optimization or catalyst tuning. The ECH process runs via a single electron path of hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) rather than hydride transfer according to quantum chemical calculations. Two consecutive HAT cycles must be completed to hydrogenate one substrate molecule, which renders the process more sensitive to mass transport effects and reaction design than hydride transfer mediated ECH with two electrons transferred in one step. Mechanistically, upon an initial one-electron reduction of [CoCl] , the complex undergoes HAT at one of its benzylic C–H positions to afford a dearomatized ligand structure. A key step of the active ECH cycle is then the oxidative addition of H 2 O to a Co(I) intermediate, affording a fleeting Co(III)-hydroxy-hydride, which immediately undergoes HAT to the substrate, forming a more stable Co(II)–OH species. A proton coupled electron transfer regenerates Co(I) for the next cycle. Using Bu 4 NOH in water as hydrogen atom source proved the resilience towards high pH values and suggests that the process does not rely on high proton activity in the electrolyte.
