Furthermore, its application in a dye-sensitized solar cell resulted in a power conversion efficiency of 1.48%. These results demonstrate that the optimized polymer electrolyte exhibits enhanced photovoltaic efficiency in dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) and high capacitive performance in electric double-layer capacitors (EDLCs), thereby illustrating its dual functionality.

title: Copper Recovery from Metallurgical Slags Using Biomass in the Form of Fruit Seeds/Stones as a Reducing Agent
summary: Civilizational development, which depends on the availability of raw materials, has accelerated tremendously in recent decades. This is due to globalization and the growth of emerging markets. It represents a huge opportunity for an innovat
content: Civilizational development, which depends on the availability of raw materials, has accelerated tremendously in recent decades. This is due to globalization and the growth of emerging markets. It represents a huge opportunity for an innovative approach to both production and consumption. Along with civilizational growth, we also face negative consequences that lead to climate change. To meet the demands regarding climate neutrality, people have started analyzing the possibility of running production processes using substrates that either eliminate or significantly reduce the use of non-renewable resources. Considering the specifics of metal extraction and production, it is important to note that chemistry and thermodynamics play a key role here. This involves, on the one hand, understanding how carbon or its oxides are absorbed, which is essential for plant growth, and on the other, using components of so-called biomass for controlled chemical reactions. These regulations regarding climate neutrality and the type of raw materials are reflected in detail in the relevant European Union directives. Copper production in Poland is a strategic sector of the economy. Considering the scale of production and the consumption of natural resources, developing the possibility of partially replacing them will constitute a process innovation. Research into copper recovery from slag to date has focused primarily on improving the efficiency of the slag reduction process by intensifying bath mixing and improving the mass transfer process in the liquid phase. Given that biomass contains a significant proportion of volatile matter, this may additionally have a beneficial impact on the efficiency of using this type of material in the process. Many parameters still need to be investigated before the obtained results can be tested on a larger scale, enabling transfer to industrial conditions. The study presented the results of research on the potential use of biomass to reduce secondary raw materials coming from the copper industry. A Gibbs free enthalpy analysis was carried out for possible chemical reactions and their likelihood of occurring. As a source of metals, a material similar in composition to slag generated in the copper industry was used. Considering that copper ores contain about 1 wt. %, it makes even more sense to use secondary slag, which contains up to 10 wt. % copper. As part of the work, tests of the pyrometallurgic slag reduction process were carried out with the use of selected types of biomass. The tests were carried out in a metallurgical aggregate, at a temperature of 1300 °C in the time range from 1 to 5 h. The main parameters determining the efficiency of the process were to determine the degree of removal of the main metals, i.e., Cu and Pb, as well as to determine the content of these elements in the secondary slag. Verification of the possibility of replacing coal with biomass in real industrial conditions requires verifying primarily the e

title: Circularity measures enhance resilience of net zero pathways for agriculture
summary: Abstract Reducing environmental impact of agriculture is paramount for sustainable food production. Development of a circular bioeconomy can contribute to environmental objectives, yet the interaction of circularity measures with net zero s
content: Abstract Reducing environmental impact of agriculture is paramount for sustainable food production. Development of a circular bioeconomy can contribute to environmental objectives, yet the interaction of circularity measures with net zero strategies is poorly understood. Using integrated modelling and 12 key performance indicators, we assess the sustainability and resilience of two simulated circular strategies implemented within a business as usual and three net zero greenhouse gas emission pathways for Ireland’s land sector. Two circularity strategies were designed: Energy-focused circularity maximised domestic feedstock utilisation for bioenergy production via anaerobic digestion. Feed-focused circularity minimised imported (overseas) inputs to national livestock systems. Net zero requires large-scale transformation across the land sector. Circularity moderately enhances greenhouse gas emission reductions through energy and livestock feed substitution but considerably strengthens the resilience of net zero pathways by lowering dependence on imported fertilisers, feeds and/or energy (depending on the circularity strategy). This work highlights opportunities to embed circularity within net zero land use strategies to improve resilience.

title: Resource-efficient use of industrial residue for multifunctional cacao nanofibers
summary: This study evaluates cacao residue from chocolate production for resource-efficient production of multifunctional nanofibers. The underlying hypothesis is that preserving non-cellulosic constituents during processing can enable resource-eff
content: This study evaluates cacao residue from chocolate production for resource-efficient production of multifunctional nanofibers. The underlying hypothesis is that preserving non-cellulosic constituents during processing can enable resource-efficient nanofiber production while contributing unique functionalities. Cacao residue yielded 30% after bleaching, with the main components being fat and holocellulose. Fibrillation produced cacao nanofibers at an energy demand of 3.9 kWh/kg, compared with the reference, a commercial wood pulp, with 8.2 kWh/kg after the same processing time. The cacao nanofibers displayed bioactivity, hydrophobic behavior, and excellent redispersibility not observed for the reference material, which has cellulose as the main component. The bioactivity of cacao nanofibers included strong antioxidant, mild antibacterial, and moderate anti-collagenase activity. Utilization of the natural composition offers a resource-efficient approach to unlock the potential of cacao residue into specific multifunctional nanofibers with potential for further development of coating, cosmeceutical, and biomedical applications.

title: Evaluating the global economy-wide impact of energy efficiency policies in buildings
summary: The building sector accounts for nearly one-third of global final energy use. A range of energy efficiency policies can help reduce energy consumption in the sector. These policies include building energy codes, which improve energy efficie
content: The building sector accounts for nearly one-third of global final energy use. A range of energy efficiency policies can help reduce energy consumption in the sector. These policies include building energy codes, which improve energy efficiency in new buildings, as well as retrofit programs and whole-building performance standards, which address efficiency of existing buildings. In this study, we use the Global Change Analysis Model to assess the impacts of these policies on building energy use and other key outcomes globally and across regions. Additionally, we explore how compliance rates influence policy effectiveness and examine the interactions between building efficiency policies, socioeconomic development, and related policy issues. Our study shows that energy demand from the building sector will rise significantly through 2050, absent policies. Socioeconomic development and population gains will be the dominant contributors to this growth. The sector’s energy use could be considerably reduced by implementing effective building efficiency policies. We find that universal adoption and high compliance of advanced building efficiency policies could reduce building energy use by approximately 44% by 2050. Low policy compliance, however, could reduce their effectiveness by nearly half. Furthermore, the impacts of these policies vary by region. Our study indicates that emerging economies in South Asia and Africa would benefit the most from policies targeting new buildings, with gross savings at nearly 1% of GDP in 2050. Meanwhile, China and countries in Europe and North America would benefit the most from a combination of policies addressing both new and existing buildings.

title: Reconciling the role of clay mineral formation on net alkalinity generation during rock weathering: Insights from reactive transport models of shale, granite, and basalt
summary: Abstract. Clay minerals, while ubiquitous in soil, have wide-ranging and countervailing impacts on global biogeochemical cycles. Their compositional diversity makes predicting their formation conditions and impacts on soil solution chemistr
content: Abstract. Clay minerals, while ubiquitous in soil, have wide-ranging and countervailing impacts on global biogeochemical cycles. Their compositional diversity makes predicting their formation conditions and impacts on soil solution chemistry a grand challenge. In this proof of concept study, we unpack the influence of clay mineral formation on alkalinity generation during rock weathering: a key process regulating atmospheric CO2 levels over geologic time. Because they remove aqueous Si and Al from solution during formation, clay minerals may enhance silicate mineral dissolution and thereby enhance alkalinity generation. However, clays can also offset the alkalinity produced during silicate dissolution by generating acidity when they form. To identify whether, or to what extent, clay minerals enhance alkalinity generation, we employ reactive transport models of idealized granite, basalt, and shale weathering over a range of environmental conditions. Clay mineral formation typically increases net alkalinity generation by enabling greater silicate dissolution. This enhancement is most pronounced at low fluid flow rates and low soil CO2 concentrations when thermodynamic conditions require clays for continued silicate dissolution and sustained alkalinity generation. However, clay-enhanced alkalinity generation diminishes at low erosion rates when primary mineral supply decreases; in less common instances where chlorite forms, clay formation can lead to a net alkalinity consumption. Overall, clay minerals promote CO2 drawdown and modify the silicate weathering feedback.

title: Renewable water treatment using electrodialysis for hydrogen production
summary: Hydrogen production in arid and semi-arid regions is constrained by water availability and groundwater quality. This study presents a proof of concept treatment integrating alkaline softening and electrodialysis (ED) to condition real brack
content: Hydrogen production in arid and semi-arid regions is constrained by water availability and groundwater quality. This study presents a proof of concept treatment integrating alkaline softening and electrodialysis (ED) to condition real brackish groundwater for hydrogen production. ED is particularly attractive for waters with low or moderate salinity, as it provides an alternative to conventional reverse osmosis that operates at low pressure while enabling progressive deionization. Real brackish groundwater from Castilla La Mancha, Spain, characterized by high mineralization and a complex ionic composition, was used to evaluate the treatment. Alkaline softening achieved complete Mg removal and approximately 80% Ca removal, reducing divalent ions responsible for mineral scaling while recovering CaCO 3 and Mg(OH) 2 as potentially valuable mineral products. Subsequent ED decreased groundwater conductivity from 10,520 to approximately 1060 μS/cm within 90 min, corresponding to nearly 90% conductivity reduction. At this stage, sulfate, chloride and conductivity complied with the physicochemical criteria considered under Spanish drinking water regulations. Further ED reduced conductivity to approximately 6 μS/cm, demonstrating that the same treatment can progressively achieve different water quality targets, from conditions compatible with drinking water criteria to highly deionized water suitable for electrolysis. The treated water was subsequently validated in both alkaline water electrolysis (AWE) and proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzers, showing polarization performance comparable to commercial ultrapure water. These results demonstrate the technical feasibility of treatment using ED to integrate brackish groundwater desalination, mineral resource recovery and water conditioning for decentralized hydrogen production. • Electrodialysis effectively removed sulfate, nitrate and chloride from real brackish groundwater. • Softening improved ion transport while recovering CaCO 3 and Mg(OH) 2 mineral products. • Nearly 90% conductivity reduction yielded water meeting drinking water quality criteria. • Further electrodialysis reduced conductivity to approximately 6 μS/cm. • Treated water performed comparably to ultrapure water in PEM and AWE electrolyzers.

title: Laboratories in global politics: Towards technopolitical histories of security
summary: Abstract Contemporary security governance increasingly relies on science and technology, yet little attention has been paid to how their place in security has been historically constituted and continues to shape security practices. High-con
content: Abstract Contemporary security governance increasingly relies on science and technology, yet little attention has been paid to how their place in security has been historically constituted and continues to shape security practices. High-containment laboratories working with dangerous pathogens exemplify this puzzle: while expert debates have focused on governing these dual-use technologies, they often overlook the historical conditions that enabled their global expansion and continue to affect the insecurities these laboratories generate. This article examines how the rise of high-security laboratories has been intertwined with changing understandings of biological threats and approaches to governing them. Bringing together research on technopolitics, global history, and security studies, the paper develops technopolitical histories of security , an analytical framework for the historical study of technoscientific systems in security politics. The framework examines how security rationalities are materialized in scientific practices and technologies, how these arrangements are constituted through global connections and power asymmetries, and how they prefigure subsequent approaches to security. Empirically, the article traces high-security laboratories across three technopolitical arrangements: biological warfare, biological defence, and biological preparedness. It shows how pathogen research mobilized for past security projects laid the structural foundations for contemporary biological security governance, making visible the enduring political effects of technoscientific systems.

title: Probabilistic evaluation of climate impact and life cycle cost of geotechnical designs
source: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Engineering Sustainability
summary: Sustainability considerations are becoming increasingly important in geotechnical engineering, driven by climate legislation and sustainability goals. Life cycle assessment (LCA) and life cycle cost analysis (LCCA) are commonly applied to e
content: Sustainability considerations are becoming increasingly important in geotechnical engineering, driven by climate legislation and sustainability goals. Life cycle assessment (LCA) and life cycle cost analysis (LCCA) are commonly applied to evaluate environmental impacts and life cycle costs (LCC) of geotechnical design alternatives. However, uncertainties exist in life cycle inventory parameters, and a structured framework for incorporating these uncertainties into LCA and LCCA when comparing geotechnical design alternatives is currently lacking. This paper proposes a methodology in which input parameters are modelled as stochastic variables within the planning and decision making processes to identify geotechnical design alternatives with the lowest potential life cycle impact. Specifically, the methodology models uncertainties in material quantities, emission factors, unit costs, and monetisation parameters; combines LCA and LCCA results into a single decision-support metric using weighting factors; and provides a probabilistic evaluation for decision making by quantifying the probability of selecting a suboptimal design alternative. The methodology is illustrated by comparing the climate impact and LCC of two railway embankment design alternatives using Monte Carlo simulations: piled embankment and excavation and fill.

title: Geothermal reservoir characteristics, genesis, and potential in the Sanjiaochenggou area, Jinchang Depression
summary: Medium- to low-temperature geothermal resources hosted in sedimentary basins are important for regional heating and direct utilization. This study investigates the geothermal reservoir characteristics, fluid origin, genesis, and development
content: Medium- to low-temperature geothermal resources hosted in sedimentary basins are important for regional heating and direct utilization. This study investigates the geothermal reservoir characteristics, fluid origin, genesis, and development potential of the Sanjiaochenggou area in the Jinchang Depression, a poorly explored inland sedimentary basin in the eastern Hexi Corridor. An integrated investigation was conducted using hydrogeological surveys, wide-field electromagnetic and controlled-source audio-frequency magnetotelluric surveys, geothermal drilling, comprehensive well logging, borehole temperature measurements, pumping tests, hydrochemical analyses, and environmental isotope techniques. The results indicate a confined sedimentary-basin geothermal system, with the principal reservoirs hosted in sandstone and sandy conglomerate of the Lower Neogene and Cretaceous strata beneath a relatively impermeable Neogene mudstone caprock. The temperature reaches 61.7 °C at 1,992 m, with an average geothermal gradient of approximately 1.77 °C/100 m. Pumping-test analyses yielded a representative transmissivity of 21.69 m 2 /day. The geothermal fluid is Cl–Na-type brine with an average total dissolved solids concentration of 40.99 g/L. Isotopic evidence indicates meteoric recharge followed by deep circulation, prolonged water–rock interaction, and long residence within a relatively closed hydrogeological system. For the 47.02 km 2 assessment area, the reference heat-in-place estimate is 2.27 × 10 18 J, while deterministic scenarios yield 8.84 × 10 17 –2.86 × 10 18 J. By cross-validating geophysical interpretations against the JCDR-1 borehole and separating borehole-controlled from inferred resources, this study establishes a site-specific conceptual model and deterministic uncertainty framework for evaluating comparable inland sedimentary-basin geothermal systems with limited deep-borehole control.

title: Empowering student-led climate solutions: the role of AI in STEAM education
summary: This convergent mixed-methods study investigates the strategic integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into a university-level STEAM curriculum to empower students to design climate solutions. Combining quantitative survey data from 69
content: This convergent mixed-methods study investigates the strategic integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into a university-level STEAM curriculum to empower students to design climate solutions. Combining quantitative survey data from 69 undergraduate students selected via a complete cohort census sampling approach (response rate: 84.1%) and multi-tiered purposive qualitative interviews with N = 25 participants ( N = 11 experts, N = 9 faculty members, and N = 5 student innovators), the findings indicate high technological familiarity and widespread adoption (100% AI tool use). Specifically, students reported the highest agreement for AI enhancing their creativity and learning independence (86.9%, M = 4.12), supporting their capacity to pivot from data collection to strategic solution design (73.9%, M = 3.78), and bolstering their perceived empowerment to propose climate solutions (76.8%, M = 3.84). Furthermore, self-reported student perceptions indicated that AI supported their critical thinking process (68.1%, M = 3.65), representing perceived cognitive scaffolding rather than an objective measure of skill performance. This supports the qualitative finding that AI acts as a “Complexity Mediator” in climate tasks. However, notable concerns were reported regarding accuracy (60.9%) and plagiarism (59.4%). To address this, the study proposes the AI-Empowered STEAM Climate Action Model (AISC-AM), a conceptual framework that structures STEAM as a Multi-Scalar Problem-Solving Ecosystem and mandates critical AI literacy and an “AI-in-the-Loop” validation structure. Informed by preliminary stakeholder appraisal, the proposed AISC-AM offers a structured pedagogical workflow to mitigate operational risks while connecting student-led research to regional climate policy platforms via youth organizational partnerships.

title: DFT-guided engineering of halide perovskite quantum dots: From excited-state dynamics and defect chemistry to predictive materials discovery
summary: Halide perovskite quantum dots (HPQDs) have emerged as promising materials for next-generation optoelectronic technologies, yet achieving simultaneously high efficiency, stability, and controllable functionality requires a deeper understand
content: Halide perovskite quantum dots (HPQDs) have emerged as promising materials for next-generation optoelectronic technologies, yet achieving simultaneously high efficiency, stability, and controllable functionality requires a deeper understanding of their atomic-scale mechanisms. This review highlights how density functional theory (DFT) and its advanced extensions have transformed the rational engineering of HPQDs from empirical optimization toward mechanism-driven design. Time-dependent DFT and nonadiabatic molecular dynamics approaches are discussed for elucidating excited-state evolution, carrier relaxation, charge separation, recombination dynamics, and electron–phonon interactions. The role of DFT in revealing defect chemistry, vacancy-dependent trap formation, dopant stability, and composition-driven band engineering is examined, emphasizing the importance of surface environments and dynamic structural effects in nanoscale systems. Recent advances in DFT-guided surface passivation, heterostructure engineering, and molecular interface design are reviewed through their demonstrated impact on optical performance and device stability. Remaining challenges, including model–experiment discrepancies, computational scaling, and accurate treatment of dynamic surfaces, is analyzed. Finally, emerging strategies integrating machine-learning potentials, high-throughput screening, and atomic-resolution characterization are discussed as pathways toward predictive materials discovery and accelerated development of advanced HPQD-based optoelectronic devices.

title: Spatial perspective on perceived fairness of climate-related fuel tax increases
summary: We explore the perceived fairness of fuel tax increases from a spatial perspective. Actions in transport sector are needed to meet climate change mitigation targets, but such policies may disproportionately impact rural and urban residents,
content: We explore the perceived fairness of fuel tax increases from a spatial perspective. Actions in transport sector are needed to meet climate change mitigation targets, but such policies may disproportionately impact rural and urban residents, leading to spatially varying experiences of injustice. Perceived fairness is the most important determinant of public opinion towards mitigation policies, but perceived fairness of these policies itself has been understudied. We combine our inquiry of perceived fairness regarding fuel tax increases with considerations of spatial justice. We explore, whether residential area type, region, and variables such as climate concern, trust in climate policies, political orientation and use of fossil-fuelled car, are associated with perceived fairness of increasing fuel tax, and whether there are regional differences in these variables. Data were collected via a survey in June 2022 in three regions with different characteristics in Finland: Helsinki, Finland Proper, and Northern Ostrobothnia. Our results reveal that residents in rural areas and sparsely populated regions perceive fuel tax increases as less fair. Climate concern, trust and political orientation were found to influence fairness perceptions. Moreover, climate concern and trust were lower in sparsely populated regions. Considerations of fairness perceptions are important for successful climate mitigation policy.

title: Constraint-Aware Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient for Energy Management of Fuel Cell Hybrid Tramways
summary: Fuel cell hybrid trams combine high energy density with zero tailpipe emissions, making them relevant to carbon-peaking and carbon-neutrality goals in urban rail. Traditional energy management methods rely on fixed rules or accurate system
content: Fuel cell hybrid trams combine high energy density with zero tailpipe emissions, making them relevant to carbon-peaking and carbon-neutrality goals in urban rail. Traditional energy management methods rely on fixed rules or accurate system models, limiting their adaptability to changing traction demands and multiple operating constraints. This paper develops a constraint-aware TD3-based energy management system (CTD3 EMS) for coordinating the fuel cell, battery, and supercapacitor as traction demand changes. The system model includes source dynamics, conversion losses, traction loads, and SOC limits. CTD3 extends conventional TD3 by using a Lagrangian mechanism to handle operating constraints and a reward function that accounts for hydrogen consumption, power balance, and energy-storage stress. Simulations on representative urban routes show that CTD3 reaches a stable return sooner and exhibits less fluctuation during training than conventional TD3 and fixed strategies. Compared with the benchmark strategy, CTD3 reduces fuel-cell power fluctuations by 35% and records lower direct hydrogen consumption. Direct consumption is also below conventional TD3.Hydrogen consumption is also 24.8% lower than that achieved by conventional TD3. The findings highlight that CTD3 enhances both energy utilization and energy storage stability, providing a robust approach for intelligent control and practical deployment in fuel cell hybrid trams.

title: SolarEV Cities for deep urban decarbonization: A critical review of integration gaps and transition pathways
summary: Urban decarbonization is essential for meeting global climate goals; however, progress toward integrated low-carbon urban energy systems remains inadequately slow. The SolarEV City Concept integrates rooftop photovoltaic (PV) generation wit
content: Urban decarbonization is essential for meeting global climate goals; however, progress toward integrated low-carbon urban energy systems remains inadequately slow. The SolarEV City Concept integrates rooftop photovoltaic (PV) generation with electric vehicles (EVs) as city-scale distributed mobile energy storage, using EV batteries to increase the value and flexibility of urban rooftop PV. Modeling studies suggest that high-penetration PV+EV systems could supply 60–95% of municipal electricity demand under scenarios aligned with future sustainable-city development, but real-world integration remains limited. Despite rapid worldwide growth of both PV and EV markets, bidirectional Vehicle-to-Home/Building (V2H/V2B) and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) applications have advanced unevenly, revealing a persistent PV-EV integration gap. This critical integrative review analyzes this gap using a socio-techno-economic framework encompassing six interdependent dimensions: climate, urban structure, technology, economics, policy, and society, across nine countries: Australia, China, France, India, Indonesia, Japan, the Netherlands, South Korea, and the United States. Cross-national comparison shows that implementation is constrained by fragmented bidirectional-charging standards, immature value-stacking and compensation models, distribution-grid and market-access constraints, regulatory separation between energy and transport sectors, and equity barriers that disproportionately limit access for renters, apartment residents, and lower-income households. Five transition-pathway archetypes, ranging from Japan’s resilience-driven V2H pathway to regulation-enabled commercial V2G pathways in France and the Netherlands, demonstrate that SolarEV Cities require a transition from parallel PV and EV promotion toward shared urban-energy visions, interoperable digital infrastructure, feeder-aware planning, inclusive market designs, and multi-stakeholder implementation platforms that convert rapid PV and EV innovation into scalable, resilient, and socially inclusive urban decarbonization.

title: Water-scarcity footprints of industrial hydrogen production under Vietnam’s power-sector transition plan
summary: Hydrogen can support industrial decarbonization, but its expansion may transfer environmental pressure to freshwater systems, where production in developing countries coincides with regional water scarcity. This study quantified the volumet
content: Hydrogen can support industrial decarbonization, but its expansion may transfer environmental pressure to freshwater systems, where production in developing countries coincides with regional water scarcity. This study quantified the volumetric and scarcity-weighted blue-water implications of industrial hydrogen production under Vietnam's 2030 and 2050 power-sector transition scenarios. A cradle-to-gate water-footprint inventory was combined with region-specific Available Water Remaining (AWARE) characterization factors to compare wind-powered hydrogen (WPH), photovoltaic hydrogen (PVH), and coal-based hydrogen (CTH) under mutually exclusive deployment scenarios using the upper bounds of the production ranges as scenario-scale assumptions. Under the scenarios, WPH had the lowest national water consumption (WC) and hydrogen water-scarcity footprint (HWSF) in both years: 18.20 million m 3 and 39.60 million m 3 eq in 2030, and 728.00 million m 3 and 1648.13 million m 3 eq in 2050. In 2030, CTH had a lower HWSF than PVH (65.92 versus 68.51 million m 3 eq) despite having the highest WC (34.02 million m 3 ). In 2050, CTH had the highest HWSF (2340.31 million m 3 eq), whereas PVH had the highest WC (1333.00 million m 3 ). Rankings depended on the indicator used: in 2050, CTH had the unweighted grid-referenced system-scale comparative potential (1476.02 million m 3 ), whereas WPH had the highest scarcity-adjusted grid-referenced potential (3579.90 million m 3 eq). Water-aware reallocation reduced national HWSF by 17.7-42.5% but increased regional HWSF in the Southern region. These results indicate that technology choice, deployment scale, power-system structure, and spatial allocation shape hydrogen-related water outcomes. Hydrogen siting and power-sector planning should incorporate spatial water-scarcity screening and explicitly evaluate regional burden shifting. • WPH minimized national water consumption and HWSF in both scenarios. • CTH HWSF was below PVH in 2030 but highest by 2050. • CTH led the unweighted grid-referenced system-scale potential; WPH led the scarcity-adjusted grid-referenced potential. • Water-aware allocation cut national HWSF by 17.7-42.5%. • Spatial scarcity screening improves industrial hydrogen location.

title: Economic Profitability of ESG Investments in the Wine Sector: A Bibliometric Systematic Literature Review
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines whether and under which conditions ESG investments are associated with profitability in the wine sector. A PRISMA‐guided bibliometric–systematic review of 83 peer‐reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science
content: ABSTRACT This study examines whether and under which conditions ESG investments are associated with profitability in the wine sector. A PRISMA‐guided bibliometric–systematic review of 83 peer‐reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science combines bibliometric mapping, qualitative synthesis, and MMAT‐based quality appraisal. ESG investments do not generate uniform returns. Profitability emerges when firms transform sustainability investments into organizational capabilities and stakeholders recognize and reward the resulting value, a process shaped by internal, external, and temporal boundary conditions. Wineries should tailor ESG strategies to their capabilities, market context, and time horizon, while policy support should address sector‐specific structural barriers. Integrating the Natural Resource‐Based View and Stakeholder Theory, the study proposes a unified framework explaining heterogeneous ESG–profitability outcomes. However, the evidence base is predominantly environmental, limiting conclusions for social and governance dimensions.

title: Toward Climate Change Resilience and the Carbon‐Neutral Transition in Emerging Economies Through Circular Technologies and Green Energy Transmission Systems
summary: ABSTRACT Despite growing evidence on the environmental benefits of green innovation, empirical findings for emerging economies remain limited and inconclusive, particularly regarding the joint role of environmental patents and renewable ene
content: ABSTRACT Despite growing evidence on the environmental benefits of green innovation, empirical findings for emerging economies remain limited and inconclusive, particularly regarding the joint role of environmental patents and renewable energy in reducing carbon emissions. Given the rapid economic growth of these countries, it is important to understand how environmental patents and climate change mitigation technologies influence sustainable economic growth in emerging markets. Using robust heterogeneous panel estimation methods that account for cross‐sectional dependence, the results consistently show that green innovation, measured by environmental patents, and renewable energy support the carbon‐neutral transition by reducing carbon emissions in emerging economies. The findings demonstrate that while green innovations significantly reduce emissions, the emissions‐reducing impact of renewable energy adoption is quantitatively larger. In contrast, energy consumption remains an important contributor to emissions. Overall, the study highlights that promoting green innovation together with renewable energy adoption is important for supporting long‐term environmental sustainability and the transition to carbon neutrality in emerging economies.

title: Extended fractional Hofstadter states at high field in twisted bilayer graphene above the magic angle
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
summary: When a Chern band is partially filled, a fractional Chern insulator (FCI)—the lattice analog of a fractional quantum Hall state—can arise. Though the full range of possible scenarios for producing such a state is not established, the most t
content: When a Chern band is partially filled, a fractional Chern insulator (FCI)—the lattice analog of a fractional quantum Hall state—can arise. Though the full range of possible scenarios for producing such a state is not established, the most tractable models combine strong electronic interactions with the quantum geometry of the parent Chern band meeting specific criteria. In twisted bilayer graphene, the importance of interactions can be tuned by varying the interlayer twist. Here, we study a sample with twist near 1.4 ° , large enough to suppress the zero-field correlated states. We find that applying a strong magnetic field restores the importance of electron–electron interactions: at nearly half a magnetic flux quantum per moiré unit cell, deep in the Hofstadter regime, odd-denominator fractional states appear in multiple Hofstadter subbands. These fractional states persist over larger ranges of density, and are more robustly quantized, than nearby integer states, opposite to what is seen in other fractional quantum Hall and FCI systems.

title: Merkez Bankacılığında Paradigma Değişimi: Yeşil Para Politikası Uygulamaları ve ECB, BOE, TCMB Karşılaştırması
source: İnönü University International Journal of Social Sciences (INIJOSS)
summary: İklim değişikliği, merkez bankalarının geleneksel fiyat ve finansal istikrar görevlerini yeniden tanımlamasını gerektiren köklü bir dönüşüme yol açmıştır. Bu çalışma, merkez bankacılığındaki paradigma değişimini yasal yetki alanları, varlık
content: İklim değişikliği, merkez bankalarının geleneksel fiyat ve finansal istikrar görevlerini yeniden tanımlamasını gerektiren köklü bir dönüşüme yol açmıştır. Bu çalışma, merkez bankacılığındaki paradigma değişimini yasal yetki alanları, varlık alım programları, teminat çerçeveleri ve seçici kredi mekanizmaları olmak üzere dört operasyonel gösterge üzerinden Avrupa Merkez Bankası (ECB), İngiltere Merkez Bankası (BoE) ve Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankası (TCMB) örnekleriyle karşılaştırmalı olarak incelemektedir. Yöntem olarak literatür taraması ve kavramsal sentez kullanılmıştır. Politika metinleri ve ampirik literatür incelendiğinde, gelişmiş ülke merkez bankaları ECB ve BoE’nin iklim risklerini başlangıçta finansal sistemi koruma odaklı savunmacı bir yaklaşımla ele aldığı; iklim stres testleri, ÇSY raporlama standartları ve varlık alımlarının yeşil eğilmesiyle sistemik riski azaltmayı hedefledikleri görülmüştür. 2021’den itibaren ise yasal yetki genişlemeleriyle bu bankaların yeşil dönüşümü aktif destekleyen daha ilerlemeci bir role evrildiği tespit edilmiştir. Sonuç olarak çalışma, merkez bankalarının iklim politikası tutumlarının ekonomik gelişmişlik düzeyi ve ulusal yapısal kısıtlara göre farklılaştığını ortaya koyarak literatüre katkı sunmaktadır.

title: Strength and environmental benchmarking of waste-derived activators in fly ash-slag alkali-activated concrete: A systematic and quantitative assessment
summary: Commercial sodium silicate (CSS) remains a widely used activator in alkali-activated concrete (AAC), but its production can substantially contribute to the embodied environmental impacts of AAC. Although waste-derived activators (WDAs) synt
content: Commercial sodium silicate (CSS) remains a widely used activator in alkali-activated concrete (AAC), but its production can substantially contribute to the embodied environmental impacts of AAC. Although waste-derived activators (WDAs) synthesized from silica-rich wastes have received increasing attention, comparative evidence linking their mechanical performance, environmental impacts, eco-efficiency and low-carbon procurement potential remains limited. This study addresses this gap through a quantitative and environmental benchmarking assessment of CSS, sole WDA (SWDA) and hybrid WDA (HWDA) systems used in fly ash-slag AACs. A database of 40 AAC formulations from 20 studies was compiled. Life cycle assessment was combined with dataset-level statistical comparisons, strength-normalized environmental indicators, sustainability ranking, Pareto analysis and procurement-oriented benchmarking to establish an integrated framework for evaluating WDA technologies. The compiled WDA formulations achieved compressive strengths comparable to CSS formulations, indicating that selected waste-derived systems can achieve compressive strengths within the investigated structural-grade range. Simultaneously, the WDA systems reduced average global warming potential (GWP) by approximately 34% relative to CSS (95% CI: 19–49%) and exhibited lower GWP per unit compressive strength. Activator production remained the dominant environmental hotspot, contributing 75–82% of total GWP. Thermochemically synthesized waste glass (WGP-TMC) activators exhibited favorable strength-GWP trade-offs within the defined assessment framework, with the identified Pareto frontier consisting exclusively of SWDA formulations. Furthermore, several SWDA and HWDA formulations attained Market Beating embodied carbon classifications under the Low Carbon Concrete Group framework. The findings therefore indicate that selected WDA systems, especially WGP-TMC-based formulations, have promising potential for lower-carbon AAC production.

title: Rule of law and ecological footprint: The mediating roles of human capital and financial development in OECD and non-OECD countries
summary: The aim of this research is to examine the effect of the rule of law on the ecological footprint within the framework of the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) model extended to 67 economies, 26 of which are OECD members and 41 non-members,
content: The aim of this research is to examine the effect of the rule of law on the ecological footprint within the framework of the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) model extended to 67 economies, 26 of which are OECD members and 41 non-members, during 1996–2021. Feasible Generalized Least Squares (FGLS) and System Generalized Method of Moments (SYS-GMM) regressions are used, along with mediating regressions, to assess the role of human capital and financial development. The results support the EKC hypothesis, with the rule of law and natural resource income having a positive effect on the ecological footprint. The transition to renewable energy reduces the ecological footprint, while oil prices have a negative effect in OECD economies. The effect of large urban agglomerations on the ecological footprint is inconclusive. The effect of the rule of law on the ecological footprint is more pronounced in OECD economies. The mediation analysis shows that human capital and financial development act as transmission channels, with differences in the direction of the human capital effect between the two groups of economies. The main results are robust against alternative measures and different subsamples and subperiods. Policymakers promoting the strengthening of the rule of law should incorporate environmental objectives, while the development of human capital and the financial system should be geared toward activities compatible with environmental sustainability. Furthermore, the transition to renewable energy sources must be accelerated to reduce dependence on fossil fuel-intensive activities and curb pressure on the environment.

title: Agriculture, institutions, and ecological pressure in South Asian countries
summary: South Asian countries face rising ecological pressure linked to demographic change, economic growth, agricultural transformation, and uneven institutional capacity. This study examines how food production, agricultural value added, crop yie
content: South Asian countries face rising ecological pressure linked to demographic change, economic growth, agricultural transformation, and uneven institutional capacity. This study examines how food production, agricultural value added, crop yield, carbon intensity, government effectiveness, rule of law, economic development, and population are associated with ecological footprint per capita in Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka over 2000–2024 within an extended STIRPAT framework. The analysis uses cross-sectional dependence and slope-heterogeneity tests, panel unit-root and cointegration procedures, fixed-effects models, heterogeneous long-run estimators, quantile regression, and robustness checks. The results show that food production, agricultural value added, carbon intensity, and economic development are positively associated with ecological footprint in the benchmark models, while population is negatively associated with it. Crop yield and rule of law do not show stable significant associations in the main specifications. In the long-run estimators, carbon intensity remains the most consistent positive correlate of ecological pressure, while government effectiveness shows a negative association in the AMG model. Overall, ecological pressure in South Asia is most consistently associated with carbon-intensive development, whereas agricultural and institutional effects are more sensitive to specification.

title: Taking responsibility for the environmental impact of medical societies
summary: It is well recognised that modern healthcare has an enormous carbon footprint that is contributing to the climate crisis. However, the contribution of medical societies and their associated activities is largely ignored. The Australian and
content: It is well recognised that modern healthcare has an enormous carbon footprint that is contributing to the climate crisis. However, the contribution of medical societies and their associated activities is largely ignored. The Australian and New Zealand Society of Nephrology and its Environmental Sustainability Committee (ESC) are taking action to mitigate their impact on climate change. This viewpoint describes actions taken since the formation of the ESC in 2017 and serves as encouragement for all medical societies to incorporate environmental sustainability into their everyday practice.

title: Construction of Nuclear Power Plants in Kazakhstan: Economic, Environmental and Scientific Implications
summary: This article reveals the main goals of international experience in nuclear power plant (NPP) construction, analyses of benefits and risks that NPP operations may have on the economy and the development of a country’s scientific potential an
content: This article reveals the main goals of international experience in nuclear power plant (NPP) construction, analyses of benefits and risks that NPP operations may have on the economy and the development of a country’s scientific potential and examines annual report data. The article’s methodological approach examines the full range of opportunities and prospects not only in energy production but also in the development of new technologies, medicine, environmental protection, and promotion of scientific and technological progress. The originality and value of the article analyze the economic, environmental, and social aspects of NPP construction, focusing on safety, greenhouse gas emissions, includes NPV analysis to assess the investment attractiveness, as well as institutional risks, potential advantages and comparative analysis of the RK electricity development scenarios. The article finds out that nuclear energy contributes to increased national energy security, creation of hightech companies which are involved into the energy research, creation and providing people with working places, as well as the development of start-ups.

title: Decarbonisation under cap-and-trade: an integrated network Data Envelopment Analysis model with a second-scoring auction mechanism
source: Journal of the Operational Research Society
summary: This study develops a centralised Network Data Envelopment Analysis (NDEA) model within a Directional Distance Function (DDF) framework and integrates it with a second-scoring auction mechanism for carbon permit reallocation under a cap-and
content: This study develops a centralised Network Data Envelopment Analysis (NDEA) model within a Directional Distance Function (DDF) framework and integrates it with a second-scoring auction mechanism for carbon permit reallocation under a cap-and-trade system. The model evaluates the performance of Decision-Making Units (DMUs) within a two-stage network structure and determines surplus and deficit volumes of CO2 permits. An endogenous scarcity-based pricing framework is then introduced to link carbon permit prices to the permit shortages and surpluses derived from the model. Subsequently, a second-scoring auction mechanism determines endogenous transaction prices and trading volumes through bilateral permit exchanges. The proposed framework is applied to the European bioenergy supply chain to investigate whether the mechanism can facilitate permit reallocation and reduce the inefficiency of participating DMUs.

title: A Control Strategy With Hybrid Compressor Modeling for Electric Vehicle CO 2 Heat Pump Systems
summary: ABSTRACT To address the significant range attenuation of electric vehicles in cold climates, this study proposes a simulation and optimization framework for a transcritical CO 2 heat pump system. Given the computational inaccuracies of trad
content: ABSTRACT To address the significant range attenuation of electric vehicles in cold climates, this study proposes a simulation and optimization framework for a transcritical CO 2 heat pump system. Given the computational inaccuracies of traditional polynomial models in characterizing compressor performance under supercritical conditions, a hybrid compressor sub‐model is developed. This sub‐model integrates a physical foundation with a Particle Swarm Optimization‐Back Propagation (PSO‐BP) neural network to accurately predict mass flow rate and power consumption, achieving a mass‐flow‐rate MAPE within 1.5% on the testing set, with power consumption errors within 0.5%–3.89% and mass flow rate errors within 0.5%–4.71% over the full operating envelope. This high‐accuracy compressor model is then embedded within a system‐level physical model built in MATLAB/Simscape. Based on this enhanced simulation platform, a Phased Variable PTC Cooperative Control Strategy is proposed to resolve the conflict between rapid heating and energy efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate that at −25°C, the proposed strategy reduces cabin warm‐up time by 57.1% compared with the pure heat pump mode while achieving an average COP of 1.776 over the entire warm‐up process, representing a 77.6% improvement in COP compared with conventional pure PTC heating (COP = 1.000). The research demonstrates that enhancing critical component modeling with data‐driven techniques can effectively support the development of precise, energy‐efficient thermal management strategies for EVs.

title: CRISPR‐Cas Tools for Dissecting and Engineering Environmental Responses in Microalgae
summary: conditions, yet their complex regulatory networks have made relevant engineering difficult. Clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-CRISPR-associated proteins (Cas) have changed the situation, shifting microalgal
content: conditions, yet their complex regulatory networks have made relevant engineering difficult. Clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-CRISPR-associated proteins (Cas) have changed the situation, shifting microalgal research from random transgene integration toward precise editing of the genes that mediate photosynthesis, stress responses and environmental acclimation. This work reviews how CRISPR-Cas has been applied across microalgal lineages to (i) dissect genes involved in stress response and photosynthesis, (ii) streamline genomes through large-scale deletions, (iii) build stress-tolerant chassis that retain photosynthetic performance under unsatisfactory conditions and (iv) reprogramme lipid, pigment and high-value compound pathways. We then discuss the determinants of editing efficiency, including single-guide RNA design, Cas nuclease choice and engineering, species-specific delivery, host physiology (cell-wall architecture, cell cycle phase and stress-induced repair-pathway shifts) as well as screening workflows using endogenous markers and high-throughput phenotyping. We propose that integrating species-specific multi-omics analyses, artificial intelligence-assisted design and precise and controllable editing strategies will further enhance the ability of CRISPR-Cas systems to elucidate photosynthetic regulatory networks and environmental response mechanisms in microalgae, while facilitating the optimisation of microalgal metabolic traits and the engineering of environmental adaptability.

title: Amorphized and Oxidized Layered PtSe 2 as an All‐in‐One Electrocatalytic Platform for Hydrazine‐Assisted Water Splitting
summary: ABSTRACT Hydrazine‐assisted water electrolysis is a promising energy‐saving alternative to conventional water splitting; however, noble‐metal catalysts suffer severe deactivation from nitrogen‐intermediate poisoning during sustained anodic
content: ABSTRACT Hydrazine‐assisted water electrolysis is a promising energy‐saving alternative to conventional water splitting; however, noble‐metal catalysts suffer severe deactivation from nitrogen‐intermediate poisoning during sustained anodic operation. Herein, amorphized and oxidized layered PtSe 2 is presented as an all‐in‐one bifunctional electrocatalytic platform solving this challenge. Plasma treatment induces simultaneous surface oxidation, amorphization, and Pt clusterization to form vertically integrated Pt–PtSe x O y heterostructures, as verified by transmission electron microscopy and x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Density functional theory and in situ Raman spectroscopy reveal a potential‐dependent reaction network: N─H dehydrogenation dominates at low bias, while N─N cleavage becomes accessible at elevated potentials. Within this network, the amorphous PtSe x O y matrix acts as an efficient electron sink and proton‐accepting environment. By rendering Pt clusters optimally electron‐deficient, it cooperatively facilitates proton‐coupled electron transfer during N─H activation and fundamentally suppresses the accumulation of strongly bound nitrogen intermediates, resulting in enhanced intrinsic hydrazine oxidation activity with increased turnover frequencies. Simultaneously, the formation of Pt clusters within this modulated coordination environment drastically boosts the cathodic hydrogen evolution reaction beyond commercial Pt/C benchmarks. Leveraging this synergistic bifunctionality, a symmetric two‐electrode electrolyzer achieves highly energy‐efficient overall water splitting, delivering long‐term stability and demonstrating state‐of‐the‐art performance among transition metal compound‐based electrocatalysts.

title: Operando Chlorination Engineering in PEMWE for Direct Brine Electrolysis to Produce Green Hydrogen
summary: ABSTRACT Direct seawater electrolysis in proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers is severely bottlenecked by competitive chlorine evolution and catalyst corrosion. Here, we report an operando chlorination strategy that harnesses corros
content: ABSTRACT Direct seawater electrolysis in proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers is severely bottlenecked by competitive chlorine evolution and catalyst corrosion. Here, we report an operando chlorination strategy that harnesses corrosive ions (Cl − , SO 4 2 − ) to self‐assemble a renewable catalytic layer on a defective RuIrAg pre‐catalyst for highly selective water oxidation. In acidic brine (0.5 M H 2 SO 4 + 3.0 M KCl), it achieves a remarkably low oxygen evolution reaction (OER) overpotential of 108 mV at 10 mA cm − 2 , with a full‐cell energy consumption of 41.01 kWh kg − 1 H 2 at 1 A cm − 2 . In seawater containing 0.25 M Na 2 SO 4 , the system ensures exclusive OER, completely suppressing chlorine evolution up to 3.0 A cm − 2 , and demonstrates 200 h of continuous stability at 1 A cm − 2 (2.59 V). Mechanistically, this robust performance stems from Ag‐induced frustrated Lewis pairs (FLPs). These continuously regenerating FLPs accelerate OER kinetics via enhanced water activation. Simultaneously, the spatially offset FLPs, synergizing with embedded lattice chlorines and AgCl domains, strictly block Cl − chemisorption and dimerization to prohibit Cl 2 evolution. This work establishes a new paradigm for high‐performance electrolysis via operando chlorination and provides a viable route to green hydrogen from direct seawater.

title: Funding and Financing Mechanisms for Decarbonization at Higher Education Institutions
summary: A growing number of higher education institutions (HEIs) are decarbonizing their campuses, with thermal energy networks supported by ground-source-heat pumps (GSHPs) as the most common approach (Barron et al., 2025). The value proposition o
content: A growing number of higher education institutions (HEIs) are decarbonizing their campuses, with thermal energy networks supported by ground-source-heat pumps (GSHPs) as the most common approach (Barron et al., 2025). The value proposition of these systems includes net savings on energy and maintenance, increasing occupant comfort, reducing air pollution and addressing deferred maintenance, guarding against future regulatory risk, providing education and research opportunities, and helping institutions meet climate goals. Despite the many benefits of decarbonization, funding and financing pose a significant challenge given the high upfront costs for GSHPs and building retrofits. “How will we pay for this?” is likely to be the first question when a major infrastructure project is proposed. These capital barriers have the potential to slow the rate at which HEIs can take on these projects and realize the associated economic, social, climate and air quality benefits. Previous research has called for context-specific solutions to financing decarbonization (Long et al., 2024). In this working paper, we compile context-specific approaches for HEIs. We describe the current funding and financing mechanisms used by HEIs for decarbonization and outline potential future sources. This paper is primarily intended for HEIs to use as a guide for early conversations about the economics of GSHP projects.. We present data gathered from HEIs on the capital costs and payback periods of such projects, recognizing that these metrics are incomplete. We primarily focus on the transition of campus heating systems, but note funding and financing for solar and other projects where relevant. Current funding and financing approaches include direct institutional spending, tax credits, state funding and incentives, utility incentives, gifts, internal carbon prices, private debt, green bonds, Green Revolving Funds, and Public Private Partnerships. We highlight a few emerging areas worth attention by both HEIs and state policymakers that can accelerate decarbonization in the non-profit (and for profit) sectors including green banks, Inclusive Utility Investment, public utility Thermal Energy Networks (TENs), and Geothermal Renewable Energy Credits. These tools are worth attention because they can potentially remove the upfront capital barrier to decarbonization for a wide range of customers.

title: Technological neutrality in EU Hydrogen Regulation : An Assessment of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/2359
summary: Hydrogen plays an important role in the European Union’s climate and energy policy, particularly in sectors where direct electrification is difficult. While renewable hydrogen remains in the EU’s long-term priority, low-carbon hydrogen is r
content: Hydrogen plays an important role in the European Union’s climate and energy policy, particularly in sectors where direct electrification is difficult. While renewable hydrogen remains in the EU’s long-term priority, low-carbon hydrogen is recognized as a worth considering option. Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/2359 establishes the methodology for assessing greenhouse gas emissions savings from low-carbon fuels and is therefore central to the legal framework governing low-carbon hydrogen. This thesis applies a doctrinal legal research method. It examines the methodology laid down in Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/2359 from the perspective of technological neutrality. The main research question is to what extent is the methodology consistent with the principle of technological neutrality in EU energy law. The thesis examines the regulatory framework within which the Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/2359 was adopted. The principle of technological neutrality and its application in the case law of the Court of Justice of the European Union are analysed, followed by an examination of the Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/2359 and the methodology it establishes. According to the principle of technological neutrality, legislation, regulation and public procurement should neither favour nor discriminate against any particular technology. This thesis introduces a test for assessing whether a legislative measure is technologically neutral under EU law. The Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/2359 can be considered technologically neutral, as it does not favour specific production pathways.

title: The impact of molecular transport in turbulent non-premixed NH3/H2/N2 jet flames at elevated pressures
summary: The modelling of turbulent combustion of ammonia is particularly challenging due to the complex chemistry featuring an exceptionally wide range of primary chemical time-scales demanding accurate inclusion of turbulence–chemistry interaction
content: The modelling of turbulent combustion of ammonia is particularly challenging due to the complex chemistry featuring an exceptionally wide range of primary chemical time-scales demanding accurate inclusion of turbulence–chemistry interactions. The latter are here treated using a transported joint-scalar probability density function method that enables direct inclusion, without simplification, of a comprehensively validated H/N/O mechanism. The approach is used to model two turbulent ammonia/hydrogen/nitrogen flames at a pressure of 5 atm and at a Reynolds number of 11,200. The use of hydrogen rich mixtures at low Reynolds numbers, together with increased scalar gradients at elevated pressures, raises the issue of differential diffusion, which is included through a decomposition of the terms for molecular transport in composition space and molecular transport in physical space. The latter, which is often neglected under high-Reynolds-number assumptions, is included, while molecular transport in composition space is treated using the Euclidean Minimum Spanning Tree and Modified Curl’s models. The current approach provides good overall agreement with experimental data for both mean and root-mean-square values. The inclusion of molecular transport in physical space produces modest, but consistent, improvements in hydrogen statistics, especially downstream where turbulence has decayed. By contrast, the application to a turbulent hydrogen diffusion flame shows a substantial impact. These findings clarify the role of molecular transport in turbulent flames featuring high hydrogen concentrations. Novelty and significance statement Current transported joint-scalar probability density function (JPDF) methods normally neglect molecular transport in physical space (MTPS) by invoking high-Reynolds-number assumptions, limiting their ability to represent differential diffusion. The limitation is of particular concern for turbulent cracked-ammonia flames at elevated pressures, where local scalar gradients are enhanced and slow ammonia oxidation coexists with fast hydrogen chemistry. This work establishes the first JPDF-MTPS treatment of such flames and further demonstrates the importance of retaining locality in composition space for micromixing models. Its significance also lies in identifying the contribution of differential diffusion in regions of strong scalar gradients and reduced turbulence, rather than being limited to near-field burner regions as previously reported. It is further shown that the impact increases with hydrogen concentration through the application of JPDF-MTPS to a turbulent non-premixed hydrogen flame.

title: Productivity, litter dynamics and soil fertility in agroforestry systems with coconut and cupuassu trees in eastern amazon
summary: Abstract Agroforestry systems (AFS) are sustainable land use strategies that promote productivity and environmental conservation. The intercropping of coconut palm ( Cocos nucifera L.) and five progenies of cupuassu trees [ Theobroma grandi
content: Abstract Agroforestry systems (AFS) are sustainable land use strategies that promote productivity and environmental conservation. The intercropping of coconut palm ( Cocos nucifera L.) and five progenies of cupuassu trees [ Theobroma grandiflorum (Willd. ex Spreng.) Schum.] was evaluated in terms of soil fertility, litter dynamics, and species productivity in Mojú, PA, Brazil. The experiment was implemented in randomized blocks with five treatments (AFS cultivated with cupuassu progenies 174, 186, 215, 286, and Tp) and four replicates. For some variables, these treatments were also compared to a native forest (FOR) and a pasture (PAS). Soil fertility variables at different depths, litterfall and stock, growth, and fruit production were evaluated using ANOVA (F-Test), mean comparison tests (Tukey test for variables involving the five experimental treatments only, and Fisher’s LSD tests, for variables involving the further areas besides the experimental treatments), and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) were applied to these data. Treatments 174, 286, and Tp showed the best fertility results, with pH up to 4.7, exchangeable Ca above 23 mmol c dm⁻ 3 , and BS above 50% in the 0–10 cm layer. FOR had lower pH (3.5) and higher Al saturation (Al sat = 79.5%). Litterfall showed greater accumulation in the dry season. Genotype 215 yielded higher fruits weight (102.5+7.0 kg ha −1 ), and pulp weights (40.5+3.2 kg ha −1 ), while 186 had more fruits per plant. Intercropping with cupuassu trees did not negatively affect the coconut trees and promoted maintenance of soil fertility, especially pH, SOM, P, exchangeable Ca and BS, compared to FOR and PAS. The results demonstrate that different cupuassu progenies offer different benefits, such as greater productivity or more positive impacts on soil fertility, which might be complementary to each other. Therefore, using progenies with these complementary attributes in the same planting with coconut trees can enhance the benefits of AFS.

title: Smart policy, green innovation: The mediation role of environmental regulation
summary: Digitalization has become a key enabler for sustainable transformation, as it increases technological capacity, optimizes resource use and facilitates green innovation. This study examines the link between digitalization, environmental regu
content: Digitalization has become a key enabler for sustainable transformation, as it increases technological capacity, optimizes resource use and facilitates green innovation. This study examines the link between digitalization, environmental regulations, and green innovation by employing a cross-country panel data set from OECD and World Bank sources for the period 2004–2022. The study uses Structural Equation Modeling to analyze the direct and indirect relationships between digitalization, environmental regulations, and green innovation. Fixed Effects, Panel Corrected Standard Errors and Driscoll-Kraay estimations further validate the robustness of the findings. The results indicate that digitalization is an important key factor of sustainable technological advancement and that it has a significant impact on green innovation. Moreover, the results illustrate that the relationship between digitalization and green innovation is mediated positively by environmental regulations, which underscore that the environmental regulations enhance the impact of digitalization on green innovation. The findings of this study have important policy implications because it shows that to enhance green innovation, environmental policies need to be digitally enabled and incentive based. Future research could build on this analysis by examining sector-specific impacts, other digitalization dimensions, and the influence of institutional factors on sustainable innovation outcomes.

title: Enhancing combustion in an ethanol rotary engine via turbulent jet ignition: parametric study and mechanism analysis
summary: Enhancing the combustion of ethanol rotary engine (ERE) is crucial for carbon neutrality. This study systematically compares the effects of conventional spark plug ignition mode (CSPIM) and turbulent jet ignition mode (TJIM) on the performa
content: Enhancing the combustion of ethanol rotary engine (ERE) is crucial for carbon neutrality. This study systematically compares the effects of conventional spark plug ignition mode (CSPIM) and turbulent jet ignition mode (TJIM) on the performance of an ERE. This investigation employs a combined methodology of experimental validation and numerical simulation, systematically analyzes the combustion characteristics of both ignition modes across multiple equivalence ratio conditions. Furthermore, this research elucidates the effect of jet nozzle diameter (JND) on the combustion behavior of the TJIM. The results reveal that TJIM’s effectiveness is governed by the coupling between the energy of the jet flame and the concentration of the mixture in the pre-combustion chamber. It demonstrates superior flame propagation and combustion at equivalence ratios of 1.0 and 1.2 by generating highly turbulent jet flames, but underperforms CSPIM under an equivalence ratio of 0.8 due to reduced jet flame intensity. Furthermore, the optimal JND shifts with the global equivalence ratio — 3.5 mm for lean and 2.0 mm for stoichiometric combustion. The JND governs a trade-off between the mass of fuel in the pre-combustion chamber and the jet flame velocity. While TJIM significantly reduces CO emissions via more complete combustion, it increases NO formation due to higher temperatures.

title: From Computation-Ready to Claim-Ready: An Evidence Framework for MOF Machine Learning
summary: Scientific data are routinely transformed so they can be stored, joined and used by machine-learning models. These steps enable scale, but they can also remove the context that tells us what a prediction means and how far it can be trusted.
content: Scientific data are routinely transformed so they can be stored, joined and used by machine-learning models. These steps enable scale, but they can also remove the context that tells us what a prediction means and how far it can be trusted. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) make this problem especially clear: one nominal material may appear as an experimental crystal, an activated simulation structure, a charge-assigned model or a row of descriptors, while information about protonation, counterions, coordination environment or measurement conditions may disappear along the way. We introduce claim readiness: a framework for asking whether the evidence preserved through a data pipeline is sufficient for the scientific claim made at the end of it. By tracing chemical evidence, identifier joins and evaluation choices, we show that data can be highly usable for machine learning yet incomplete for chemistry-sensitive interpretation, and that a model can still be useful for ranking candidates even when its value-level accuracy decreases under a harder split. The wider lesson is not specific to MOFs: trustworthy scientific machine learning requires a traceable connection between the representation used by the model and the evidence needed to support the resulting claim. Highlights • Claim readiness matches scientific claims to evidence preserved in data pipelines • Model-ready materials data can lose chemistry needed for interpretation • Data joins change which materials enter representation comparisons • Harder data splits reduce accuracy while useful candidate ranking can remain

title: Contribution of subnational regions to national climate change mitigation targets
summary: This study developed a methodology for analyzing the mitigation measures expected of each region within a country, as well as the resulting regional energy supply–demand balances, given national decarbonization targets and assumed future en
content: This study developed a methodology for analyzing the mitigation measures expected of each region within a country, as well as the resulting regional energy supply–demand balances, given national decarbonization targets and assumed future energy system conditions. Using national-level values as an overarching framework, the method represents interregional energy flows and constructed two scenarios: (1) a scenario in which all regions make efforts of equal stringency to collectively achieve the national target (CN1) and (2) a scenario in which each region seeks to achieve carbon neutrality independently within its own jurisdiction (CN2). For each scenario, regional energy supply and demand, carbon absorption by forests, and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions were calculated. The methodology was applied to Japan, treating the nation as a whole and its prefectures as regions, to estimate regional energy balances and GHG emissions under CN1 and CN2 in the context of Japan’s 2050 carbon neutrality target. Under CN1, prefectural GHG emissions relative to the baseline year ranged from 0% to 24%. Given that interregional transfers of renewable energy are prohibited under CN2, some prefectures retained substantial unused renewable energy potential, whereas many others were unable to achieve carbon neutrality within their own boundaries. These findings can support prefectural governments in formulating rational, long-term, and concrete targets by providing reference values for emission and absorption goals and for the specific measures required. The analysis also highlights the need for cooperation between regions where achieving carbon neutrality is relatively feasible and those where it is considerably more challenging.

title: Applying point defect thermodynamics to Prussian Blue: Experiments and modelling
summary: Prussian Blue, Na 1 + ξ Fe[Fe(CN) 6 ] is a promising low-cost cathode material for sodium-ion batteries (SIB). Despite its importance, the range of stoichiometry ξ of this mixed ionic and electronic conducting phase and the point defect str
content: Prussian Blue, Na 1 + ξ Fe[Fe(CN) 6 ] is a promising low-cost cathode material for sodium-ion batteries (SIB). Despite its importance, the range of stoichiometry ξ of this mixed ionic and electronic conducting phase and the point defect structure are not known in adequate detail. An electrochemical cell using a sodium electrode, the solid Na + electrolyte NASICON and Prussian Blue is assembled. The course of the cell potential U cell vs. ξ is measured by galvanostatic intermittent coulometric titration (GITT), the chemical diffusion coefficient D ̃ Na of sodium is determined by evaluation of the cell potential transients. Point defect thermodynamics is used to model relations between stoichiometry ξ , defect concentrations, cell potential U cell , chemical potential and chemical diffusion coefficient D ̃ Na of sodium. The thermal equilibrium between high-spin Fe 3＋ , low-spin Fe 2＋ , low-spin Fe 3＋ and high-spin Fe 2＋ , i.e. “electrons” and “holes”, is decisive for the electrochemical properties. U cell vs. ξ and D ̃ Na vs. ξ exhibit characteristic sigmoidal courses with an inflection point at ξ = 0 . The equilibrium constant K el for electron–hole formation is obtained by fitting the experimental data. The corresponding Gibbs free enthalpy Δ G el 0 has a value of 0.3 eV, in accordance to Marcus-Hush theory, the energy of optically and thermally excited intervalence charge transfer. D ̃ Na is in the order of 10 −12 to 10 −11 cm 2 s −1 , the electronic charge carrier mobilities u e ′ and u h ⋅ in the order of 10 −10 and 10 −9 cm 2 (Vs) −1 , indicating the presence of strongly localised small polarons. A full sodiation results in a Prussian White phase with a nominal composition Na 2 Fe[Fe(CN) 6 ]. A full desodiation seems to be impossible, ending up at a limiting composition of approximately Na 0.2 Fe[Fe(CN) 6 ]. The results of this study offer valuable insights for a better understanding the electrochemical (cycling) behaviour.

title: A Territorial Approach to Transitioning Oil and Gas Producing Regions: Comparative Practices and Prospects for Canada
summary: Abstract Oil and gas transitions are relatively new and especially difficult because the sector is large, economically central, and deeply embedded in national energy systems. Territorial approaches—grounded in regional political economies,
content: Abstract Oil and gas transitions are relatively new and especially difficult because the sector is large, economically central, and deeply embedded in national energy systems. Territorial approaches—grounded in regional political economies, institutions, and community impacts—offer a politically feasible way to begin meaningful oil and gas transitions in Canada's producing regions. Our article first traces the evolution of Canadian oil and gas governance within federal climate architectures and entrenched fossil regionalisms, then draws on comparative case studies of Esbjerg (Denmark), Taranaki (New Zealand), and Aberdeen (Scotland) to show how territorially grounded policies and just transition institutions can help regions move beyond fossil lock‐in. It concludes by distilling cross‐cutting lessons into a governance framework for regionally differentiated transitions in Canadian oil and gas producing regions.

title: Watts to wealth: Electricity, efficiency, and industrial asset pricing
summary: We develop a production-based asset-pricing framework that places electricity at the center of equity return formation. Motivated by a dual-output SIDO technology, we isolate two price-orthogonalized fundamental predictors: a real-activity
content: We develop a production-based asset-pricing framework that places electricity at the center of equity return formation. Motivated by a dual-output SIDO technology, we isolate two price-orthogonalized fundamental predictors: a real-activity scale signal ( Δ EC net ) and a productivity residual ( EE net ). Using year-over-year (YoY) industrial panels for Italy and Sweden, we select forecasting lags via BIC and apply Newey–West HAC inference to evaluate return predictability across distinct energy market structures. At the annual horizon, the predictive signals reveal a marked, specification-dependent cross-country divergence. In Italy, the scale signal ( Δ EC net ) is a strong, FDR-surviving positive predictor in Construction & Materials ( p < 0.001 ), marginally positive in Basic Resources ( p < 0.10 ), and statistically significant in the pooled foundational panel ( p < 0.05 ), though a regime-stability analysis around August 2020 shows that extreme carbon- and power-price volatility crowds out operational signals in several segments during crisis periods. Furthermore, physical energy efficiency ( EE phys ) exhibits valuation-consistent negative loadings in the pooled Italian panel (reaching significance in excess returns), while carbon-cost expectations (EUA) exert a persistent drag on foundational sector returns.
