THP + CAD achieved the most consistently favourable SWI balance, maintaining a 100% above-median frequency up to 25% FW. The AnMBR-based systems exhibited higher volatility and increased the GHG footprint by approximately 4.5%. Ammonia rose with food waste addition, yet free ammonia stayed below inhibitory levels in all scenarios. Optimization indicated that for the THP + CAD + AnMBR configuration, a 0.35 bypass ratio and a 50-day SRT maximized the SWI. These findings show that AD configuration performance depends on the operating regime, which the SWI makes explicit.

title: Transport cost-benefit analysis: critical evaluation and improvement
summary: Cost–benefit analysis (CBA) remains the dominant framework for the ex ante evaluation of transport policies and infrastructure investments, grounded in welfare economics and aimed at maximizing aggregate social welfare. However, a growing b
content: Cost–benefit analysis (CBA) remains the dominant framework for the ex ante evaluation of transport policies and infrastructure investments, grounded in welfare economics and aimed at maximizing aggregate social welfare. However, a growing body of literature questions whether CBA adequately captures the multidimensional objectives of contemporary transport policy, including effectiveness, efficiency, and equity. This paper addresses this debate by systematically identifying and structuring criticisms of CBA in transport, drawing on a scoping review of 75 publications and insights from two expert workshops involving 16 specialists from multiple disciplines. The analysis categorizes criticisms into four groups: (1) fundamental limitations of CBA; (2) shortcomings in practical application; (3) issues related to debatable policy questions; and (4) decision-making challenges. Building on these insights, the paper discusses potential avenues for improvement, including better integration of distributional and accessibility effects, refinement of valuation methods, and alternative approaches. The results suggest that many shortcomings attributed to CBA stem from how it is applied within policy processes. The continued use of CBA in transport policy contexts requires an understanding of inherent weaknesses, their improvement, and appropriate use.

title: The Pattern of Freshwater Consumption by Fossil Fuel Extraction in China Based on Geospatial Datasets
summary: ABSTRACT Despite the wide study of energy‐related water consumption and virtual water, the water consumption of fossil fuel extraction and virtual water related to fossil fuel trade are not fully understood at the level of fossil fuel sites
content: ABSTRACT Despite the wide study of energy‐related water consumption and virtual water, the water consumption of fossil fuel extraction and virtual water related to fossil fuel trade are not fully understood at the level of fossil fuel sites. Here, we assess the water consumption of primary fossil fuel extraction based on a fossil fuel inventory. We find that the total freshwater consumption of fossil fuel extraction is 1.2 billion m 3 in China, with coal, oil, and gas accounting for 52.6%, 44.7%, and 2.8% of the total, respectively. The virtual water transfer via fossil fuel trade across provinces is 798 million m 3 , amounting to 66% of the freshwater consumption for fossil fuel extraction. Coal‐related virtual water accounts for 48% of total virtual water whereas oil‐ and gas‐related virtual water transfer accounts for 52%. The freshwater consumption related to fossil fuel extraction is driven by the domestic consumption of China rather than the international exports to other nations. The construction sector is responsible for 36% of the total freshwater consumption due to its use of fossil‐fuel‐intensive products (i.e., petroleum, coking, metal and electricity). The study fills the gap in the assessment of freshwater consumption by fossil fuel extraction and reveals the water inequalities caused by fossil fuel trade.

title: DOES ENERGY INTENSITY STRENGTHEN THE INDUSTRIALIZATION–ENVIRONMENTAL DEGRADATION NEXUS? EVIDENCE FROM SELECTED ASIAN ECONOMIES
summary: With the growth of Asia's industry, concerns over carbon emissions and energy usage have grown. The aim of this study is to test whether the relationship between industrialization and CO₂ emissions remains constant when energy intensity var
content: With the growth of Asia's industry, concerns over carbon emissions and energy usage have grown. The aim of this study is to test whether the relationship between industrialization and CO₂ emissions remains constant when energy intensity varies within the Asian economies analyzed for the period 2000–2021. Driscoll–Kraay standard errors to account for heteroskedasticity, serial correlation, and cross-sectional dependence. The results indicate that there is a positive relationship between industrialization and energy intensity and CO₂ emissions, while there is a negative relationship between renewable energy consumption and emissions. The main result is that the relationship between industrialization and energy intensity is positive and very strong, meaning that the industrialization process becomes more intensive in energy consumption as energy intensity increases. This is confirmed by the marginal effects estimates: at low energy intensity levels, there is no statistically significant link between industrialization and emissions, while the link is positive and gradually more pronounced at average and high energy intensity levels. The results indicate that reduction in energy intensity is one of the key factors for cleaner industrial development in the selected Asian economies.

title: ESG Due Diligence як правова умова доступу до сталих інвестицій
source: The Scientific Issues of Ternopil Volodymyr Hnatiuk National Pedagogical University Series pedagogy
summary: The article is devoted to the characteristics of ESG Due Diligence as a legal condition for domestic enterprises to attract sustainable capital from private foreign investors. In the conditions of war and post-war recovery, it is important
content: The article is devoted to the characteristics of ESG Due Diligence as a legal condition for domestic enterprises to attract sustainable capital from private foreign investors. In the conditions of war and post-war recovery, it is important for stabilizing the activities of domestic business entities to obtain additional financial resources. One of such areas is attracting sustainable investments from investors from EU countries. A necessary stage for sustainable investment is conducting ESG Due Diligence, which ensures the comprehensiveness of the analysis of the information received regarding the level of implementation of ESG factors at the enterprise. It is substantiated that ESG Due Diligence is an independent type of Due Diligence, which is not reduced to a simple sum of such types of Due Diligence as environmental, social or managerial. Similar features between ESG Due Diligence and legal (juridical) Due Diligence are given. The difference between ESG Due Diligence and legal (juridical) Due Diligence is determined. These are seen as: the purpose of conducting it, which is to create conditions for attracting sustainable investments; orientation on sustainability risk management; performing a predictive function; a wide range of risk assessments (the subject of the recipient company’s activities, risks in supply chains, risks in the climate sector, regarding decent work standards and inclusiveness, the effectiveness of the company’s anti-corruption policies and the transparency of the management system, verification of non-financial reporting for the absence of signs of greenwashing; taking into account the interests of not only the parties to the future contract, but also the interests of employees, consumers, local communities, the interests of future generations in the context of compliance with the requirements of carbon neutrality, environmental protection, etc. It is emphasized that the EU has adopted a set of acts necessary for the gradual transition from voluntary to mandatory ESG Due Diligence: Regulation of the European Union (EU) 2020/852 (EU Taxonomy), Regulation (EU) 2019/2088 on disclosure of information related to sustainable development in the financial services sector (SFDR Regulation), Directive (EU) 2022/2464 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 December 2022 on corporate sustainability reporting (CSRD), Directive (EU) 2024/1760 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024 on corporate sustainability due diligence (CSDDD).

title: Nonlocal, nonlinear electrostatics: like-charge attraction and asymmetric solvation
summary: We study an equilibrium system, where linear molecules with a rigid charge distribution interact via the mean-field generated by the Coulomb coupling. We focus on the nonlinear regime, which is valid close to external charges immersed in th
content: We study an equilibrium system, where linear molecules with a rigid charge distribution interact via the mean-field generated by the Coulomb coupling. We focus on the nonlinear regime, which is valid close to external charges immersed in the system. The finite molecular size in this regime leads to a nonlocal response at short distances. First, we show that the mean-field potential is non-monotonic, i.e., like charges can attract each other. Second, we show that the polarization induced by an external charge (and hence its solvation structure) depends on the sign of this charge, violating the effective C-symmetry of the macroscopic electrodynamics. We identify several scenarios of this effect, characterize it with the free energy and entropy differences, and compare it with analogous effects in asymmetric electrolytes described by nonlinear Poisson-Boltzmann equations.

title: Lithium Niobate Surface-Acoustic-Wave Resonator for Very-High-Frequency Isolated Power Conversion
summary: Piezoelectric devices offer a promising magnetic-free alternative for high-frequency power electronics, enabling compact energy transfer with inherent galvanic isolation. Here we demonstrate a lithium niobate surface acoustic wave (SAW) res
content: Piezoelectric devices offer a promising magnetic-free alternative for high-frequency power electronics, enabling compact energy transfer with inherent galvanic isolation. Here we demonstrate a lithium niobate surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonator that enables isolated power transfer and addresses the challenges in existing piezoelectric devices for power applications, including operation frequencies, power delivery figure of merit (FOM), power handling, and electrical isolation. Our application-optimized 40-MHz SAW resonator, with the two electrically isolated interdigital transducers (IDTs) and acoustic Bragg mirrors, achieves a 25.7 W output power at a less than 15 °C temperature rise with only passive cooling through the back mounting side, and an isolation voltage of 2.17 kV. In DC-AC power conversion, we demonstrate a peak efficiency of 93.8 %, a power delivery FOM of 13.47 mW/V$^2$ and a peak chip power density of 81.7 W/cm$^3$. DC-DC conversion is also demonstrated by connecting a diode rectifier to the output IDT, despite efficiency degrading to 52.7 %. Our results advance SAW devices as one of the core components for next-generation very-high-frequency, miniaturized, high-density, magnetic-free, isolated power converters.

title: Crystallographic and spectroscopic studies of CO2-reduction by Myoglobin-Based semi-artificial enzymes
summary: The conversion of CO2 into value-added chemicals is a key challenge for carbon neutrality. Synthetic metal catalysts enable photo/electrochemical CO2 reduction, but are generally non-sustainable. Natural enzymes, such as carbon monoxide deh
content: The conversion of CO2 into value-added chemicals is a key challenge for carbon neutrality. Synthetic metal catalysts enable photo/electrochemical CO2 reduction, but are generally non-sustainable. Natural enzymes, such as carbon monoxide dehydrogenase, have high activity/selectivity, but are limited by complex biosynthesis and O2 sensitivity. Semi-artificial enzymes, where synthetic cofactors are embedded in protein scaffolds, offer a promising alternative. Hemoproteins are good candidates, as their native heme can be replaced with other metal-porphyrins, while the protein matrix enhances substrate access. Based on recent findings with Co- porphyrin myoglobin, we will investigate CO2 reduction by sperm whale myoglobin containing Fe/Co-porphyrin. In-crystallo spectroscopy at the FIP2 beamline will enable structural characterization of key intermediates. This work will clarify the catalytic mechanisms and guide the design of new CO2-reducing biocatalysts.

title: A Compressible Miles Instability for Wind-Wave Generation in a Neutral Atmosphere
summary: We study the normal-mode stability of a flat interface between compressible Euler flow in the air and incompressible Euler flow in the water, including gravity and surface tension. The base state is quiescent water beneath a hydrostatic, co
content: We study the normal-mode stability of a flat interface between compressible Euler flow in the air and incompressible Euler flow in the water, including gravity and surface tension. The base state is quiescent water beneath a hydrostatic, constant-entropy shear flow $U(z)$ with $U(0)=0$, so the atmosphere is neutrally stratified. For a small ratio $\varepsilon$ of the air density at the interface to the water density, and for uniformly subsonic wave-relative flow, we establish a compressible analog of the critical-layer instability of Miles, extending the rigorous incompressible theory of Bühler, Shatah, Walsh, and Zeng. For a real phase speed $c_r$, the singular coefficient at a regular critical level $U(z_c)=c_r$ has a residue proportional to $Q=U''+gU'/a^2=\barρ_0(U'/\barρ_0)'$, with gravitational acceleration $g$, sound speed $a$, and normalized base-state air density $\barρ_0$. Thus the gradient of specific vorticity replaces the curvature $U''$ of the incompressible theory. We prove a limiting absorption principle at regular, non-resonant phase speeds and a residue formula for the imaginary part of the boundary value $Z_{\mathrm a}^+(k,c_r)$ of the air-side pressure response at wavenumber $k>0$. Let $c_k>0$ be the phase speed of the free gravity-capillary wave. If $\mathrm{Im}\,Z_{\mathrm a}^+(k,c_k)>0$, then, for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, the dispersion relation has exactly one unstable root $c_\varepsilon$ in a neighborhood of $c_k$ that does not depend on $\varepsilon$. A sufficient condition is $Q\le0$ at every critical level and $Q<0$ at the highest one. As the Mach number $M\to0$, $Z_{\mathrm a}^+$ converges to its incompressible counterpart at rate $O(M^2)$. Under the corresponding incompressible sign condition, the unstable root satisfies $|c_\varepsilon(M)-c_\varepsilon(0)|\le C\varepsilon M^2$ with $C$ independent of $\varepsilon$ and $M$.

title: Institutional aspects of mobilizing Islamic Finance for infrastructure projects
summary: The predicted infrastructure deficit of US$84 billion in Kazakhstan by 2040 can be substantially mitigated through the execution of public-private partnership (PPP) initiatives and the attraction of investments from alternative sources, suc
content: The predicted infrastructure deficit of US$84 billion in Kazakhstan by 2040 can be substantially mitigated through the execution of public-private partnership (PPP) initiatives and the attraction of investments from alternative sources, such as Islamic finance. Islamic finance has significant potential to bridge this gap but faces institutional barriers to mobilizing it. This study examines the institutional conditions affecting the mobilization of Islamic finance for infrastructure PPPs in Kazakhstan. Directed qualitative content analysis of institutional documents is guided by Douglass North’s distinction between formal rules, informal constraints, and enforcement. The analysis combines legislation, regulatory materials, and published market evidence with two illustrative cases, the BAKAD road and Kokshetau Hospital. The study finds that Kazakhstan’s challenge hindering the effective mobilization of Islamic finance for infrastructure PPPs is not only to expand the existing fragmented regulatory framework for Islamic finance but also to realign formal institutions with deep-rooted social informal norms and regulate enforcement mechanisms. This study makes a unique contribution by examining the mobilization of Islamic finance within PPP frameworks in Kazakhstan, a topic the existing literature typically analyzes separately. Its originality lies in comprehensive institutional analysis, which encompasses both theoretical and practical discussions on informal and enforcement barriers to mobilizing Islamic finance resources that are not obvious.

content: Ekonomske fakultete, avtor predloženega dela z naslovom Vloga industrijske politike pri razvoju trga električnih vozil na Kitajskem, pripravljenega v sodelovanju z mentorjem red.prof.dr.Markom Jakličem POVZETEK V diplomskem delu sem analiziral industrijske politike Kitajske in njihov vpliv na razvoj trga električnih vozil.Namen naloge je bil ugotoviti, na kakšen način je industrijska politika vplivala na oblikovanje in širitev tega trga.V okviru analize so bili obravnavani instrumenti na strani povpraševanja in ponudbe ter regulativni in infrastrukturni instrumenti.Ključna ugotovitev naloge je, da Kitajska ni izvajala industrijske politike zgolj kot nabor obsežnih in finančno zahtevnih ukrepov, temveč je instrumente uvajala strateško ter postopoma, skladno z razvojnimi fazami trga.Takšen pristop je omogočil, da so gospodarski subjekti delovali v skladu s svojimi lastnimi interesi, hkrati je bil dosežen razvoj trga električnih vozil, ki v takšnem obsegu ob prostem delovanju trga in brez intervencije države ne bi bil mogoč.

title: Labour reallocation and production-network recomposition in the green transition
summary: A growing number of countries are adopting policies to reduce greenhouse-gas emissions, a process expected to reshape production systems and labour markets by altering relative prices and changing production and demand patterns across secto
content: A growing number of countries are adopting policies to reduce greenhouse-gas emissions, a process expected to reshape production systems and labour markets by altering relative prices and changing production and demand patterns across sectors. We develop an agent-based monetary input--output network model to analyse the medium-term effects of climate policies on production networks and sectoral labour allocation. The model features heterogeneous industries and households, incorporates greenhouse-gas emissions accounting, and is calibrated to a multi-regional input--output database covering the world economy. We simulate two alternative climate-policy scenarios over 2026--2035: one based on countries' nationally determined contributions and another targeting larger reductions in global emissions. The results reveal significant economy-wide reallocation: fossil-energy sectors contract, low-carbon energy sectors expand, and their positions within production networks change asymmetrically. Fossil energy loses relevance as a direct supplier and exerts less forward influence, while its remaining production becomes more dependent on intermediate inputs and upstream suppliers; low-carbon energy primarily strengthens its role as a supplier. Carbon pricing also generates sectoral labour gaps that, under mobility frictions, imply greater potential transitional unemployment. Because the model allows only limited technological change and adjustment within existing production links, the simulations provide a counterfactual assessment of how existing production structures respond to a relatively rapid climate transition, revealing the adjustment pressures that emerge when policy ambitions advance faster than the productive system's capacity to adapt.

title: Escaping the Composite Fermi Sea: An Incompressible State at Half Filling in Graphene's Lowest Landau Level
summary: Recent experiments in monolayer and trilayer graphene have observed incompressible even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states within narrow regions of parameter space associated with crossings of zeroth Landau levels. This is surprisin
content: Recent experiments in monolayer and trilayer graphene have observed incompressible even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states within narrow regions of parameter space associated with crossings of zeroth Landau levels. This is surprising because at half filling the Coulomb interaction in the zeroth Landau level is expected to favour a compressible composite Fermi liquid. Here we provide the first quantitative energetic study of the candidate incompressible phases and of the microscopic mechanisms that can stabilise them near such Landau-level crossings. Using exact diagonalization and infinite density-matrix renormalisation group, we first study ultra-short-range corrections to the Coulomb interaction arising from finite layer separation, lattice-scale effects, and electron-phonon coupling. We find that a sufficiently strong attractive short-range interaction drives the composite Fermi liquid first into a weakly paired \(d\)-wave pseudospin-singlet state and subsequently into a strongly paired state. However, microscopic estimates of these short-range corrections are far too small to stabilise either incompressible phase. We then incorporate Landau-level mixing through screening within the random-phase approximation. Screening substantially reshapes the effective interaction, suppresses the weak-pairing regime, and strongly enhances the tendency toward strong pairing. For a realistic range of microscopic parameters, the strongly paired phase is stabilised over a substantial fraction of that range. Our results identify the interplay of Landau-level mixing and ultra-short-range interactions as a plausible microscopic mechanism for the experimentally observed incompressible states in monolayer and trilayer graphene and point toward a strongly paired composite-fermion phase as their candidate ground state.

title: Combined Hydrogen and Oxygen transport membranes in the activation of Methane
summary: Dense ceramic membranes have been extensively studied for gas separation and as reaction supports for significant environmental processes. In the work presented in this thesis, yttrium/zirconia doped barium cerate (BaCe0.8Y0.2O3-δ- BCY20 an
content: Dense ceramic membranes have been extensively studied for gas separation and as reaction supports for significant environmental processes. In the work presented in this thesis, yttrium/zirconia doped barium cerate (BaCe0.8Y0.2O3-δ- BCY20 and BaCe0.6Zr0.2Y0.2O3-δ- BCZY) powders were synthesised using the sol-gel method and were calcinated to remove impurities (e.g. carbonates) in both conventional and microwave sintering furnaces at 900-1250OC, to understand the process and attempt to reduce the calcination temperature. Results from the calcination tests proved that the use of a microwave furnace can reduce the calcination time and temperature for BCY20, from 1200OC for 12h in a conventional furnace, to 1000OC for 1h, thereby saving time and energy. For BCZY, the using a microwave furnace does not make a difference to the calcination temperature, the addition of the high melting point ZrO2 could not be removed at temperatures below 1250OC. BCZY20 and BaCe0.6Zr0.2Y0.2O3-δ-Ce0.8Gd0.2O3-δ dense membranes, were produced in the laboratory at low temperatures (1150OC), with the addition of 1-2% ZnO sintering aid and microwave furnace, alongside the samples containing 2% ZnO displaying a 92% relative density when sintered at 1150OC for 6h. The success of producing a dense membrane in the laboratory meant catalytic tests could be completed. BaCe0.6Zr0.2Y0.2O3-δ was selected as the membrane support for wireless Electrochemical Promotion for CO oxidation on Pt. In a dual-chamber reactor, the use of H2/H2O flow in the sweep side, induced promoting species supply, to the catalyst in the reaction side of the reactor. Moderate promotion of the catalytic rate up to 10%, was observed for temperatures up to 650OC, while this promotional effect was reversible and repeatable. The encouraging preliminary catalytic experiments together with the membrane’s stability under the applied conditions reinforce the candidacy of BCZY membranes for intermediate-temperature applications in catalytic membrane reactors. Continuing with the success of the wireless EPOC of CO oxidation on Pt using BCZY support, BCZY:CGO hollow fibre hybrid membrane was applied to the dehydrogenative conversion of methane with in-situ continuous removal of hydrogen in a hollow fibre catalytic membrane reactor (HFCMR). This proved successful at 775OC, in a counter current setup, the use of a membrane showed 50% increase of reaction rate compared to a regular packed bed reactor, injecting air into the sweep side of the system, to permeate into the reactor side and burn the poisoning carbonous product off to increase the reactions lifetime, albeit with a slight decrease in rate due to the production of CO and CO2.

title: Modeling Carbon Emissions Driven by Land‐Use Change: Uncertainty and Sensitivity Analysis of Dynamic Global Vegetation Models
summary: Abstract As a key component of the climate system, terrestrial carbon dynamics are commonly simulated using Dynamic Global Vegetation Models (DGVMs), which provide essential information for estimating the global carbon budget. However, subs
content: Abstract As a key component of the climate system, terrestrial carbon dynamics are commonly simulated using Dynamic Global Vegetation Models (DGVMs), which provide essential information for estimating the global carbon budget. However, substantial uncertainties persist in DGVM‐based estimates of land‐use change carbon emissions, and their process‐level origins remain poorly constrained. Here, we harmonize DGVM‐based net land‐use emissions (E NLUC ) from 23 TRENDY2025 DGVMs using a transient, time‐varying PFT‐level land‐cover correction that explicitly removes the loss of additional sink capacity (LASC), and apply a hierarchical Bayesian mixed‐effects variance decomposition framework to characterize between‐DGVM heterogeneity in fitted coefficients associated with land‐use predictors. LASC correction reveals that uncorrected DGVMs artificially converge toward bookkeeping estimates, masking persistent structural deficiencies—most notably the limited representation of wood harvest, forest management, and other peat‐related activities incorporated in bookkeeping models. Between‐DGVM heterogeneity in fitted coefficients is greater for persistent regrowth area than for current deforestation, particularly at decadal‐to‐centennial timescales and in the tropics, where the fitted association with persistent regrowth area varies substantially among models. This uncertainty can propagate into residual land sink estimates, complicating the diagnosis of land–atmosphere carbon exchange. Our results highlight that improving the representation of secondary forest recovery, including sub‐grid land‐use processes and forest management, is critical for reducing uncertainties in land‐use and land‐use change emissions in next‐generation DGVMs.

title: Certified passive house: an effective control of radon in domestic construction
summary: The international Certified Passive House Standard delivers high thermal comfort based on the principles of excellent building fabric and balanced mechanical heat recovery ventilation. Considering that the typical person in developed countr
content: The international Certified Passive House Standard delivers high thermal comfort based on the principles of excellent building fabric and balanced mechanical heat recovery ventilation. Considering that the typical person in developed countries (such as Ireland and the United Kingdom) spends 90% of their time indoors, there are surprisingly few academic studies on air quality in the home. Indoor air quality and the prevalence of overheating are attracting an increasing amount of research attention across Europe, but post occupancy monitoring of indoor radon concentrations is severely underrepresented, especially in Ireland and the UK. Radon is a naturally occurring radioactive gas and known carcinogen that presents a potential risk to occupier health. This PhD research investigates measured radon levels in certified Passive House buildings in Ireland and the UK and presents the findings. The research has found that 97 monitored Certified Passive House Standard buildings exhibit 60% lower indoor radon concentrations at 36 Bq/m3 than the national average of 77 Bq/m3 and reference levels (Target level 100 Bq/m3 and Action Level 200 Bq/m3). A series of comparison case studies located in high risk geogenic radon areas have demonstrated a significant contrast with comparison homes reinforcing the main findings. The second major finding found a uniform distribution of radon levels between upstairs and downstairs in the Certified Passive House sample (6%) when compared against standard buildings with natural ventilation (33%-35%). The evidence from this study suggests a 18% reduction in indoor radon concentrations between timber frame construction and masonry construction. Then finally, initial evidence suggests that the EnerPhit standard (18% reduction) will mitigate against elevated radon levels in buildings being retrofitted. This is an issue currently pertinent to the Construction Industry. The growth of energy-efficient standards (such as Passive House) and common principles (such as increased airtightness levels and mechanical ventilation systems) have accelerated the need for research data on indoor radon concentrations. This research bridges the knowledge gap between the fields of indoor air quality (specifically radon), health, sustainability, and the built environment. The study outlines the implications for policy and practice including practical recommendations.

title: Naming men as men again: three key challenges for men, masculinities and organizations in the polycrisis
summary: In this article, we set out what we suggest are three key challenges for critical studies on men, masculinities and organizations in the context of the polycrisis. We first provide an overview some of the major contributions over recent dec
content: In this article, we set out what we suggest are three key challenges for critical studies on men, masculinities and organizations in the context of the polycrisis. We first provide an overview some of the major contributions over recent decades of Feminist Studies on Organizations, Critical Studies on Men and Masculinities, Critical Management Studies, Critical Leadership Studies, and Critical Studies on Men, Masculinities and Organizations. In one sense, the article can be understood as ‘naming men as men, again’ in Organization Studies, more than 30 years after the 1994 article on ‘naming men as men’. We then work collectively to assess contemporary and future challenges and intersectional gender relations in organizations, and critical studies thereon. The key challenges addressed are: socio-technological challenges, with the focus on digitalization and artificial intelligence (AI); ecological challenges, with the focus on ecological collapse and crises in the (m)Anthropocene; and political challenges, with the focus on authoritarianism and the possibilities for global governance. The article concludes with key recommendations for a future research agenda for critical studies on men, masculinities and organizations, namely: naming men as men, again; interorganizational clusters and relations; links between challenges; control of AI and its harms; authoritarianism and destruction; collective, emancipatory global governance; and ethical ecojustice planetary futures.

title: Integrasi Energi Terbarukan, Penyimpanan, Dan Fleksibilitas Beban Pada Bangunan Gedung Hijau Untuk Memperkuat Ketahanan Energi Perkotaan
summary: Bangunan Gedung Hijau (BGH) berpotensi menjadi simpul aktif sistem energi kota, tetapi efisiensi atau keseimbangan energi tahunan belum dengan sendirinya menjamin layanan saat jaringan terganggu. Penelitian ini menganalisis bagaimana energi
content: Bangunan Gedung Hijau (BGH) berpotensi menjadi simpul aktif sistem energi kota, tetapi efisiensi atau keseimbangan energi tahunan belum dengan sendirinya menjamin layanan saat jaringan terganggu. Penelitian ini menganalisis bagaimana energi terbarukan, penyimpanan, dan fleksibilitas beban perlu diintegrasikan untuk memperkuat ketahanan energi perkotaan. Tinjauan literatur sistematis terarah dilakukan terhadap 30 artikel jurnal akses terbuka periode 2020-2026. Artikel diverifikasi melalui teks lengkap dan DOI, kemudian diekstraksi berdasarkan konteks, intervensi, indikator, temuan, keterbatasan, dan kontribusi terhadap fase antisipasi, penyerapan gangguan, pemulihan, serta adaptasi. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa energi terbarukan memperkuat ketersediaan lokal, tetapi manfaat resiliensinya dibatasi variabilitas dan kemampuan operasi saat padam. Penyimpanan menjembatani ketidaksesuaian waktu antara produksi dan kebutuhan, sedangkan fleksibilitas memperkecil puncak, menggeser konsumsi, serta memprioritaskan beban kritis. Ketiganya menghasilkan nilai tertinggi setelah beban dasar ditekan, dikendalikan oleh sistem manajemen energi, dan diuji dengan skenario gangguan. Penelitian mengusulkan metrik jam otonomi, cakupan beban kritis, energi tidak terlayani, keberhasilan islanding, cadangan state of charge, serta waktu pemulihan. Bagi Indonesia, integrasi tersebut perlu diterapkan bertahap pada BGH tropis dan fasilitas vital melalui audit beban kritis, submetering, commissioning, pengujian operasi pulau, dan agregasi energi tingkat kawasan.

title: Rethinking land degradation neutrality in hyper-arid ecosystems: Functional neutrality, recovery memory and process-based monitoring for SDG 15.3.1
source: Journal of Degraded and Mining Lands Management
summary: Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) has become a central policy framework for translating SDG 15.3 into measurable land action, but its interpretation remains difficult in hyper-arid ecosystems. This critical conceptual review evaluates wheth
content: Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) has become a central policy framework for translating SDG 15.3 into measurable land action, but its interpretation remains difficult in hyper-arid ecosystems. This critical conceptual review evaluates whether land cover, land productivity, and soil organic carbon are ecologically diagnostic in the world’s driest landscapes. Evidence was synthesized from LDN policy, dryland ecology, soil carbon science, remote sensing, aeolian geomorphology, salinity research, restoration ecology, and Nature-based Solutions. The review shows that sparse vegetation, low productivity, exposed mineral surfaces, and low SOC can represent natural desert reference conditions, while important degradation may occur through wind erosion, salinization, biological soil crust disturbance, hydrological disconnection, thermal stress, and loss of post-rainfall recovery capacity. Four recurrent misclassification pathways are identified: false degradation, false recovery, hidden degradation, and false neutrality. A Functional LDN Framework is proposed to link state, process, function, risk, and feasibility. The framework retains global SDG 15.3.1 comparability while adding dryland-specific diagnostics, recovery memory, and functional equivalence rules. Recalibrating LDN around ecosystem function can improve degraded land management, restoration targeting, and monitoring credibility in hyper-arid regions.

title: Editorial: Rewriting archaeology with AI
summary: Frontispiece 1. Ancient Greek computing technology: the Antikythera mechanism, on display at the Hellenic National Archaeological Museum in Athens (inv.no.X 15087).This 2000-year-old device is claimed to be the world's first analogue comput
content: Frontispiece 1. Ancient Greek computing technology: the Antikythera mechanism, on display at the Hellenic National Archaeological Museum in Athens (inv.no.X 15087).This 2000-year-old device is claimed to be the world's first analogue computer.It was retrieved in 1901 from an ancient shipwreck off the Greek island of Antikythera.This fragmentary and corroded, box-shaped bronze device originally measured about 340mm high.Inscriptions identified on it support the consensus that it was constructed to predict the positions of celestial bodies.It featured several interlinked indicators, driven by a system of interlocking gearwheels, which displayed the positions of the moon and the sun and likely the planets within the zodiac, the date according to the Egyptian calendar, a Greek lunisolar calendar, and details of upcoming solar and lunar eclipses.Modern research, including a new digital simulation, suggests that the mechanism was prone to errors.It could only be cranked to about four months into the future before its complex system of interconnected gears jammed or its teeth disengaged and everything needed to be reset.Is there a lesson here for modern computing technology?Photograph: Francesco Bini.CC BY-SA 4.0.

title: 环境属性理论框架下的原子模型与核外电子配对机制
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Abstract Within the framework of the Environmental Attribute Theory (EAT, 环境属性理论), this paper systematically establishes a full-chain atomic model and extranuclear electron pairing theory from a single atom to chemical reactions. EAT reduce
content: Abstract Within the framework of the Environmental Attribute Theory (EAT, 环境属性理论), this paper systematically establishes a full-chain atomic model and extranuclear electron pairing theory from a single atom to chemical reactions. EAT reduces physical phenomena to the distribution and motion of fundamental medium particles (Dianxon ψ+/ψ−, 电性子 ψ+/ψ−; Zhongxon ψ0, 中性子 ψ0). Its highest principle—the principle of minimization of environmental imbalance (环境不平衡性最小化原理)—requires the total environmental imbalance degree U_atom (总环境不平衡度) of the system to tend to a minimum. This paper proves that the basic structural unit of extranuclear electrons is the "dual-center symmetric motion pair" (双圆心对称运动对)—two electrons moving in opposite directions on a circle of equal radius with the atomic nucleus as the symmetry center. This configuration is an inevitable result of minimizing U_atom, simultaneously achieving triple minimization effects: far-field electrical neutrality (远场电中性) (∇ρ_e^net → 0), far-field diamagnetism (远场抗磁性) (∇×(ρ_e v)^net → 0), and minimum system energy. We derive in detail the mechanical equilibrium equation for a single electron in the electron pair under the synergistic action of the Coulomb attribute force (库仑属性力) and the magnetic field attribute force (磁场属性力), revealing the dual role of the magnetic field attribute force as a "locking force" (锁紧力) and a centripetal force component. At the multi-electron atomic level, we prove the geometric origin of the electron shell capacity formula N_max(n) = 2n^2 (电子层容量公式)—the n-th shell uniformly distributes n^2 motion axes (运动轴) on a spherical surface, with each axis corresponding to one electron pair; we demonstrate the inter-shell motion coupling mechanism (层间运动耦合机制) (all electrons move in the same direction) and the symmetric distribution principle of electrons in unfilled shells (未满层电子的对称分布原则) (the tetrahedral configuration of the carbon atom explains the diamond structure). At the chemical bond level, we uniformly interpret covalent bonds (共价键) and ionic bonds (离子键) as the result of motion axis network reconstruction (运动轴网络重构) to reduce the composite system's U_total, giving a unified bond energy expression E_bond = κ_E(ΣU_i − U_composite) (键能表达式); we reduce the driving force of chemical reactions to the microscopic criterion U_product < U_reactant (化学反应驱动力), establishing a correspondence with the classical ΔG < 0 criterion (ΔG < 0 判据); and we clarify that the photo-thermal phenomena of reactions (反应光热现象) originate from free-state Zhongxon fluctuations (自由态中性子波动) excited by the variable-speed motion of electrons. This paper provides a unified medium-dynamics framework (介质动力学框架) based on first principles for understanding atomic structure, chemical bonds, and chemical reactions, achieving a complete causal chain (因果贯穿) from fundamental medium particles to chemical phenomena, and proposes several quantitatively verifiable theoretical predictions for subsequent experimental testing. Keywords: Enviro
