The addition of peanut flour or pre-digested peanuts to human fecal bioreactors increased levels of megasphaera, clostridia and bifidobacteria, associated with high levels of SCFA production. 246 metabolites were significantly altered following peanut fermentation. All 10 tested bifidobacterial strains were able to metabolize peanut in vitro , with B. longum strain 160 being the most effective. Following growth on peanuts, bifidobacterial supernatants enhanced IL-10 secretion, but reduced TNF-alpha and IL-5 secretion from stimulated PBMCs. Conclusions. Peanuts are metabolized by early life microbes generating immunoregulatory metabolites. These metabolites may play an important role in their allergy protective effects complementing mechanisms associated with direct antigen sampling by the immune system.

title: Vibrational strong coupling influences product selectivity in a model for post-transition-state bifurcation reactions
summary: In this study, we explore the possibility of modulating product selectivity (branching ratios) in post-transition-state bifurcation reactions via vibrational strong coupling (VSC) to an optical cavity. Detailed classical and quantum dynamic
content: In this study, we explore the possibility of modulating product selectivity (branching ratios) in post-transition-state bifurcation reactions via vibrational strong coupling (VSC) to an optical cavity. Detailed classical and quantum dynamical calculations on a model potential reveal that the branching ratio can be enhanced by nearly a factor of two under VSC conditions. Interestingly, upon altering the shape of the potential, we find a switch in the cavity frequency at which maximum enhancement in selectivity is observed. Apart from emphasizing the role of both cavity-system and intramolecular energy transfer to the observed enhancements, we highlight the complexity of the VSC mechanism in terms of the choice of the cavity frequency vis-à-vis the various molecular mode frequencies. Our work shows that, in principle, cavity quantum electrodynamics can reshape dynamical outcomes in reactions with complex potential energy landscapes.

title: WAPOSAL: a multi-regional wave dataset from satellite altimetry for significant wave height, period estimation, and wave power density
summary: Abstract. Accurate assessment of wave power density (WPD) is essential for marine renewable energy development and for validating numerical wave models, particularly in coastal and nearshore regions where in situ observations are sparse. Th
content: Abstract. Accurate assessment of wave power density (WPD) is essential for marine renewable energy development and for validating numerical wave models, particularly in coastal and nearshore regions where in situ observations are sparse. This study presents a high-resolution, multi-region wave dataset generated within the WAPOSAL (Wave Power & Satellite Altimetry) project, derived from Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) altimetry data acquired by the Sentinel-3A/B and CryoSat-2 missions. Significant wave height and normalized radar cross-section were obtained using the SAMOSA+ retracker, and zerocrossing wave period was estimated based on an empirical regression method calibrated with in situ buoy and ERA5 data. Wave power density was then computed along altimeter tracks across eleven regions: Norway & Baltic Sea, UK & North Sea, French Facade, Spain Atlantic, Portugal, Mediterranean sea, Madeira, Canary Islands, Azores Archipelago, French Guiana and French Polynesia. The temporal coverage spans 2011–2023, depending on the region and the satellite mission considered. The present paper describes the database and illustrates its use through simple application examples. The dataset in its current format and version can be discovered, shared and cited via the following link: https://doi.org/10.57780/ESA-1AB8CF3 (Ponce de Léon et al., 2026).

title: A Tale of Two Heterocycles: How Oxygen and Sulfur Shape Divergent Kemp Reactivity
summary: ABSTRACT The Kemp elimination is a well‐studied reaction that proceeds through the deprotonation of carbon‐3 of benzisoxazoles, coupled with irreversible ring opening by cleavage of the labile O‐N bond. The base‐catalyzed reaction is concer
content: ABSTRACT The Kemp elimination is a well‐studied reaction that proceeds through the deprotonation of carbon‐3 of benzisoxazoles, coupled with irreversible ring opening by cleavage of the labile O‐N bond. The base‐catalyzed reaction is concerted, with no detectable intermediate. Due to their compositional and structural similarities, benzisothiazoles are also candidates for Kemp elimination reactions; however, little information was previously available on these compounds. We found that benzisothiazoles also undergo Kemp elimination, and we have characterized the Kemp product. As previously observed with benzisoxazoles, reactions of benzisothiazoles are significantly accelerated by polar, aprotic solvents and by the presence of electron‐withdrawing groups (EWG) on the six‐membered ring. In mixed water/DMSO systems, we found a strong inverse linear relationship between the logarithm of the second‐order rate constant and the mole fraction of water for both benzisoxazoles and benzisothiazoles. Linear free‐energy relationship (LFER) analyses reveal opposing solvent‐dependent behavior between the two heterocycles: DMSO steepens substituent sensitivity in benzisoxazoles relative to water but dampens it in benzisothiazoles. Extrapolation of the chemically controlled regime suggests that transitioning from water to pure DMSO produces a remarkable ~14‐order‐of‐magnitude increase in the intrinsic chemical reactivity of 5‐nitrobenzisoxazole, compared to an ~7‐order‐of‐magnitude acceleration for 5‐nitrobenzisothiazole. This divergence highlights fundamental differences in how protic and aprotic media stabilize the localized phenolate versus the soft, polarizable thiophenolate anion.

title: The Electrodynamical Nature of Chiral Nanoplasmonics from the Quantum Regime to the Mesoscale
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Abstract Chiral plasmonic nanostructures are rapidly emerging as ideal substrates for enantioselective sensing, chiral near-field engineering, and plasmon-assisted catalysis, owing to their exceptional sensitivity to structural handedness.
content: Abstract Chiral plasmonic nanostructures are rapidly emerging as ideal substrates for enantioselective sensing, chiral near-field engineering, and plasmon-assisted catalysis, owing to their exceptional sensitivity to structural handedness. However, whether an atomistic classical electrodynamic description can capture the plasmonic chiroptical response across size regimes spanning from the quantum to the mesoscale remains an open question, limiting the development of predictive theoretical methods for the design of novel chiral plasmonic architectures. Here, we show that a fully atomistic classical electrodynamic model, coupling intraband charge transport and interband polarization, quantitatively reproduces state-of-the-art ab initio and experimental chiroptical spectra across the quantum-to-classical regime, from atomistically defined chiral Ag and Au nanostructures to DNA-origami-assembled Au nanorods containing up to ∼105 atoms. Our results show that a classical atomistic description remains valid in both the quantum regime and the mesoscale, providing the missing foundation to connect local structural motifs to chiroptical response and paving the way for the atomistically defined, rational design of chiral plasmonic nanostructures optimized for targeted applications.

title: Reconciling intrinsic and ecosystem water-use efficiency reveals physiological mechanisms underlying carbon-water coupling across biological scales
summary: Understanding how carbon-water coupling scales from leaves to ecosystems remains a major challenge because water-use efficiency (WUE) metrics integrate physiological, hydrological, and ecological processes. We integrated tree-ring width, tr
content: Understanding how carbon-water coupling scales from leaves to ecosystems remains a major challenge because water-use efficiency (WUE) metrics integrate physiological, hydrological, and ecological processes. We integrated tree-ring width, triple stable isotopes (δ13C, δ18O and δ2H), eddy covariance (EC) observations, and a process-based model to investigate the drivers of intrinsic (iWUE) and ecosystem water-use efficiency (WUEeco) across biological scales in a mature Fagus sylvatica forest between 2004 and 2023. Modelled and isotope-derived iWUE were strongly correlated (r = 0.61, p < 0.05) and both indicated an approximately 20% long-term increase, consistent with increasing gross primary productivity. In contrast, WUEeco derived from EC was lower than model estimates and exhibited a positive trend not reproduced by the model. This divergence primarily reflected differences in biological representation and hydrological integration, as the single-species model underestimated ecosystem evapotranspiration by excluding co-occurring deciduous and evergreen species together with understory vegetation. Triple-isotope analyses showed that the long-term increase in iWUE was driven by enhanced photosynthetic assimilation rather than sustained stomatal closure, whereas δ18O and δ2H variability was mainly controlled by source-water dynamics. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for reconciling leaf- and ecosystem-scale WUE and improving predictions of forest carbon-water coupling under climate change.

title: Boron-assisted stabilization of low-resistivity mixed-valence Cu–O thin films prepared by reactive magnetron sputtering
summary: This study systematically investigated the influence of boron incorporation in Cu-O thin films and the effect of oxygen partial pressure ( p ox ) on the phase evolution, chemical bonding, and electrical characteristics of the prepared films
content: This study systematically investigated the influence of boron incorporation in Cu-O thin films and the effect of oxygen partial pressure ( p ox ) on the phase evolution, chemical bonding, and electrical characteristics of the prepared films. A phase transition from Cu 2 O to Cu 2 O/Cu 4 O 3 to CuO was observed as oxygen partial pressure increased. Boron incorporation significantly broadened the stability window of the Cu 2 O and Cu 4 O 3 phases and delayed the transition to CuO at higher oxygen partial pressure. In the highly B-doped Cu‒O films, Cu 4 O 3 was stabilized even under oxygen-rich conditions along with CuO phase, suggesting that boron significantly altered the oxidation pathway. The formation of B‒O and possible B‒O‒Cu configurations altered the local oxygen chemistry and promoted mixed-valence copper oxide phases. Electrical measurements revealed that highly B-doped Cu–O films exhibited a delayed transition from a high-resistivity low- p ox regime to a low-resistivity mixed-valence regime, ultimately reaching ∼0.06 Ωcm, among the lowest reported resistivities for a CuO-like material. These findings demonstrate that boron doping is an effective approach for tailoring the phase stability, defect chemistry, and electrical characteristics of Cu‒O thin films for optoelectronic and photovoltaic applications.

title: The WEST code for large-scale excited-state materials simulations
summary: We present WEST, an open-source plane-wave pseudopotential code for large-scale excited-state materials simulations, and describe its theoretical foundations, software architecture, and capabilities. WEST implements full-frequency GW, quant
content: We present WEST, an open-source plane-wave pseudopotential code for large-scale excited-state materials simulations, and describe its theoretical foundations, software architecture, and capabilities. WEST implements full-frequency GW, quantum defect embedding theory, the Bethe-Salpeter equation, and time-dependent density functional theory within a common algorithmic framework that avoids the explicit computation of virtual electronic states. By combining density functional and density matrix perturbation theory, low-rank representations of the dielectric screening and exact exchange, and localization techniques, WEST achieves favorable computational scaling with system size. The code supports the calculation of quasi-particle and neutral excitation energies, optical and photoluminescence spectra, excited-state forces, and non-adiabatic couplings, with interoperable workflows connecting to quantum chemistry, vibronic coupling, and quantum computing packages. A hierarchical parallelization strategy and graphics processing unit (GPU) acceleration deliver near-ideal strong scaling to thousands of GPUs, enabling accurate excited-state simulations of systems with more than a thousand atoms. Representative applications, spanning the full optical cycle of solid-state spin defects, self-trapped excitons in metal-halide perovskites, and the optical response of liquid water and ice, demonstrate the accuracy and versatility of the code across diverse material classes. The capabilities implemented in WEST establish the code as a scalable platform for predictive excited-state simulations, high-throughput materials discovery, and the generation of high-fidelity datasets for machine learning in computational materials science.

title: The PSR J0435+3233 Triple System
summary: Abstract The detailed evolution of triple star systems is complicated and poorly known. Using archived optical/infrared and gamma-ray data, we identified the pulsar PSR J0435+3233 as a gamma-ray pulsar in a hierarchical triple system, with
content: Abstract The detailed evolution of triple star systems is complicated and poorly known. Using archived optical/infrared and gamma-ray data, we identified the pulsar PSR J0435+3233 as a gamma-ray pulsar in a hierarchical triple system, with a helium white dwarf (WD) as a close inner binary companion and a Sun-like star as the distant tertiary. PSR J0435+3233 and the WD companion are in a circular orbit with a period of P orb1 = 8.0 days and an eccentricity of e = 0.00016. The tertiary is a G-type subgiant with a mass of 0.98(12) M ⊙ at a distance of 2.1(4) kpc from the Earth. By simultaneously fitting the observed spin-period variations of the gamma-ray emission (over 16.7 yr) and radio emission (over 4.9 yr) from PSR J0435+3233, the changes in the inner orbital parameters, the Shapiro delay, Gaia astrometry, and the outer companion mass, we determined the outer elliptical orbit for the tertiary, with a period P orb2 = 73.5 yr and an eccentricity e 2 = 0.598. The outer orbit is either nearly perpendicular to the inner orbit with a mutual inclination of ∼85 ∘ , or moderately inclined by ∼54 ∘ . For the former geometry, the pulsar, the WD, and the tertiary star have masses of 1.16(5) M ⊙ , 0.273(8) M ⊙ , and 0.91(5) M ⊙ , respectively; for the latter geometry, the corresponding masses are 1.34(15) M ⊙ , 0.305(23) M ⊙ , and 1.13(7) M ⊙ . This is a unique triple system for detailed multiband observations and for studying the evolutionary path and dynamic processes of a primordial triple star system. It will ultimately evolve into a system consisting of a neutron star and two WDs.

title: Performance and prospects of polyurethane-based scintillators for neutron and gamma radiation detection
summary: Organic scintillators have been used for decades to detect gamma rays or fast neutrons at low cost. Despite extensive efforts it is still difficult to combine stability, ruggedness, high light yield, and decent pulse-shape discrimination (P
content: Organic scintillators have been used for decades to detect gamma rays or fast neutrons at low cost. Despite extensive efforts it is still difficult to combine stability, ruggedness, high light yield, and decent pulse-shape discrimination (PSD) in a single scintillator material. We took the unusual approach of embedding phosphors and wavelengths shifters in a solid polyurethane matrix, trying to combine the robustness of a common construction material with scintillating properties and PSD performance. The plastic scintillators resulting from years of research ultimately meet these intentions. Moreover, the production process is less demanding and less complex than that of conventional plastic scintillators. It allows to directly integrate light sensors or electronics into the scintillator. This opens the door for the construction of extremely compact and robust plastic detectors for the simultaneous detection of fast neutrons and gamma rays. This paper presents basic recipes and properties of scintillators based on this novel conception and discusses first applications in neutron imaging and personal radiation protection.

title: Bromide-mediated enhancement of far-UVC/peracetic acid process for selective micropollutant abatement
summary: Abstract Far‑ultraviolet 222 nm (UV 222 ) effectively activates oxidants to degrade organic micropollutants (OMPs) in advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), but its synergy and ecotoxicity with bromide (Br − ) are unclear. This study investig
content: Abstract Far‑ultraviolet 222 nm (UV 222 ) effectively activates oxidants to degrade organic micropollutants (OMPs) in advanced oxidation processes (AOPs), but its synergy and ecotoxicity with bromide (Br − ) are unclear. This study investigates the synergy of peracetic acid (PAA) and Br − by UV 222 (UV 222 -PB) for OMPs degradation. The system’s fluence-based rate constant for model pollutants (0.0159 cm 2 ·mJ −1 ) is 3.01 and 15.74 times that of UV 254 -PB and UV 365 -PB. Radical and theoretical analyses show that far‑ultraviolet strengthens the interaction between PAA and Br − , prolongs radical chains, and boosts organic radicals and reactive bromine species, dominating electron‑rich OMPs oxidation. Correlations of ln( k obs ) with vertical ionization potential and highest occupied molecular orbital energy for 10 OMPs confirm selective oxidation. UV 222 -PB performs robustly in various water matrices and shows low ecotoxicity in assays such as seed germination and zebrafish embryo. Life cycle assessment confirms its sustainability. These findings offer insights and guidance for UV 222 -based AOPs in brominated water treatment.

title: [CII] as a global cold gas tracer in novel hydrodynamical simulations
summary: ̧ii emission is a powerful probe of the gas content in galaxies, especially at early stages of evolution. Given its low excitation potential, the ̧ii 158 μm line is the main coolant of neutral gas in photodissociation regions and giant mole
content: ̧ii emission is a powerful probe of the gas content in galaxies, especially at early stages of evolution. Given its low excitation potential, the ̧ii 158 μm line is the main coolant of neutral gas in photodissociation regions and giant molecular clouds, and hence a tracer of all phases of the interstellar medium. However, there is no consensus on the nature of the gas traced by this emission. We aim to provide insights into the physics of the ̧ii emission and predictions for future observations. We used four pre-prepared simulations performed with a version of which includes the ̨rome chemistry package. We implemented a post-processing semi-analytical model to simulate the ̧ii emission. We analysed an isolated Milky Way-mass-size galaxy, and three merger configurations: a co-rotating, counter-rotating, and perpendicular major merger of two Milky Way-mass-size galaxies. We reproduce fundamental relations such as the ̧ii luminosity and the star formation rate, łcii-SFR relation, in which mergers show an extra component for the ̧ii emission not traced by the star formation alone. During quiescent or starburst stages, galaxies deviate from the łcii-SFR relation. We find that in our simulations ̧ii is a robust tracer of molecular gas, as well as atomic gas in both cold and warm phases on a global scale. Our results indicate that around 50 percent of the total ̧ii emission is traced by molecular gas, while 30 to 40 percent is traced by atomic and ionised hydrogen regardless of the initial configuration of the merger simulation. Our findings suggest that the nature of the ̧ii emission depends strongly on the merger history of galaxies, in which mergers and starbursts can act as more efficient drivers of ̧ii emission through collisions with molecular hydrogen.

title: All-Optical Control of Interfacial Polarization in MoS2/WSe2 Heterobilayers
summary: Abstract All-optical tuning of van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures with coherent radiation offers a powerful strategy for manipulating interfacial electronic properties on femtosecond time scales. Using real-time time-dependent density fun
content: Abstract All-optical tuning of van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures with coherent radiation offers a powerful strategy for manipulating interfacial electronic properties on femtosecond time scales. Using real-time time-dependent density functional theory, we predict a transient out-of-plane polarization in MoS2/WSe2 heterobilayers driven by intense ultrafast pulses. In the weak-field regime, the system preserves its intrinsic type-II band alignment, whereas at intermediate intensities, the field triggers a nonlinear enhancement of interlayer charge transfer. High-harmonic generation spectra undergo a crossover from the perturbative to the strong-field regime accompanied by the pronounced enhancement of a photoinduced interfacial dipole. At the highest intensities, interlayer polarization enhancement is sustained by massive field-driven spatial delocalization of electronic density into the vdW gap, promoted by localized charge saturation due to Pauli blocking. Lattice strain modifies the resonance conditions while preserving this strong-field polarization enhancement, establishing a microscopic mechanism for all-optical manipulation of interfacial dipoles at the ultrafast timescale.

title: Pollinator risks and recovery from air pollutant interactions during the fossil‐fuel transition
source: Frontiers in Ecology and the Environment
summary: By altering the composition and concentration of floral scents, air pollutants such as ozone (O 3 ) and nitrogen oxides (NO x ) disrupt the ability of insect pollinators to locate flowers, threatening biodiversity and crop production. We ex
content: By altering the composition and concentration of floral scents, air pollutants such as ozone (O 3 ) and nitrogen oxides (NO x ) disrupt the ability of insect pollinators to locate flowers, threatening biodiversity and crop production. We examine the impact of these pollutants on pollinator performance and evaluate the short‐ and long‐term consequences of transitioning away from fossil fuels by considering the effects of multiple pollutants in combination. Although O 3 and NO x individually impair pollinator foraging, our supporting meta‐analysis reveals a sub‐additive effect when they occur together. Under a middle‐of‐the‐road emissions scenario (SSP2‐4.5), tropospheric O 3 levels are projected to rise until mid‐century, intensifying stress on pollinators. Beyond 2050, O 3 levels are expected to decline as the transition to clean energy reduces emissions of precursors like NO x . Pollinator recovery rate will depend on the emissions pathway followed and how effective policies are in cutting NO x and other ozone‐precursor emissions. This work connects improvements in air quality to the stability of global ecosystems and builds on previous reviews by quantifying pollutant interactions and providing actionable insights for policymaking .

title: Chromogranin A-phosphatidic acid association coordinates late stages of regulated exocytosis
summary: Chromogranin A is a major component of secretory granules that contributes to granule biogenesis, cargo organization and regulated secretion in neuroendocrine cells. We previously identified a phosphatidic acid (PA)-binding domain (PABD) wi
content: Chromogranin A is a major component of secretory granules that contributes to granule biogenesis, cargo organization and regulated secretion in neuroendocrine cells. We previously identified a phosphatidic acid (PA)-binding domain (PABD) within CgA that promotes secretory granule formation by remodeling trans-Golgi network membranes. Here, we investigate whether this lipid-protein association also contributes to the late stages of regulated exocytosis. Using fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy combined with Förster resonance energy transfer, we find that CgA undergoes a stimulation-dependent association with PA at exocytic sites in living cells. Immunofluorescence and electron microscopy further show that CgA remains transiently associated with fused secretory granule membranes. Functional analyses reveal that disruption of the PABD alters secretory granule exocytosis by accelerating CgA release, modifying quantal catecholamine release and fusion pore dynamics, and changing the early kinetics of secretory granule membrane retrieval. Together, these findings support a model in which the CgA/PA association is not restricted to secretory granule biogenesis but also contributes to the temporal coordination of multiple post-fusion events during regulated secretion. This work identifies a lipid-protein interaction that links distinct stages of the secretory granule life cycle in neuroendocrine cells. Chromogranin A binds phosphatidic acid at exocytic sites, coordinating secretion beyond granule formation. Disrupting this interaction alters cargo release, fusion pore dynamics, and membrane retrieval, linking distinct stages of the secretory granule life cycle.

title: The JWST Proto-PAH project: Aromatic backbones with extensive aliphatic substitution account for both the aromatic and aliphatic emission
summary: We find that the aromatic and aliphatic emission bands in four carbon-rich post-asymptotic giant branch stars with class D emission arise from a single carrier population: extensive aliphatic decoration of an aromatic skeleton, i.e. molecul
content: We find that the aromatic and aliphatic emission bands in four carbon-rich post-asymptotic giant branch stars with class D emission arise from a single carrier population: extensive aliphatic decoration of an aromatic skeleton, i.e. molecules with a coherent aromatic backbone and an unusually high aliphatic content. This conclusion is based on JWST NIRSpec and MIRI/MRS spectroscopy, covering 2.88--28.7 The aliphatic 3.4 feature is stronger than the aromatic 3.3 feature, reversing the ratio seen in sources with typical polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) emission. If the aromatic emission arose from nominal PAHs, the 3.3 feature -- unavailable in previous observations -- together with the mid-infrared aromatic features, would constrain them to be large (≳200 carbon atoms), compact, and at least partially ionized. These properties predict a strong 8.6 feature. However, the 8.6 feature is weak or absent in all four sources, ruling out PAHs as the source of the aromatic emission. Instead, the emission must arise from the same carriers as the aliphatic emission. The position of the 6.9 feature and the broadened 11–14 out-of-plane emission independently support this. The and feature strengths vary across the sample, with the class D2 sources showing higher content. These carriers are far more aliphatic than the PAHs of planetary nebulae and the interstellar medium. However, they retain the aromatic skeleton that produces their aromatic features.

title: Direct P K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy evidence of phosphorus immobilization in anoxic peat soils
summary: Abstract. Rewetting of drained agricultural peatlands is widely promoted to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions, yet concerns remain that reductive dissolution of Fe(III) (hydr)oxides may mobilize bound phosphorus (P) and increase eutrophicat
content: Abstract. Rewetting of drained agricultural peatlands is widely promoted to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions, yet concerns remain that reductive dissolution of Fe(III) (hydr)oxides may mobilize bound phosphorus (P) and increase eutrophication risk. However, P concentrations following rewetting can vary by orders of magnitude among peatlands, and the processes controlling this variation remain unclear. In this study, we investigated the mechanisms controlling P retention in a rewetted fen (Løvenborg, Denmark) using synchrotron-based P K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and µ-X-ray fluorescence (µ-XRF), bulk soil chemistry, selective extractions, and porewater analyses. The study site is characterized by near-neutral pH (6.8–7.2), elevated calcium (Ca) concentrations (~ 0.5 mM), and substantial pools of ~200 mmol oxalate extractable Fe and Al. Fe(III) reduction reached up to 79% of the oxalate-extractable Fe pool, yet dissolved P remained below detection limits (< 0.1 µM) in all samples, demonstrating a clear decoupling between Fe(III) reduction and P release. Calculated mobilized P greatly exceeded measured porewater P, indicating rapid re-immobilization within the soil matrix. Bulk P K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra were similar under oxic and anoxic conditions and were dominated by organic and Fe/Al-associated P, with no clear bulk evidence of vivianite or hydroxyapatite. In contrast, µ-XANES data collected from hotspots of P identified using µ-XRF revealed localized domains of Fe- and Al-associated P together with Ca phosphates and vivianite-like Fe(II) phosphate phases that are not observed in bulk spectra. Thermodynamic modeling shows strong supersaturation with respect to vivianite and weaker supersaturation for Ca-P. The results of this study imply that P dynamics in neutral, Ca-rich peat soils are governed by microscale mineralogical heterogeneity that is not captured by bulk analytical techniques, suggesting that conventional Fe-based or bulk redox indicators may overestimate P release following peatland rewetting.

title: Global Justice Index Report 2025
summary: Abstract Global Justice Index, whose most results are presented here, is an ongoing, multiyear research project based at the Fudan Institute for Advanced Study in Social Sciences to assess countries’ contributions to and performance in the
content: Abstract Global Justice Index, whose most results are presented here, is an ongoing, multiyear research project based at the Fudan Institute for Advanced Study in Social Sciences to assess countries’ contributions to and performance in the advancement of global justice. Building on the conceptual framework and measurement methodology that have been developed in previous reports of the project, the Global Justice Index Report 2025 presents the seventh annual assessment, drawing on country-level data for 2023. This report evaluates global justice across ten issue areas: climate change, peacekeeping, humanitarian aid, terrorism and armed conflicts, cross-national criminal governance, refugees, anti-poverty efforts, education, public health, and the protection of women and children. The indicators for these issues are selected and assessed with reference to the principles of the Common but Differentiated and Respective Capabilities and Cosmopolitan but Due-diligent Responsibilities. This report provides country rankings, regional comparisons, thematic analyses, and policy implications for each of the issue areas. To assess uneven data availability, it reports two versions of the Global Justice Index: a nine-issue index that covers 156 countries and excludes anti-poverty, and a 10-issue index that covers 142 countries. Both of these indices are calculated using the equal-weight geometric mean of the scores for their constituent issues. In the results, the United States, China, Germany, Japan, and several European countries occupy the leading positions in both versions of the index. Europe and North America continue to be the strongest performers as regions, and many of the lowest-ranked countries are concentrated in Sub-Saharan Africa and in the fragile states in Oceania and Asia. The findings highlight persistent regional disparities, the importance of building comprehensive state capacity, and the growing interdependence of different dimensions of global justice in a period that has been marked by armed conflict, climate-related disasters, economic pressures, and geopolitical fragmentation. This report concludes by discussing the policy applications and methodological limitations of the index, as well as identifying directions for improving data quality, measurement, and future global justice research.

title: Bio-VQVAE: multivariate and multi-scale time-series generation for bioprocess data augmentation
summary: Biomanufacturing digitalization relies heavily on data-driven modeling, yet the scarcity of high-quality labeled data remains a bottleneck. Multivariate fermentation data exhibit temporal patterns at multiple scales and complex statistical
content: Biomanufacturing digitalization relies heavily on data-driven modeling, yet the scarcity of high-quality labeled data remains a bottleneck. Multivariate fermentation data exhibit temporal patterns at multiple scales and complex statistical dependencies among process-state and operational variables. Current time-series generation methods often have difficulty preserving multi-scale temporal patterns and statistical dependencies among process variables. This paper proposes Bio-VQVAE, a generative framework designed to improve the representation of these characteristics in a vector-quantized latent space. We introduce a Large Selective Kernel mechanism to adaptively capture temporal patterns at different scales by dynamically adjusting the effective receptive field. Furthermore, an Efficient Multi-Scale Attention module is integrated to enhance cross-dimensional feature interaction and facilitate the empirical learning of dependencies among process variables. Evaluation on the IndPenSim benchmark shows that Bio-VQVAE achieves the lowest mean values across all four quantitative metrics among the evaluated baseline models. Notably, the method achieves superior fidelity in preserving multivariate correlation structures and temporal autocorrelation consistency, even under constrained data regimes. These results demonstrate the potential of Bio-VQVAE for in-distribution augmentation of multivariate bioprocess time series and for supporting downstream predictive modeling.

title: Acid Mine Drainage Treatment Using a Sulfidogenic Bioreactor and Selective Two-step Precipitation of Multiple Metal(loid)s
summary: Abstract This study investigated the treatment of acid mine drainage (AMD) and the precipitation of metals and metalloids using sulfur species delivered in gaseous and liquid forms. An up-flow sulfidogenic reactor was operated for 58 days t
content: Abstract This study investigated the treatment of acid mine drainage (AMD) and the precipitation of metals and metalloids using sulfur species delivered in gaseous and liquid forms. An up-flow sulfidogenic reactor was operated for 58 days to obtain stable sulfate-reducing conditions. Under the final operating conditions, the bioreactor reached maximum sulfate and COD removal efficiencies of 95% and 92%, respectively, with peak alkalinity and sulfide concentrations of ≈ 2010 mg CaCO₃/L and 326 mg/L. Using the generated sulfide and alkalinity, precipitation tests were conducted on a synthetic AMD solution containing various metal(loids) (Fe, Pb, Zn, Cu, Ni, Sn, Co, Cr, Cd, V, Mn, Sb, As, and Se), with H 2 S gas and HS⁻/HCO 3 ⁻ liquid phases as the precipitating agents. Consequently, Pb, Sn, As, Cu, and Se precipitated at low pH via H 2 S gas, while Zn, Cd, Fe, Co, and Ni precipitated at high pH via HS⁻/HCO 3 ⁻ liquid phases. XRD analysis of the precipitates obtained from the liquid-phase sulfide process at a pH of 5.5 ± 0.2 revealed distinct 2θ peaks between 35° and 65°, confirming the presence of Zn, Ni, Co, and Fe in the precipitates. The results of this study demonstrate that sulfidogenic reactors are an effective tools for both the remediation of AMD and the selective precipitation of metals and metalloids.

title: Ultra‐Sensitive, Decoupled Multimodal Sensing via Dual‐Network Iontronic Organohydrogels
summary: ABSTRACT Flexible sensors capable of mimicking human skin's multimodal perception are highly desired for wearable electronics. However, achieving inherently decoupled detection of multiple physical stimuli in a single device remains a funda
content: ABSTRACT Flexible sensors capable of mimicking human skin's multimodal perception are highly desired for wearable electronics. However, achieving inherently decoupled detection of multiple physical stimuli in a single device remains a fundamental challenge. Here, a polyacrylamide/polyvinyl alcohol/glycerol/calcium chloride (PAM/PVA/Gly/CaCl 2 , PPGC) dual‐network ionic organohydrogel is integrated into a stacked architecture that physically separates capacitive pressure sensing from resistive temperature and strain sensing, enabling inherent signal decoupling. The dual‐network structure, together with Gly‐induced hydrogen bonding, endows the organohydrogel with robust mechanical properties, anti‐drying capability, and self‐healing behavior. The capacitive pressure sensor achieves an ultrahigh sensitivity of 9426 kPa −1 in the low‐pressure regime and response/recovery times as fast as 20 ms. The resistive temperature sensor exhibits a linear response from 20°C to 100°C with a temperature coefficient of resistance of −0.269°C −1 . Cross‐decoupling experiments confirm negligible interference between pressure and temperature signals. Practical demonstrations include gesture recognition using a five‐channel array, real‐time breath monitoring for apnea screening, and spatial mapping of simultaneous pressure and temperature stimuli with a 4 × 4 sensor array. This strategy provides a promising platform for advanced wearable health monitoring and human‐machine interaction.

title: Möbius Kekulene
summary: Encoding prescribed topologies in rigid conjugated frameworks offers a route to tuning electronic properties but is constrained by severe geometric strain. We synthesized and isolated Möbius kekulene, a compact, all-benzenoid double-strande
content: Encoding prescribed topologies in rigid conjugated frameworks offers a route to tuning electronic properties but is constrained by severe geometric strain. We synthesized and isolated Möbius kekulene, a compact, all-benzenoid double-stranded counterpart of planar kekulene. Its synthesis was enabled by strain-trajectory programming, in which precursor connectivity is designed to control strain accumulation during cyclization. Comparison of two precursors revealed contrasting strain trajectories: MCP1 concentrated the torsional deformation into an inaccessible late-stage closure, whereasMCP2 accommodated deformation progressively, reducing the largest strain increment and affording Möbius kekulene 1. Crystallography confirms a singly twisted topology with a calculated strain energy of 73.9 kcal/mol per twist, highest among reported Möbius π-systems. Despite pronounced distortion, 1 retains a Clar-type localized electronic structure analogous to planar kekulene, with local aromaticity progressively perturbed toward the twist region. These results establish strain-trajectory programming as a design principle for accessing highly constrained molecular topologies.

title: Reverse coprecipitation synthesis of rock-salt-type high-entropy oxide (MgCoNiCuZn)O for high-performance asymmetric supercapacitors
summary: Abstract High-entropy oxides (HEOs) have attracted significant attention in diverse fields because of their unique crystal structures and tunable chemical compositions, making them promising candidates for advanced electrochemical energy st
content: Abstract High-entropy oxides (HEOs) have attracted significant attention in diverse fields because of their unique crystal structures and tunable chemical compositions, making them promising candidates for advanced electrochemical energy storage. In this study, a rock-salt-type high-entropy oxide, (MgCoNiCuZn)O, was synthesized by a reverse coprecipitation method. The effects of precipitant dosage and calcination temperature on the average particle size of the resulting HEO powder were systematically investigated. Electrochemical characterization revealed that the asprepared HEO electrode delivered a specific capacitance of 660 F g -1 at a current density of 1 A g -1 , indicating favorable ion-transport properties. An asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) assembled using this material operated within an optimal voltage window of 0-1.5 V and achieved a specific capacitance of 253 F g -1 at 1 A g -1 . The device also exhibited an energy density of 79 Wh kg -1 at a power density of 749 W kg -1 and a maximum power density of 7500 W kg -1 . These findings highlight the potential of reverse coprecipitation for synthesizing HEOs with promising performance as supercapacitor electrode materials.

title: Strain-engineered piezo-phototronic interface modulation in flexible GaN/monolayer MoS2 heterostructures
summary: A flexible, strain-mediated, and photo-responsive device based on a heterostructure comprising a chemical vapor deposition (CVD)-grown MoS 2 monolayer and metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD)-grown GaN films is fabricated. By int
content: A flexible, strain-mediated, and photo-responsive device based on a heterostructure comprising a chemical vapor deposition (CVD)-grown MoS 2 monolayer and metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD)-grown GaN films is fabricated. By integrating the distinct piezo-phototronic properties of GaN with the excellent carrier transport characteristics of MoS 2 , the device exhibits a synergistic response to both mechanical strain and optical excitation. Under compressive and tensile strain, piezo-polarization charges generated in the GaN layer effectively modulate interfacial charge transport at the MoS 2 monolayer, leading to significantly enhanced sensing performance. The device achieves ultrahigh gauge factors of 2224 and 3349 at a compressive strain of −0.25% under halogen and UV illumination, respectively, corresponding to ~11.1 and ~11.7 times higher sensitivity than standard metallic stain gauges. Furthermore, it demonstrates rapid electro-opto-mechanical responses, detecting halogen and UV irradiation with response and recovery times of 186/84 ms and 83/53 ms, respectively, under −0.25% compressive strain. These results reveal strong coupling between strain-induced polarization and photoexcited carrier dynamics at the nanoscale interface. This work provides new insights into strain-engineered interfacial charge modulation in low-dimensional heterostructures and establishes a promising platform for multifunctional, self-powered, ultra-sensitive and active flexible optoelectronics.

title: Spatiotemporal Regulation of Hierarchical Assembly of Hydroxyapatite for Enamel Remineralization
summary: The hierarchical structure of tooth enamel confers exceptional mechanical robustness, yet its biomimetic regeneration remains a significant challenge. We develop an enzymatic mineralization system (EMS) that achieves enamel regeneration by
content: The hierarchical structure of tooth enamel confers exceptional mechanical robustness, yet its biomimetic regeneration remains a significant challenge. We develop an enzymatic mineralization system (EMS) that achieves enamel regeneration by directing the hierarchical assembly of hydroxyapatite (HAP). Within the EMS, the alkaline phosphatase hydrolyzes β-glycerophosphate (β-GP), triggering the mineralization reaction of calcium phosphate (CaP) and controlling its structural evolution. The mineralization process is characterized by a series of spatiotemporal events, in which CaP prenucleation clusters initially form and transform into HAP nanorod building blocks; these units then hierarchically self-assemble into microscale crystalline bundles that resemble native enamel rods. Mechanistically, differential adsorption of β-GP on the (100) and (002) facets of HAP, together with facet-dependent enzymatic cleavage of surface-bound β-GP, generates high-energy facets and interfacial energy differences that drive the hierarchical assembly, beginning with c-axis-oriented attachment followed by lateral aggregation. Extending this new strategy to enamel remineralization, the EMS restores the native microstructure and essential mechanical properties. Moreover, a hydrogel-based EMS demonstrates clinical translatability through effective in vivo repair. This paradigm of interfacial energy-modulated assembly provides a robust blueprint for the bottom-up construction of complex, high-performance biomimetic materials.

title: Study on Thermal Properties and Crystallization Behavior of Silica‐Modified Polyetheretherketone Composites
summary: ABSTRACT This study employs KH560 to surface‐modify nano‐SiO 2 , which is then melt‐blended with PEEK to prepare composites with loadings of 0–7 phr. At 3 phr, the melting temperature rose to 348.5°C, the melting enthalpy reached a maximum
content: ABSTRACT This study employs KH560 to surface‐modify nano‐SiO 2 , which is then melt‐blended with PEEK to prepare composites with loadings of 0–7 phr. At 3 phr, the melting temperature rose to 348.5°C, the melting enthalpy reached a maximum of 80.33 J g −1 , and the corrected crystallinity remained comparable to that of pure PEEK, while the filler dispersion was the most uniform. Concurrently, the water contact angle decreased from 81.7° to 70.6°–72.8°, thermal conductivity increased substantially, and the dielectric breakdown strength nearly doubled, reaching ≈24.7 kV mm −1 at 5 phr. Compared with the higher loadings commonly reported in the literature, significant multi‐property improvements were achieved at only 3–5 phr. These results demonstrate that KH560 surface modification effectively enhances the thermal, crystallization, dielectric, and surface performance of PEEK at low filler contents.

title: Sensitivity-Based Performance Optimisation of a Lead-Free Formamidinium Tin Iodide (Fasni3) Perovskite Solar Cell Using Scaps-1d Simulation
summary: This work presents a design and simulation framework for the multi-parameter optimization of a lead-free Perovskite Solar Cell (PSC) with an FTO/CeO2/FASnI3/CuI structure. It focuses on the device parameters that influence operational stabi
content: This work presents a design and simulation framework for the multi-parameter optimization of a lead-free Perovskite Solar Cell (PSC) with an FTO/CeO2/FASnI3/CuI structure. It focuses on the device parameters that influence operational stability. Using the Solar Cell Capacitance Simulator One-Dimension (SCAPS-1D) (version 3.3.12), the study first verified the baseline performance of the device. Six parameters, previously optimized for efficiency, were re-evaluated and categorized into fixed design parameters set during fabrication and those susceptible to drift through known FASnI3 degradation pathways. Normalized sensitivity coefficients were then calculated from the simulation sweeps. The results showed a baseline Power Conversion Efficiency (PCE) of 22.04%, an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.9843V, a short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 26.01 mA/cm², and a fill factor (FF) of 86.12%. Following multi-parameter optimisation of bandgap, absorber thickness, and back-contact work function, the device achieved an optimised PCE of 24.85%, with a Voc of 0.9307 V, a Jsc of 30.65 mA/cm², and an FF of 87.10%. Sensitivity analysis revealed that electron affinity is the most influential factor on PCE, with roughly 19 percentage points per eV, followed by acceptor density (about 0.57 percentage points per decade) and defect density (around 0.20 percentage points per decade). The study highlights interfacial electron affinity control as a priority for enhancing device stability, since among the parameters examined PCE proved most sensitive to drift in electron affinity; defect density, however, remains the parameter most likely to drift in practice through the known Sn²⁺ oxidation pathway.

title: Optimal dietary glycerol monolaurate supplementation improves growth performance, antioxidant capacity, immune responses and intestinal microbiota in juvenile largemouth bass
summary: Introduction Plant-derived functional additives have gained increasing attention as sustainable alternatives in aquafeed. This study aims to investigate the effects of dietary monolaurin on productive performance, innate immune indicators,
content: Introduction Plant-derived functional additives have gained increasing attention as sustainable alternatives in aquafeed. This study aims to investigate the effects of dietary monolaurin on productive performance, innate immune indicators, antioxidative effects, and gut flora in largemouth bass ( Micropterus salmoides ). Methods Fish were fed diets containing 0, 500, 800, 1100, and 1400 mg/kg GML for 56 days, with three replicates per treatment. Results The results showed that GML supplementation significantly improved growth performance. Final body weight was higher in the 800 and 1100 mg/kg groups, while weight gain rate and specific growth rate peaked at 800 mg/kg. Whole-body crude lipid content decreased in the 500 and 800 mg/kg groups, whereas crude protein content increased across all GML-supplemented groups. GML also enhanced antioxidant capacity by increasing total antioxidant capacity and catalase and superoxide dismutase activities while reducing malondialdehyde levels. Serum acid phosphatase and alkaline phosphatase activities peaked in the 800 and 1100 mg/kg groups. The expression levels of il6 and tnfa were significantly downregulated in the 800 and 1100 mg/kg groups, while those of tgfb1a and il22 were significantly upregulated. Intestinal microbiota analysis revealed that GML reshaped the gut microbial community. The relative abundances of Aeromonas and Pseudomonas decreased at 800–1400 mg/kg, whereas those of Cetobacterium and Bacteroides increased at 800 mg/kg and 1100 mg/kg. Regression analysis based on final body weight estimated the optimal dietary GML level at 750 mg/kg. Discussion These findings indicate that appropriate dietary GML supplementation can promote growth while improving antioxidant status, selected innate immune responses, and intestinal microbial balance in largemouth bass. Thus, GML may serve as a promising plant-derived functional feed additive in largemouth bass aquaculture.

title: Polarization-Driven Hydride Transfer Promotes Cobalt Tetrasulfophthalocyanine-Catalyzed Hydrogen Evolution by Five Orders of Magnitude
summary: The hydricity of M–H intermediates is a key descriptor and optimization target for the rational design of molecular hydrogen evolution electrocatalysts. Adsorption to an electrode surface is known to augment catalytic rate, but it remains u
content: The hydricity of M–H intermediates is a key descriptor and optimization target for the rational design of molecular hydrogen evolution electrocatalysts. Adsorption to an electrode surface is known to augment catalytic rate, but it remains unclear how adsorption affects M-H hydricity. Herein, we quantitatively compare the catalytic activity and mechanism of the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) from cobalt tetrasulfophthalocyanine (CoTSPc) in a dissolved aqueous form (CoTSPc (aq) ) and when adsorbed to the surface of a carbon electrode (CoTSPc/C). At the same electrode potential, CoTSPc/C catalyzes HER at a rate that is over five orders of magnitude faster than CoTSPc (aq) . Mechanistic studies indicate that both CoTSPc/C and CoTSPc (aq) catalyze HER via a rate-limiting hydride transfer to a proton donor in solution to form H 2 . Hydride transfer from Co-H in CoTSPc (aq) is a purely chemical step defined by a constant hydricity of 22.4 kcal mol −1 that is independent of applied potential. In contrast, hydride transfer from Co-H in CoTSPc/C is strongly polarization dependent, decreasing hydricity by ~23 kcal mol −1 V −1 to values as low as 1.2 kcal mol −1 at −1.1 V vs SHE, leading to the observed rate promotion. We attribute this mechanistic change to the positioning of the CoTSPc-H intermediate within the electrochemical double layer, such that the hydride traverses the interfacial electrostatic potential difference during the RLS. These results demonstrate the power of surface adsorption to generate highly reactive molecular hydrides and fundamentally reshape the free energy landscape of electrocatalysis.

title: UV Index monitoring and forecasting in Cyprus: the effect of ozone, aerosols and clouds
summary: Abstract. Surface ultraviolet (UV) radiation is strongly influenced by clouds, aerosols, and total column ozone, making accurate operational forecasting challenging in regions with highly variable atmospheric conditions. This study evaluate
content: Abstract. Surface ultraviolet (UV) radiation is strongly influenced by clouds, aerosols, and total column ozone, making accurate operational forecasting challenging in regions with highly variable atmospheric conditions. This study evaluates UV Index (UVI) variability and forecasting over Cyprus using more than one year of observations from a five-station ground-based monitoring network. Spectral measurements from a Bentham spectroradiometer were combined with broadband UV observations, all-sky imagery, AERONET aerosol measurements, and satellite ozone products to evaluate the regional Cyprus Erythemal Radiation Forecasting System (CERYFOS) and the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) corresponding product. Ground-based observations showed a strong seasonal cycle across Cyprus, together with regional differences associated with altitude and local atmospheric variability, particularly at the mountainous Kyperounda station. Both forecasting systems reproduced observed UVI well under typical atmospheric conditions. For the all sky conditions, CERYFOS and CAMS achieved RMSE values of 0.72 and 0.60 UVI, respectively, decreasing to 0.47 and 0.40 UVI under clear-sky cases. In contrast, performance deteriorated under cloudy conditions, with RMSE increasing to 1.65 and 1.12 UVI, respectively, identifying cloud representation as a major source of forecast uncertainty. Ozone-related uncertainties generally produced relatively small UVI deviations, whereas aerosol errors became increasingly important under enhanced aerosol loading, as particularly evident during the 23–24 July 2025 wildfire, underestimated aerosol loading resulted in forecast errors exceeding 4 UVI units. These results demonstrate the importance of accurate cloud and aerosol representation and coordinated ground-based observations for improving operational UVI forecasting in the Eastern Mediterranean.

title: Hierarchical Organization Modulates Transient Thermal Relaxation Dynamics in Chitinous Cuticles from Marine and Terrestrial Organisms
summary: Abstract Chitinous cuticles are hierarchical biological composites in which the molecular organization spans multiple structural length scales. Although the relationships between chitin chemistry and mechanical performance have been extensi
content: Abstract Chitinous cuticles are hierarchical biological composites in which the molecular organization spans multiple structural length scales. Although the relationships between chitin chemistry and mechanical performance have been extensively investigated, the structural factors governing transient thermal relaxation remain poorly understood. In particular, it remains unclear whether localized thermal dissipation in biological cuticles can be predicted from the molecular composition alone. Here, we investigate transient thermal relaxation in hydrothermal tubeworm cuticles, purified tubeworm chitin, and terrestrial beetle cuticles using time-resolved photothermal measurements correlated with Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and structural analyses with wide-angle X-ray scattering. Despite exhibiting broadly similar chemical signatures, the investigated cuticles display markedly different thermal accumulation, heat dissipation kinetics, and relaxation behaviors under localized laser excitation. By comparing thermal responses of the chitinous samples from marine and terrestrial organisms and the native versus protein-renovelled samples, we found that transient thermal relaxation cannot be predicted from molecular composition alone but emerges from hierarchical organization across multiple structural levels.

title: Sub-4 nm Pt5Sm Intermetallic Catalyst toward Efficient and Durable Oxygen Reduction for Fuel Cell Applications
summary: It is remarkably attractive but challenging to develop fine Pt-rare-earth intermetallic catalysts toward efficient and stable oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) for fuel cell applications. In this work, an amino-assisted method was employed to
content: It is remarkably attractive but challenging to develop fine Pt-rare-earth intermetallic catalysts toward efficient and stable oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) for fuel cell applications. In this work, an amino-assisted method was employed to prepare the carbon-supported Pt5Sm (Pt5Sm/C) catalyst, which exhibited an average size of 3.8 ± 1.0 nm with a core-shell structure consisting of a Pt-enriched surface over a hexagonal Pt5Sm intermetallic core. The introduction of Sm into the Pt lattice induced strong electron interactions between Sm and Pt and enhanced the resistance to Pt oxidation, thereby improving the catalytic kinetics and durability for the ORR. In rotating disk electrode tests, the Pt5Sm/C catalyst delivers a promising ORR activity of 430.3 A·gPt-1 with only a 10.3% loss after 30,000 cycles, significantly outperforming commercial Pt/C. Furthermore, in H2/air fuel cell tests, the Pt5Sm/C catalyst exhibited a peak power density of 853 mW·cm-2 with only a voltage drop of 56 mV at 0.8 A·cm-2 after 30,000 cycles. This work demonstrates that Pt-rare-earth intermetallic catalysts are promising candidates for high-performance and durable fuel cell applications.

title: Upgrading Oil Palm Empty Fruit Bunch Bio Oil via Catalytic Hydrodeoxygenation Using Nickel Impregnated Activated Carbon and Natural Zeolite Catalysts
source: Indonesian Journal of Environmental Management and Sustainability
summary: Biomass is a promising alternative energy feedstock because of its cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin content and its availability as an agricultural and plantation residue. Pyrolysis can convert biomass into bio-oil, a complex liquid con
content: Biomass is a promising alternative energy feedstock because of its cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin content and its availability as an agricultural and plantation residue. Pyrolysis can convert biomass into bio-oil, a complex liquid containing oxygenated compounds such as ketones, acids, phenols, alcohols, aldehydes, and hydrocarbons. This study evaluates the upgrading of crude bio oil (CBO) derived from oil palm empty fruit bunches (EFB) using nickel impregnated activated natural zeolite (ZAA/Ni) and nickel-impregnated activated carbon (AA/Ni) catalysts under hydrodeoxygenation (HDO) conditions. The physicochemical properties and available GCMS results were compared descriptively before and after upgrading. After correction of the compound classifications and recalculation from the listed GCMS peaks, the hydrocarbon peak-area totals were 20.59% for CBO, 20.36% for ZAA/Ni, and 26.66% for AA/Ni. The AA/Ni-treated bio oilshowed an increase in higher heating value (HHV) from 39.13 to 40.27 MJ/kg. Because the original chromatograms and independent replicate measurements were unavailable for this revision, the GCMS results are interpreted as semi quantitative, and the numerical differences are not presented as statistically significant. Overall, AA/Ni showed the more favorable combination of oxygen removal and HHV improvement under the tested conditions, although the increased viscosity indicates that further stabilization or fractionation would be required before considering diesel-equivalent applications.

title: Multi- p arameter E valuation of M ultilayer G ravity F iltration for S ki- R esort S now melt W ater P retreatment and R e us e
summary: To address the issues of centralized discharge and resource recovery of snowmelt water, a multi-layered gravity filtration system for snowmelt water discharge in ski resorts was developed using filter cotton, activated carbon, quartz sand,
content: To address the issues of centralized discharge and resource recovery of snowmelt water, a multi-layered gravity filtration system for snowmelt water discharge in ski resorts was developed using filter cotton, activated carbon, quartz sand, and gravel. The experiment examined the impact of filter media combinations, filter bed thickness, filtration time, treated water volume, and inflow rate on treatment performance, using various parameters to measure it, including pH, turbidity, suspended solids (SS), color, and conductivity. The findings have shown that the composite filter bed is effective in improving the particulate matter content and visual water quality of the snowmelt water, reducing turbidity from 238.2 NTU to 17.2 NTU (removal rate of 92.8%) and achieving a suspended solids (SS) removal rate of 65.97%. The rates of turbidity and SS removal were 91.5% and 71.35%, respectively, when the quartz sand layer was raised to 6 cm. The choice to reduce the inflow velocity appropriately to enhance SS retention efficiency was effective, but conductivity was not reduced in equal measure to the indicators of particulate matter. The process is mainly applicable in the removal of particulate pollutants and can be used as a pretreatment unit for the non-portable reuse of snowmelt water in ski resorts.

title: Impact of disturbance on spatio-temporal dynamics of carbon dioxide efflux on forest floor in tropical sal forests of the Eastern Ghats
summary: Understanding soil carbon dynamics in tropical forests is essential for developing sustainable forest management strategies and strengthening climate change mitigation efforts. This study examined soil respiration and carbon turnover across
content: Understanding soil carbon dynamics in tropical forests is essential for developing sustainable forest management strategies and strengthening climate change mitigation efforts. This study examined soil respiration and carbon turnover across three moist deciduous sal forest types of the Eastern Ghats, India: pure sal forest (PSF), sal-dominated moist mixed forest (SDMDF), and mixed forest without sal (MDFWS). Seasonal in-situ measurements of total, autotrophic, and heterotrophic soil respiration were conducted across three forest types, along with the measurements of soil temperature, moisture and vegetation attributes. Correlation, regression and principal component analysis (PCA) were used to identify the major environmental and biotic controls of soil respiration and carbon turnover. Seasonal patterns revealed higher soil temperatures during summer and maximum soil moisture during the monsoon period. Soil respiration closely followed moisture availability, reaching peak levels during the monsoon and declining during winter. Among the forest types, MDFWS exhibited the highest mean soil respiration (1.14 g cm −2 d −1 ), followed by SDMDF and PSF. Annual soil carbon efflux ranged from 28.80 to 49.83 Mg C ha −1 y −1 , with autotrophic (root) respiration contributing a greater proportion than heterotrophic respiration. Mean residence time of soil organic carbon was highest in PSF (3.73 years) and lowest in MDFWS (1.09 years), indicating faster carbon turnover in mixed forests lacking sal dominance. Soil respiration was positively associated with soil moisture and tree density, while it showed a negative relationship with soil temperature. Multivariate analyses identified soil moisture as the primary determinant of soil respiration variability, underscoring the critical role of monsoonal precipitation and forest structure in regulating ecosystem carbon fluxes. These findings demonstrate that forest composition and hydrological conditions strongly influence soil carbon dynamics and ecosystem functioning. The study highlights the importance of conserving and sustainably managing tropical sal forests to enhance carbon retention, strengthen climate resilience, and support long-term environmental sustainability and sustainable development goals in forest-dependent landscapes of India.

title: Cysteine-based molecular switches: a focus on KEAP1 and BACH1 in regulating the antioxidant response
summary: Due to the chemical properties of their thiol groups and the surrounding amino acid environment, specific cysteines in proteins serve as the principal intracellular sensors for oxidants and electrophiles. In this review, we focus on the ubi
content: Due to the chemical properties of their thiol groups and the surrounding amino acid environment, specific cysteines in proteins serve as the principal intracellular sensors for oxidants and electrophiles. In this review, we focus on the ubiquitin ligase substrate adaptor Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (KEAP1) and the transcriptional repressor BTB and CNC homology 1 (BACH1) as representative cysteine-based molecular switches, both of which have critical functions in the cellular antioxidant response. KEAP1 is a protein endowed with a number of highly reactive cysteines, which can be covalently and preferentially modified by a wide array of reactive oxygen species, reactive nitrogen species and reactive electrophilic species, from endogenous as well as exogenous origin. Covalent cysteine modifications are also involved in the regulation of the localisation, stability and turnover of BACH1. Both KEAP1 and BACH1 antagonize the constitutively expressed transcription factor NF-E2 p45-related factor 2 (NRF2), the master regulator of the cellular antioxidant response, thus keeping the transcriptional activity of NRF2 low at homeostatic state. Cysteine modifications within KEAP1 and BACH1 render the repressor proteins inactive, resulting in rapid NRF2 activation that does not rely on de novo transcription of NFE2L2, the gene encoding NRF2. Consequently, NRF2 induces the transcriptional upregulation of a large network of genes encoding cytoprotective proteins, many of which have antioxidant functions, restoring the redox homeostasis.

title: Effects of size, shape, and functionalization on the electronic and optical properties of graphene quantum dots
summary: Graphene quantum dots (GQDs) exhibit size-dependent optical properties arising from quantum confinement, making them promising materials for applications in optoelectronics, bioimaging, sensing, photocatalysis, and energy conversion. In thi
content: Graphene quantum dots (GQDs) exhibit size-dependent optical properties arising from quantum confinement, making them promising materials for applications in optoelectronics, bioimaging, sensing, photocatalysis, and energy conversion. In this work, density functional theory (DFT), time-dependent DFT (TD-DFT), and quantitative structure–property relationship (QSPR) approaches were combined to investigate the effects of size, shape, and amine functionalization on the electronic and optical properties of armchair-edged GQDs. The results showed that increasing GQD size reduced the energy gap and produced a systematic red shift in optical absorption. Triangular and hexagonal shape GQDs exhibited similar size-dependent trends, indicating that quantum confinement dominates over geometric shape effects. Amine functionalization further modulated the optical response by altering the electronic structure and transition characteristics. QSPR models developed for the wavelength and oscillator strength of the lowest-energy electronic transition achieved good predictive performance. These findings provide useful structure–property relationships for the rational design of GQD-based optoelectronic materials.

title: Bio-waste-derived chicken feather carbon-integrated ZnGa2O4 nanocomposites for asymmetric supercapacitor application
summary: Abstract The pursuit of next-generation energy storage systems necessitates the development of advanced electrode materials that offer both high charge storage capacity and outstanding cycling stability to meet the increasing need for advan
content: Abstract The pursuit of next-generation energy storage systems necessitates the development of advanced electrode materials that offer both high charge storage capacity and outstanding cycling stability to meet the increasing need for advanced energy storage devices. Engineering hybrid nanostructures that combine conductivity, porosity, and electrochemical activity offers a promising pathway to elevate supercapacitor performance. This study reports the hydrothermal synthesis of ZnGa 2 O 4 /chicken feather carbon (ZGO/CFC) composites using varying amounts of chicken feather-derived carbon (40, 65, and 100 mg) as a sustainable carbon source. Comprehensive characterization techniques including X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman Spectroscopy, X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS), Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), and Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) analyses confirm the formation of a well-crystallized cubic ZnGa 2 O 4 structure, along with its morphological characteristics, elemental composition, and porosity. Electrochemical characterization reveal that the ZnGa 2 O 4 /100 mg chicken feather carbon electrode exhibits the highest specific capacitance of about 642.0 F g − 1 at 1 A g − 1 surpassing its counterparts. Asymmetric supercapacitor fabricated from ZnGa 2 O 4 /100 mg chicken feather carbon electrode shows specific capacitance of 67.33 F g − 1 with energy and power densities of about 21.04 Wh kg − 1 ,750 W kg − 1 respectively. In addition, it achieves a capacitive retention rate of about 94.0% and coulombic efficiency of about 95.0% which demands the integration of metal oxides with low-cost, renewable carbon materials as an effective strategy for advancing the performance of supercapacitors. The optimized ZGO/CFC composites demonstrate promising prospects for high-performance supercapacitor applications, facilitating the development for green energy storage solutions.

title: Spatiotemporal terahertz emission nanoscopy of spintronic photocurrent
summary: Capturing ultrafast spin and charge photocurrents on nanoscopic scales is essential for fundamental research in physics and engineering, as well as for future applications, such as novel spin-orbitronic devices. Accessing the fundamental dy
content: Capturing ultrafast spin and charge photocurrents on nanoscopic scales is essential for fundamental research in physics and engineering, as well as for future applications, such as novel spin-orbitronic devices. Accessing the fundamental dynamics driven by changes in electronic energy, linear momentum, and angular momentum requires probing at its native spatiotemporal scales: femtoseconds and nanometers. However, experimental approaches achieving this simultaneous resolution remain scarce and instrumentally demanding. Near-field probing offers promising platforms to combine ultrafast and nanometer resolution, typically with high sensitivity to out-of-plane electric fields. However, applying this technique to in-plane ultrafast coupled spin and charge currents is largely unexplored, although being highly application-relevant-from ultrafast spin transport in 2D materials to spin-to-charge conversion in spintronic terahertz emitters (STEs). Here, we fill this gap by performing spatiotemporal terahertz (THz) emission nanoscopy (TEN) of a photoexcited fiber-coupled STE using a scanning-probe microscope. We uncover a counterintuitive, dipolar spatial evolution of the near-field THz signal, which we show originates from the out-of-plane electric fields emerging from the in-plane spin-driven charge currents. Our findings explain why TEN is sensitive to ultrafast spin-driven in-plane charge currents, paving the way for TEN to become a fully vectorial probe for the spatiotemporal mapping of coupled nanoscale THz charge and spin dynamics.

title: Fe 3+ ‐Triggered Scalable Slow‐Corrosion Engineering for Industrial Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis at 2.0 A cm −2
summary: ABSTRACT The practical application of anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) is hindered by the lack of durable anodes for industrial‐scale current densities (≥ 1000 mA cm −2 ). Herein, we report a scalable Fe 3+ ‐triggered homo
content: ABSTRACT The practical application of anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) is hindered by the lack of durable anodes for industrial‐scale current densities (≥ 1000 mA cm −2 ). Herein, we report a scalable Fe 3+ ‐triggered homogeneous slow‐corrosion strategy to fabricate a Fe‐doped Ni(OH) 2 /NiS hybrid on nickel foam (Fe‐Ni(OH) 2 /NiS/NF) for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). This approach couples the slow corrosion of Ni foam by Fe 3+ with the in situ nucleation of the Fe‐Ni(OH) 2 /NiS hybrid, creating a seamless, interface‐free integration with exceptional mechanical adhesion. The optimized Fe‐Ni(OH) 2 /NiS/NF electrode exhibits exceptional stability for over 1100 h at ampere‐level current densities up to 2000 mA cm −2 without performance decay. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the catalyst undergoes rapid reconstruction at low potentials to form an amorphous Ni(Fe)OOH layer, which serves as the true active phase and primarily follows the adsorbate evolution mechanism, thereby avoiding the chemical degradation associated with lattice oxygen participation. Density functional theory calculations indicate that Fe doping upshifts the NiOOH d‐band center, strengthening * OH adsorption and thus lowering the * OH→ * O barrier to accelerate OER kinetics. In an AEMWE, it requires only 1.706 and 1.852 V to achieve 1.0 and 2.0 A cm −2 , respectively, maintaining stable operation at industrial currents for over 1800 h.

title: 8. Water balance
summary: A water balance is the sum of water inputs, outputs, and change in storage for a given water volume. This chapter focuses on the watershed-scale water balance at annual and seasonal time scales and explores how this water balance can be mod
content: A water balance is the sum of water inputs, outputs, and change in storage for a given water volume. This chapter focuses on the watershed-scale water balance at annual and seasonal time scales and explores how this water balance can be modified by climate change, land cover change, and stream modifications by human infrastructure. A technical section introduces indices for quantifying drought, while sustainability sections illustrate the effects of climate and land use change on the Amazon basin, effects of invasive trees on the water balance in South Africa, and effects of infrastructure in the Colorado River Basin.

title: Enhancing dye adsorption performance of sporopollenin through Thymssol-Menthol-based deep eutectic Solvent functionalization
summary: Dye pollution from industrial wastewater, including that from the batik industry, threatens aquatic ecosystems and water resources. Adsorption is a cost-effective and sustainable method for dye remediation. This study focused on synthesizin
content: Dye pollution from industrial wastewater, including that from the batik industry, threatens aquatic ecosystems and water resources. Adsorption is a cost-effective and sustainable method for dye remediation. This study focused on synthesizing thymol–menthol–based deep eutectic solvent functionalized sporopollenin (T:M@DES-Sp) as a new adsorbent for Rhodamine B (RB) remediation. The synthesized adsorbent material showed O–H and C–H stretching peaks at 3311 cm−1 and 2924 cm−1, respectively. The contact angle measurement was less than 90°, indicating a hydrophilic surface, and the thermogram showed a major weight loss in the temperature range of 120–185 °C, which is attributed to the simultaneous decomposition of thymol and menthol in a single step. The modification of Sp with DES markedly improved the adsorption performance, increasing RB dye uptake by nearly fourfold compared to Sp, underscoring the effectiveness of DES functionalization for dye removal from aqueous media. The adsorption of RB dye using T:M@DES-Sp is a spontaneous process, with ΔG° ranging from −2.39 to −0.64 kJ/mol, while ΔH° is −28.27 kJ/mol, indicating an exothermic process. T:M@DES-Sp achieved good removal efficiency for RB dye in both synthetic and real samples and demonstrated good reusability performance for up to six cycles. Moreover, its disposal after the adsorption process is nontoxic to the environment, as Pisum sativum showed 100% germination, comparable to that in freshwater. Hence, this study provides an eco-friendly and efficient solution for dye removal, supporting Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 6 by improving water quality and promoting sustainable industrial practices. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional organic solvents due to their low cost, low toxicity, and biocompatibility. Owing to their unique physicochemical properties, DESs have been widely applied in environmental applications, particularly as effective organic coating agents for adsorbents to enhance adsorption performance. Although numerous studies have reported the use of deep eutectic solvents (DESs) to modify materials such as activated carbon and biomass-based adsorbents, the functionalization of sporopollenin (Sp) with DESs remains unexplored. In this study, thymol–menthol deep eutectic solvents (T:M@DES-Sp) were employed for the first time to functionalize the surface of Sp, producing the hybrid material T:M@DES-Sp. Despite its promising potential, the adsorption performance, recyclability, selectivity, and interference behavior of T:M@DES-Sp in real wastewater matrices have not been comprehensively investigated. Therefore, this study systematically evaluates these aspects, providing the first comprehensive assessment of T:M@DES-Sp for dye removal and offering new insights into its practical application as a sustainable adsorbent for wastewater treatment.

title: An Efficient One Pot Synthesis And Antioxidant Activity of 6- (Benzylthio)-2H-Pyrazolo[3,4-d]Pyrimidine-3,4-Diamine
