title: Identifying and Prioritizing the Components of Circular Accounting: A Qualitative Study Based on Systematic Content Analysis
summary: The expansion of the circular economy has increased the need to transform accounting systems and identify the components required to support decision-making and reporting related to efficient resource utilization, waste reduction, and envir
content: The expansion of the circular economy has increased the need to transform accounting systems and identify the components required to support decision-making and reporting related to efficient resource utilization, waste reduction, and environmental performance. Despite the growing body of research on circular accounting, its constituent components and dimensions have been addressed in a fragmented manner across different studies, highlighting the need to identify and integrate these components. The present study aimed to identify, categorize, and prioritize the components of circular accounting. In terms of purpose, the study was applied, and in terms of methodology, it employed a qualitative, descriptive–analytical approach. To collect the data, scientific publications and texts related to circular accounting, the circular economy, sustainability, environmental accounting, and material flow management were systematically reviewed. During the analytical stage, conventional qualitative content analysis was used to extract relevant concepts from the texts, code them, and organize them into categories and subcomponents based on conceptual similarity. Through the process of analyzing and integrating the codes, three main categories were identified: dynamic capabilities of circular accounting, material flows in the circular economy, and institutional–environmental drivers and barriers. Subsequently, 12 subcomponents were extracted and classified: flexibility and reconfiguration; innovation and technology; learning and knowledge development; interaction and accountability; efficient material management and consumption; life cycle and environmental traceability; supply chain and resource optimization; policymakers and regulations; infrastructure and information technology; culture, education, and media; economic incentives and market pressure; and organizational and coordination barriers. To prioritize the main categories, the frequency of the extracted codes was used as the prioritization criterion. The results showed that institutional–environmental drivers and barriers, with 29 codes accounting for 45.2% of the total, had the highest frequency, followed by the dynamic capabilities of circular accounting, with 22 codes and a 34.3% share, and material flows in the circular economy, with 13 codes and a 20.3% share. The findings indicate that the formation and development of circular accounting depend not only on internal accounting capabilities but also on institutional and environmental factors, technological infrastructure, policies and regulations, culture, and coordination among stakeholders. The findings of this study can provide a basis for developing a conceptual framework and designing measurement instruments for circular accounting in future studies.

title: Nanomaterials for Water Purification Towards Global Water Crisis Sustainable Solutions
source: Innovative Reviews in Engineering and Science
summary: Providing the world's increasingly growing population with clean, affordable water is an unprecedented challenge for the 21st century. In the face of climate change and failing water quality, nanotechnology has become the center piece in in
content: Providing the world's increasingly growing population with clean, affordable water is an unprecedented challenge for the 21st century. In the face of climate change and failing water quality, nanotechnology has become the center piece in innovation in this global crisis. This article discusses the ways in which nanomaterials are leading the way in the revolution of the water purification techniques and are providing sustainable means to increase access to safe drinking water around the world. Water scarcity and pollution threaten human health, economic development and environmental sustainability. Traditional water treatment methods do not generally achieve effective removal of emerging pollutants and pathogen. Thus, the properties of nanomaterials at the molecular scale make it unique, and open new possibilities for development of more efficient, cost effective and environmentally friendly water purification. Nanotechnology is changing the way we clean and reuse water resources from nano adsorbents that remove toxic metals selectively and nanomembranes that filter out the slightest contaminants. In this article we will look at the advances in nanomaterials for water purification looking at how they work, what they are good for, and they could help enlighten us about the global water crisis. Through these innovations we’ll explore ways these are redefining the future of water management for anyone and everyone, not just industries and communities, but all across the globe.

title: Building people-centered dynamic capabilities for sustainability: An exploratory multilevel study of sustainability-driven enterprises in Indonesia
summary: Sustainability-driven enterprises (SDEs) in emerging economies depend on people, meaning committed leaders, engaged employees, and prepared successors, yet sustainable human resource management research has largely examined formal practices
content: Sustainability-driven enterprises (SDEs) in emerging economies depend on people, meaning committed leaders, engaged employees, and prepared successors, yet sustainable human resource management research has largely examined formal practices in large firms in developed economies. This study asks how SDEs in an emerging economy develop the people-based capabilities that sustainability requires, and how multi-stakeholder (Pentahelix) interactions across micro, meso, and macro levels shape that human capital development. Using an exploratory, multi-stage qualitative design based on the Gioia methodology, we interviewed ten experts spanning government, academia, industry, community, and media in Indonesia, then convened an expert panel to validate the emerging themes. The analysis identifies five reciprocal cross-level flows through which human capital for sustainability is built: top-down, bottom-up, a generative loop, informal social networks, and lateral interactions. Macro-level mandates and market pressures set the capability requirements a workforce must meet. Meso-level mechanisms such as management development programs, leadership schools, learning management systems, and “social bricolage” turn those requirements into training and orchestration routines. Micro-level moral agency, spiritual commitment, and value-internalization rituals such as weekly “Value Talks” keep people engaged and guard against burnout. A generative loop that codifies tacit leadership wisdom into explicit systems offers a way to address the “Legacy Paradox” of founder-dependent missions, and informal networks act as a “system lubricant” for trust-based collaboration. Read together, these findings treat people development as a coevolutionary, multi-actor process, and they offer HR managers and policymakers concrete guidance for cultivating sustainability champions where formal systems are thin. Keywords: Sustainable human resource management; leadership development; succession planning; knowledge management; employee commitment; Pentahelix collaboration; emerging economies

title: Book Review: “Museum of Modern Aluminum” – Bridging Industry and Art through Sustainable Design
source: Journal of Architectural/Planning Research and Studies (JARS)
summary: The book Museum of Modern Aluminum from Manufacture to Architecture documented an innovativearchitectural project by HAS Design and Research Company that redefines the application of aluminum incontemporary architecture. Inspired by the org
content: The book Museum of Modern Aluminum from Manufacture to Architecture documented an innovativearchitectural project by HAS Design and Research Company that redefines the application of aluminum incontemporary architecture. Inspired by the organic form of a dandelion and the ecological landscape ofThailand’s Koh Kret Island, the Museum of Modern Aluminum (MoMA) integrates aluminum as both a structuraland aesthetic element, showcasing its lightweight, malleable, and sustainable properties. The design featuresa dynamic façade composed of modular aluminum strips, paired with energy-efficient LED lighting that simulatesthe glow of fireflies, and landscape spaces that blend artificial and natural elements. This project not onlyhighlights the potential of aluminum in green architecture but also explores cultural transplantation, urbanmemory, and the balance between innovation and tradition. Through detailed case studies and reflections onmateriality, this book offers insights into sustainable design practices and reveals the evolving role of aluminumin shaping future-built environments.

title: Potential Native Plant Selection for Sustainable Landscape Architecture in Wangchan Forest, Rayong, Thailand
source: Journal of Architectural/Planning Research and Studies (JARS)
summary: Landscape architecture in Thailand still relies heavily on commercially propagated species. While convenient,this dependence narrows the design palette and promotes inclusion of exotic species or ecologically unsuitableplants, undermining b
content: Landscape architecture in Thailand still relies heavily on commercially propagated species. While convenient,this dependence narrows the design palette and promotes inclusion of exotic species or ecologically unsuitableplants, undermining biodiversity, long-term sustainability, and ecological resilience. By contrast, sustainablelandscape architecture prioritizes indigenous and locally adapted species that are visually expressive yetecologically matched to local conditions, thereby reducing maintenance, supporting native biota, and articulatingregional identity. This research investigated the Wangchan Forest in Rayong Province to develop a systematicprocess for identifying and selecting native plants for landscape use. The study objectives were to: (1) developa framework for selecting native species; (2) compile a list of native plants in Wangchan Forest; and (3)recommend species suitable for sustainable landscape design. The study combined botanical database analysiswith ethnobotanical inquiry. Data were drawn from Thai Plant Names by Tem Smitinand for the SoutheasternFloristic Region and complemented by semi-structured interviews with herbal doctors, local pioneers, andformer loggers with experiential knowledge of the forest. Species were evaluated using criteria emphasizingecological adaptability, microclimatic and edaphic compatibility, water requirements, and functional roles inlandscape design. Of the 13,527 plant species listed in the national database, 1,724 occur in the SoutheasternFloristic Region. Cross-referencing with local knowledge confirmed 516 species as native to Wangchan Forestand identified 137 additional species recognized locally but absent from the database, highlighting the valueof traditional ecological knowledge. Applying the selection framework yielded 125 native species recommendedfor landscape application, categorized into drought-tolerant, moderately drought-tolerant, high-humidity, andriparian or aquatic groups. Integrating scientific data with Local Ecological Knowledge thus provides a practical,replicable framework for native plant selection that expands the ecological and cultural richness of sustainablelandscape architecture in Thailand.

title: Green Attitude Links Brand Knowledge, Concern, and Positioning to Purchase Intention among Indonesian Nike Consumers
source: Jurnal Relevansi Ekonomi Manajemen dan Bisnis
summary: This study investigated how green brand knowledge, environmental concern, and green brand positioning shape green purchase intention among Nike consumers in Indonesia, with green attitude as a mediating link. Data were collected from an onl
content: This study investigated how green brand knowledge, environmental concern, and green brand positioning shape green purchase intention among Nike consumers in Indonesia, with green attitude as a mediating link. Data were collected from an online survey of 380 respondents who had bought an environmentally marketed Nike product in the past year and were tested using structural equation modeling in AMOS 24.0. Both green brand knowledge and environmental concern were significant positive predictors of green attitude, which had a strong positive effect on purchase intention. The knowledge-to-intention link operated entirely through this attitudinal pathway, whereas environmental concern retained a smaller but independent direct path, alongside an indirect one. In contrast, green brand positioning did not predict attitude or intention. Attitude toward the brand, rather than knowledge or positioning alone, emerged as the mechanism that converts these antecedents into purchase intention. Because respondents were recruited through convenience and purposive sampling within a single national market, the findings apply most directly to Indonesian Nike consumers rather than to green consumers. The study extends green marketing theory by isolating which antecedents require attitude as a conduit and offers sportswear marketers a basis for choosing among knowledge-, values-, and positioning-based messages.

title: Oil rents and domestic price dynamics: evidence from ten OPEC economies
summary: Oil-exporting economies face overlapping domestic price pressures, global energy shocks, and changes in resource income. This study examines relationships among consumer prices, oil rents, and the GDP deflator in ten OPEC economies from 199
content: Oil-exporting economies face overlapping domestic price pressures, global energy shocks, and changes in resource income. This study examines relationships among consumer prices, oil rents, and the GDP deflator in ten OPEC economies from 1990-2021, accounting for country differences and shared influences. The findings show a positive association between consumer and domestic output prices: a 1% higher GDP deflator is associated with about a 0.73% higher consumer price level in the main estimates. This relationship varies substantially across countries, documenting heterogeneous inflation dynamics in oil-exporting economies. The GDP-deflator coefficient reaches 1.253 in the group classified as having higher subsidies, compared with 0.753 in the comparison group. However, this classification coincides with regional composition, and excluding Libya reduces the descriptive coefficient gap from approximately 0.500 to 0.266. The comparison therefore highlights country heterogeneity without establishing a causal subsidy effect. Overall, the results support interpreting domestic price developments through the joint behavior of consumer prices, economy-wide prices, and resource dependence. Policy implications favor coordinated monitoring of these indicators and country-specific assessments of subsidy reform, informed by observed retail-price changes, fiscal conditions, and household exposure

title: Occupational Wearable Robotics
summary: Injuries and occupational diseases represent an important economic factor in different industrial sectors. In Italy alone, there have been over 60000 confirmed cases of occupational diseases in 2022, where musculoskeletal disorders (MSD) re
content: Injuries and occupational diseases represent an important economic factor in different industrial sectors. In Italy alone, there have been over 60000 confirmed cases of occupational diseases in 2022, where musculoskeletal disorders (MSD) represent 70% of the total. This fact highlights the importance of protecting workers against physical efforts. While current ergonomic tools can mitigate most of the risk factors, there is still a non-negligible number of tasks that cannot be completely compensated for. This is due to the high complexity and costs of the workplace reorganization, or simply strict requirements of the target task. In some of these cases, exoskeletons are a viable solution. This chapter introduces different kinds of existing exoskeletons, with particular focus on occupational exoskeletons, considering commercial systems already deployed in industry, and some of the most promising technologies which will arrive in the next years. The deployment of occupational exoskeletons is conditioned by the regulatory frameworks and by the required reorganization of the workplace. Both concepts and the latest developments are discussed in this chapter, including their integration into Industry 4.0. Finally, this chapter describes the most common evaluation methods and discusses current efforts toward standardized benchmarking methods which will allow evaluating the benefit of using exoskeletons in real applications.

title: What is energy literacy? From prerequisite for participation to social practice
summary: Energy literacy is often assumed to be a prerequisite for public participation in energy. But, it remains unclear how people's energy literacy leads to participation. This raises questions about dominant conceptualisations of energy literac
content: Energy literacy is often assumed to be a prerequisite for public participation in energy. But, it remains unclear how people's energy literacy leads to participation. This raises questions about dominant conceptualisations of energy literacy in relation to participation. We investigated energy literacy in relation to participation in energy communities, which are seen as important contexts for stimulating both. Following an abductive approach, we synthesized insights from diverse bodies of literature with empirical data from Greek energy communities, drawing on interviews and focus groups with 20 participants from energy community core teams and supporting organizations. We developed two perspectives on energy literacy, each assuming a different relation between energy literacy and participation, leading to different approaches for stimulating both. The first perspective sees energy literacy as a prerequisite for participation. It treats energy literacy as static ability that people have or lack, and operationalizes it through standardized, prescriptive, and isolated approaches. This view overlooks people's diverse needs. Therefore, we developed a broader view of energy literacy as social practice, that conceptualises energy literacy as something people do in their specific situation. Energy literacy and participation are intertwined, and operationalized through contextualized, dynamic, diverse and tailored approaches. Although the two perspectives depart from distinct conceptual assumptions, we found that approaches in practice can be placed on a continuum between them. By unpacking the conceptual assumptions, this study shows how different understandings of energy literacy shape approaches in practice, whose needs are addressed, and who are included in energy transitions.

title: Mechanisms of circularity: How epistemic, financial and material flows construct new waste geographies
summary: Circular Economy (CE) initiatives originate predominantly in the Global North, yet their material, epistemic, and financial effects increasingly manifest in Global South contexts. Using Dutch–Kenya waste relations as a critical case study,
content: Circular Economy (CE) initiatives originate predominantly in the Global North, yet their material, epistemic, and financial effects increasingly manifest in Global South contexts. Using Dutch–Kenya waste relations as a critical case study, this article examines how CE interventions transform waste materials into a marketized commodity through three interconnected variables: an epistemic variable, reframing waste and circularity through market-oriented knowledge systems; a financial, channelling investment towards formalized circular infrastructure that excludes informal and community-based actors; and a material variable, establishing new waste geographies that concentrate processing activity in the Global South. Kenya's dual position as a destination for Dutch waste exports and a recipient of Dutch CE development funding, makes it a relevant site for observing how these variables operate and interact. Drawing on interviews with Dutch and Kenyan government, donor, and civil society actors, the article argues that CE interventions restructure the governance of existing waste markets not through Dutch influence alone, but through negotiated convergence between Dutch donor priorities and the Kenyan state's own regulatory capacity constraints and economic interests. This restructuring concentrates control over the terms of participation among formal, internationally connected, and resourced actors, while progressively marginalizing informal workers who have long managed waste through community-based practices. Through an environmental justice lens drawing on Schlosberg's (2007) tripartite framework of distribution, recognition, and participation, the article demonstrates that the critical question is not only who governs the new waste geographies and on whose terms material recovery proceeds, but how donor and recipient-state interests jointly produce the exclusion of informal actors from that governance. The article contributes an integrated analytical framework for studying the shift from conventional waste trade to circular trade in North–South relations, and positions this contribution within political ecology and critical CE scholarship.

title: The Paradox of Urban Environmental Paradigms: A Theory of Legitimacy, Dominance, and Operational Divergence
summary: Why do some urban environmental paradigms become globally dominant while others remain marginal despite substantial convergence in their environmental foundations? This question captures a central paradox in contemporary urban environmental
content: Why do some urban environmental paradigms become globally dominant while others remain marginal despite substantial convergence in their environmental foundations? This question captures a central paradox in contemporary urban environmental planning: sustainable, resilient, low-carbon, circular, regenerative, and related formulations continue to proliferate, yet their institutional trajectories differ markedly. This study addresses that paradox by developing a theory explaining how urban environmental paradigms are defined, institutionally produced, legitimated, diffused, and operationalized across planning, policy, certification, and development systems. Rather than treating environmental labels as equivalent to paradigms, the study conceptualizes urban environmental paradigms as institutionally recognized organizing frames that structure problem interpretations, normative priorities, legitimate interventions, and evaluative expectations. Drawing on institutional theory, legitimacy theory, diffusion of innovations, policy mobility, market signaling, experimental governance, and bounded rationality, the analysis integrates scholarly and institutional evidence to develop a four-pillar institutional ecosystem operating through six cross-cutting mechanisms and self-reinforcing diffusion architectures. It further identifies configurational conditions associated with institutional dominance and advances the proposition that paradigms converge upstream in shared environmental logic families while diverging downstream through heterogeneous governance, implementation, and operational conditions. The resulting theory explains why conceptually convergent paradigms follow markedly different institutional and operational trajectories across contexts.

title: Adoption decision-making of AI digital humans for agricultural regional public brands in short videos
summary: Introduction This study examines the adoption of AI digital humans (AI-DHs) by agricultural regional public brands in short-video promotion. Methods A complex network evolutionary game model is developed in which brands interact on a scale-
content: Introduction This study examines the adoption of AI digital humans (AI-DHs) by agricultural regional public brands in short-video promotion. Methods A complex network evolutionary game model is developed in which brands interact on a scale-free network and update their strategies through the Fermi rule. The model considers AI-DH production and generation costs, real-human promotion costs, consumer preference, recommendation priority, and network size. For each parameter scenario, 100 stochastic simulation runs are conducted, and mean adoption trajectories with 95% simulation intervals are reported. Results Higher AI-DH-related costs reduce the relative payoff of AI-DH promotion and suppress adoption, whereas higher real-human promotion costs make AI-DH promotion comparatively more attractive. Consumer preference produces the most pronounced change in the evolutionary outcome, with higher preference shifting the system toward broader AI-DH adoption. Higher recommendation priority helps sustain AI-DH adoption during the evolutionary process but does not independently determine the final adoption state. Network size has limited influence on long-run average adoption, although larger networks reduce stochastic variation in the evolutionary process. Discussion These findings extend digital-human research from post-adoption consumer responses to the dynamic adoption decisions of agricultural regional public brands and highlight the roles of relative payoffs, platform conditions, and inter-brand learning.

title: From Exclusion to Protection: Chinese Merchant Capital in the Philippines Under US Law and Empire, 1921–1926
summary: Abstract Scholarship about the Chinese Question has largely understood it as a “coolie” question, but what if it was reframed in terms of merchants? Well-studied US anti-Chinese laws like the 1882 Chinese Exclusion Act targeted working-clas
content: Abstract Scholarship about the Chinese Question has largely understood it as a “coolie” question, but what if it was reframed in terms of merchants? Well-studied US anti-Chinese laws like the 1882 Chinese Exclusion Act targeted working-class rather than elite Chinese, like merchants and students. But in 1921, the US-controlled Insular Government in the Philippines enacted a statute known as the Chinese Bookkeeping Act (Act No. 2972), marking a moment when US Chinese exclusion laws were directed toward businessowners. The act banned Chinese-language record-keeping and affected merchants ranging from small storeowners to multi-millionaire tycoons. A group of Chinese merchants in the Philippines sued the colonial government and appealed their case to the US Supreme Court, which ruled the Bookkeeping Act unconstitutional in 1926. For the “coolie” Chinese question, the US Supreme Court said “yes” to exclusion, but for the merchant Chinese question, the Court said “no.” The Court’s rejection of a merchant Chinese exclusion became part of the Philippines’ transformation into a US colony. In relation to a patriotic Filipino capital and unmarked Euro-American capital, Chinese capital won rights even as it was framed within US law as “alien” by American and Filipino judges and politicians and, surprisingly, by the Chinese merchants themselves.

title: Comparative Histological and Immunohistochemical Study of The Effects of Energy Drinks and Cessation on The Testicular Structure of Adult and Young Male Albino Rats
source: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
summary: Concerns about the possible health risks associated with energy drinks have come to light because of their increasing usage worldwide, particularly among young people.This experimental study aimed to evaluate the effects of excessive energy
content: Concerns about the possible health risks associated with energy drinks have come to light because of their increasing usage worldwide, particularly among young people.This experimental study aimed to evaluate the effects of excessive energy drink consumption and subsequent cessation on testicular histology and serum testosterone levels in adult and young male albino rats.Thirty healthy male rats were divided equally into two main groups (adults and young), with each further subdivided into three subgroups: control, energy drink -consumed, and recovery.Rats in the energy drink -consumed groups received 20 mg/kg/day of energy drink s orally for four weeks, while the recovery subgroups underwent an additional four-week cessation period following exposure.After the experimental period, blood and testicular tissue samples were analysed using light microscope, semithin sections, immunohistochemistry, and molecular techniques.Results showed that prolonged energy drink intake significantly disrupted testicular structure, leading to shrunken seminiferous tubules, degenerated germ and Leydig cells, and markedly reduced testosterone levels.These effects were more severe in young rats.In contrast, cessation of energy drink intake resulted in substantial histological and hormonal recovery, with adult rats showing near-complete restoration and young exhibiting partial improvement.The findings highlight that energy drinks can significantly impair testicular architecture and function, particularly during the young stage, but stopping intake may allow for partial or full recovery depending on age.This study underscores the need for public awareness regarding the reproductive risks of energy drink consumption, especially among adolescents.

title: Solanum tuberosum peel extract attenuates acetaminophen-induced hepatotoxicity through modulation of inflammatory cytokines, apoptotic pathways, and CYP3A4 expression: evidence from molecular docking, Hep G2 cell assays, and an in ovo embryonic model
summary: Abstract Background CYP3A4 is the primary cytochrome P450 that plays a secondary role along with CYP2E1 in the oxidation of acetaminophen (APAP) to the toxic metabolite N-acetyl-p-benzoquinone imine (NAPQI). APAP overdosing activates c-Jun
content: Abstract Background CYP3A4 is the primary cytochrome P450 that plays a secondary role along with CYP2E1 in the oxidation of acetaminophen (APAP) to the toxic metabolite N-acetyl-p-benzoquinone imine (NAPQI). APAP overdosing activates c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK), which activates the mitochondrial membrane permeability transition (MPT). This cascade results in disruption of the hepatic homeostasis. Methods Initially, 70 compounds were short-listed and considered for molecular docking with CYP3A4. Solanine, having shown the highest docking score (− 11.2), was considered as a potential drug, and the ethanolic extract of the fruits of Solanum tuberosum was prepared from pulp and peel. Cytotoxicity of the pulp and peel extracts on Hep-G2 cells was assessed by MTT assay, colony formation assay, and DAPI staining. In the next phase, 14-day-old pathogen-free, fertilised chicken eggs were procured and inoculated with 100μL of APAP (0.01 mg/ml concentration), 10% ethanolic extract of Solanum tuberosum (STE), and 70% alcohol (vehicle control) in five challenge sets and three control sets. After 48 h, allantoic fluids were collected for RT-PCR analysis, and histopathological examination was performed for liver, heart, and brain by H&E staining. Results The peel extract demonstrated a superior safety profile, showing no inhibitory effect on Hep G2 cell proliferation up to 96 h. in ovo administration of STE significantly down-regulated IL-6, IL-10, IL-1β, TGF-β1, CYP3A4, c-Jun-K, and Bax gene expression compared with the APAP control group. Conversely, STE peels up-regulated the anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 gene. Histopathological examination revealed the protective effect of STE peel on hepatocytes against APAP-induced toxicity. Conclusion Solanum tuberosum peel extract confers significant protection through modulation of pro-inflammatory cytokines, apoptotic markers, and CYP3A4 expression.

title: Identifying brain-computer interface translational priorities with an outlook on the field in 2035
summary: Brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) have advanced rapidly, particularly over the past few decades, evolving from experimental demonstrations to powerful research tools and early-stage clinical technologies. Invasive, semi-invasive, and non-inv
content: Brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) have advanced rapidly, particularly over the past few decades, evolving from experimental demonstrations to powerful research tools and early-stage clinical technologies. Invasive, semi-invasive, and non-invasive modalities now enable neural decoding, neuromodulation, and functional restoration across diverse neurological conditions. Yet, despite striking laboratory demonstrations and growing investment, few BCIs have become viable medical products, having only a limited impact. Here, we provide a quantitative analysis to identify crucial clinical applications on which BCI translational efforts should focus to achieve substantial clinical, societal, and economic impact. Using an urgency–importance–impact framework based on disability-adjusted life years analysis, we assessed 12 neurological conditions to provide insight into how to prioritize strategic BCI development efforts. Alzheimer’s disease, stroke, depression, and anxiety, with their combined high urgency, importance, and impact, emerge as strategic targets with the greatest societal and economic stakes. We further argue that BCIs today, particularly invasive modalities, function primarily as transformative scientific instruments, analogous to the astronomic telescope in the era preceding classical mechanics, and will shape future theoretical and clinical innovation. Realizing a sustainable BCI industry beyond 2035 will require aligning basic neuroscience, artificial intelligence-driven advances, scalable clinical validation, ethical safeguards, and coordinated strategic planning.

title: Nutritional dynamics of weeds in agroecosystem and their utilization in the agro-food industry within a circular economy framework
source: Frontiers in Food Science and Technology
summary: Edible weeds are becoming more widely acknowledged that edible weeds are underutilized natural resources with substantial potential to promote circular bio-economy initiatives and sustainable food systems. Many weed species have nutritional
content: Edible weeds are becoming more widely acknowledged that edible weeds are underutilized natural resources with substantial potential to promote circular bio-economy initiatives and sustainable food systems. Many weed species have nutritional content, a variety of bioactive chemicals, and numerous uses in human nutrition, livestock feeding, and value-added agro-food products, while being historically considered unwanted elements of agricultural landscapes. The nutritional makeup, phytochemical profile, functional characteristics, and agro-food usage of a few edible weed species that are frequently found in agricultural habitats are all critically summarised in this narrative review. Major scientific databases, such as Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar, were used to retrieve literature published between recent years. The selection of species was based on their documented edible use, the availability of peer-reviewed information about their nutritional composition and potential applications, and their frequent occurrence as agricultural weeds. Evidence suggests that edible weeds are abundant in vitamins, minerals, phenolic compounds, flavonoids, carotenoids, essential amino acids, dietary fibre, weeds are abundant in vitamins, minerals, phenolic compounds, flavonoids, carotenoids, essential amino acids, dietary fibre, and other phytochemicals with antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and metabolic regulating qualities. Although interesting biological activities have been shown in experimental research, there is still a dearth of solid clinical evidence to support many of these health advantages. Edible weeds provide prospects for value-added applications in circular agricultural systems, such as livestock feeding, compost generation, natural food additives, and nutraceutical development, in addition to human nutrition. However, before broader commercialisation is possible, issues with food safety, anti-nutritional elements, processing method uniformity, regulatory approval, and customer acceptance must be resolved. In conclusion, rather than taking the place of traditional crops, edible weeds should be seen as complementary resources that help diversify food systems, increase resource-use efficiency, and support sustainable agricultural growth. To enable their responsible incorporation into resilient agro-food systems, future research should give priority to clinical validation, standardised processing technologies, safety assessment, economic feasibility studies, and commercialisation strategies.

title: Varying Mechanisms Dominate Formate Formation in Electrochemical CO2 Reduction on Cu, Au, and Pb: A Constant Potential DFT-Based Microkinetic Analysis
summary: Abstract Electrochemical CO2 reduction offers a route to convert renewable electricity into fuels and chemicals while closing the anthropogenic carbon cycle. However, the technology struggles to surpass the lab scale as it is limited by low
content: Abstract Electrochemical CO2 reduction offers a route to convert renewable electricity into fuels and chemicals while closing the anthropogenic carbon cycle. However, the technology struggles to surpass the lab scale as it is limited by low selectivity and energy efficiency. These challenges are less severe for the two-electron products, carbon monoxide and formate, making them attractive targets. Formate is of particular interest due to its potential as an energy carrier and its relatively high market value. Yet its formation mechanism remains debated, hindering rational catalyst design. Here, we combine grand canonical DFT, a hybrid explicit-implicit solvent model, and microkinetic simulations to elucidate the formate formation mechanism on Cu, Au, and Pb, and show that distinct pathways dominate on each metal. On Cu, formate formation proceeds via O-bound chemisorption of CO2 followed by protonation. Au exhibits negligible formate activity despite supporting different formate pathways depending on facet termination and applied potential, as these pathways remain kinetically unfavorable. Finally, Pb facilitates a direct outer-sphere-like process from physisorbed CO2 to formate, with high activity. The enhanced activity may originate from the distinct electronic structure of Pb, characterized by diffuse p-like states near the Fermi level, a feature shared by other formate-selective post-transition-metal catalysts. The variation in mechanisms for formate production likely underlies the difficulty of identifying universal activity descriptors for electrochemical CO2 and suggests that catalyst design might necessitate mechanism-specific descriptors.

title: StereoAtlas: A Large-Scale Dataset of Chiral Compounds with Distinct Bioactivities Curated from ChEMBL37
summary: Stereoisomers share identical two-dimensional molecular topology and exhibit a Tanimoto similarity score of exactly 1.0 under standard fingerprint methods, rendering their bioactivity differences invisible to conventional data-driven or phy
content: Stereoisomers share identical two-dimensional molecular topology and exhibit a Tanimoto similarity score of exactly 1.0 under standard fingerprint methods, rendering their bioactivity differences invisible to conventional data-driven or physics-based activity prediction approaches. Here, we present StereoAtlas, a dataset of 155,526 experimentally measured true isomer families derived from ChEMBL37, in which paired or families of stereoisomers exhibited pharmacological activity for the same biological target, in the same organism. Fold differences in activity between stereoforms were computed under two complementary strategies — MinMax and reference-form— and classified into five stereoselectivity tiers: None (<2×), Mild (2–5×), Moderate (5–10×), Strong (10–50×), and Extreme (>50×). Among 38,446 IC50 families, 9.5% exceed the 50-fold Extreme threshold, and the maximum fold difference observed is 195,000,000× at the oxytocin receptor (Kd) for the stereoisomeric families CHEMBL386547 (potent isomer) and its inactive counterparts (CHEMBL274635 and CHEMBL414373). Spanning 420,721 unique compounds, 4,519 biological targets, 471 organisms, and 879 activity types, this dataset provides a detailed, systematic, large-scale experimental resource for chirality cliff-based analysis. All data and pipeline scripts are publicly available.

title: Modular synthesis of 3,3-diaryloxetanes
summary: Abstract Oxetanes are strained four-membered oxygen heterocycles that are valuable motifs for modulating lipophilicity, metabolic stability and three-dimensional structure of pharmaceuticals. Diaryloxetanes with 3,3-substitution are recogni
content: Abstract Oxetanes are strained four-membered oxygen heterocycles that are valuable motifs for modulating lipophilicity, metabolic stability and three-dimensional structure of pharmaceuticals. Diaryloxetanes with 3,3-substitution are recognized as bioisosteres of diaryl ketones that preserve key electronic features while exhibiting distinct reactivity. However, synthesis of this motif largely relies on Lewis acid-promoted Friedel–Crafts reactions, which are restricted to electron-rich arenes and often suffer from low functional-group tolerance and competing side reactions. Here we report a method for the synthesis of 3,3-substituted diaryloxetanes from readily available 3-oxetanone through a cross-coupling reaction with tetrafluoropyridone as leaving group. The difunctionalization through subsequent addition of two aryl groups, one from an aryl halide, the other from an arylboronic ester, provides access to a variety of benzophenone bioisosteres. The nickel-catalysed cross-coupling at a fully substituted carbon centre is enabled through oxetanyl C–O bond oxidative addition and establishes programmable entry to 3,3-diaryloxetane bioisosteres that are synthetically challenging to access via traditional polar bond disconnection strategies. Mechanistic studies support a Ni(0)-mediated oxidative addition of the oxetanyl tetrafluoropyridine ester.

title: D6.2 Safety and Sustainability Assessment of Supercapacitors
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The report constitutes ARMS deliverable D6.2 SSbD framework report detailing preliminary results and findings for safety and sustainability assessment. The aim of ARMS is to develop safe and environmentally friendly supercapacitors from ear
content: The report constitutes ARMS deliverable D6.2 SSbD framework report detailing preliminary results and findings for safety and sustainability assessment. The aim of ARMS is to develop safe and environmentally friendly supercapacitors from early-stage material selection to market deployment. This deliverable compares the safety and sustainability performance between a representative commercial product and an ARMS-developed supercapacitor with the SSbD (Safe and Sustainable by Design) framework. The results are publicly accessible, serving as valuable suggestions for diverse stakeholders, including 1. public research institutions, engaged in fundamental and applied research on electrochemical energy storage. 2. Private sector organizations, including battery manufacturers, material suppliers, and technology developers, seeking sustainable innovation pathways. 3. Regulatory bodies and policymakers involved in shaping sustainable energy strategies. The SSbD results elaborated in this report follow a hierarchical approach, in which safety dimension is considered first, followed by environmental (including circularity) assessment. Safety assessment identifies potential hazards associated with materials, manufacturing processes, and end-use applications. This includes evaluating toxicity and occupational exposure risks. Building on this, the report incorporates life cycle thinking to assess environmental impacts, addressing material efficiency and recyclability. The results clarify that a neutral salt such as sodium sulfate is a safe electrolyte candidate, while EMIM-TFSI used in structural supercapacitors may cause environmental toxicity. Triton X-100 used in both commercial and ARMS flexible electrode ink is associated with significant environmental hazards, particularly acute aquatic toxicity and endocrine-disrupting effects. Greater level of Local Exhaust Ventilation (LEV) can mitigate the inhalation risks from binder outgassing (PVDF used in commercial supercapacitors and SBR used in ARMS flexible supercapacitors) particularly during electrode ink coating process. Given the preliminary energy density range (15-25 Wh/Kg) and specific capacitance (15-25 F/g) range of the ARMS supercapacitors, the climate change impact of ARMS structural and flexible supercapacitors is around half that of commercial ones. However, the use of impactful chemicals such as sodium hydroxide and muriatic acid during carbon activation process should be minimized, despite their contribution to better performance. In addition, the use of metal encapsulation materials such as aluminum foil should be optimized and avoid unnecessary cutting waste since they usually do not improve the cell performance directly. From a recycling perspective, the manufacturing process of supercapacitors should prioritize material simplicity and design-for-disassembly to improve recovery efficiency and reduce environmental burdens. title: Post-pandemic strategic evaluation of food supply chains using hybrid decision models
source: Pamukkale University Journal of Engineering Sciences
summary: The increasing complexity and disruptions in global food supply chains (FSCs), particularly after COVID-19, have emphasized the need for resilient and adaptive strategies. This study conducts a comparative analysis of various FSC structures
content: The increasing complexity and disruptions in global food supply chains (FSCs), particularly after COVID-19, have emphasized the need for resilient and adaptive strategies. This study conducts a comparative analysis of various FSC structures, such as Centralized, Decentralized, Digitalized, Localized, and Hybrid models. The comparison was carried out by applying two integrated multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) methods: Entropy-based MOORA and Entropy-based MARCOS. Objective weights for the eight criteria (cost, flexibility, resilience, lead time, sustainability, service level, innovation capability, and risk management) were assigned through the Entropy method that was used to reduce the subjective bias. In general, both methods identified the Digitalized and Hybrid supply chain models as the two highest-ranked alternatives, while the Centralized model ranked last. To make the findings even more robust, we carried out a sensitivity analysis where we changed the criterion weights in different scenarios. Moreover, an Entropy-based COPRAS method was employed for the robustness analysis, and the findings supported the stability and consistency of the rankings across different methodological approaches. By comparing two MCDM methods in a post-pandemic context, the study contributes to the literature while offering practical guidance for stakeholders on investing in digital infrastructure, adopting hybrid supply chain models, and integrating sustainability objectives into supply chain planning. The findings provide practical guidance for policymakers and executives seeking to enhance the resilience and environmental sustainability of FSCs amid global uncertainty.

title: Addressing emerging authenticity issues using novel data-driven analytics
summary: As globalization continues to grow, trade structures are becoming increasingly complex, which creates numerous challenges for businesses. One of these is ensuring the authenticity of high-priced products. Recent developments have made it cl
content: As globalization continues to grow, trade structures are becoming increasingly complex, which creates numerous challenges for businesses. One of these is ensuring the authenticity of high-priced products. Recent developments have made it clear that established control mechanisms are often inadequate for ensuring protection against fraud or mislabeling, so the need for new analytical solutions is growing rapidly. In its individual studies, this dissertation examines the application of modern data-driven approaches for the authentication of various goods of agricultural and non-agricultural origin. At the heart of all investigations is a software that was developed specifically for this research project but, thanks to its modular design, has great potential for future applications in diverse fields. It enables the automated processing, modeling, and evaluation of spectroscopic and spectrometric data. To date, there has been no solution that enables streamlined analysis of data from, for example, isotope ratio mass spectrometry (IRMS), nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (NMR), near-infrared spectroscopy (NIR), and the associated metadata in a fully reproducible and transparent manner. One area of investigation focused on the authentication of spring barley with respect to the harvest year. Grain samples were taken directly from active trade flows and then analyzed to ensure that they reflected realistic conditions in the supply chain, in contrast to numerous studies that relied on samples from strictly controlled experimental fields and are therefore hardly transferable to real-world conditions. The aim was to develop a novel analytical approach that allows differentiation of the two harvest years 2017 and the extremely dry 2018 for spring barley samples by means of multiple modern analytical techniques and to link the observed metabolic differences to the physiological responses of plants to drought stress. Samples from the 2018 harvest year showed significantly less negative δ¹³C values than those from 2017, likely reflecting reduced stomatal conductance and altered carbon assimilation during the grain-filling stage. These findings were supported by NIR, which showed lower protein, starch, and moisture content and an increase in lipid content for 2018. NMR analysis revealed elevated concentrations of the osmolyte betaine, a well-known biochemical marker for abiotic stress adaptation. By merging the isotope and NIR datasets and applying multivariate statistical analysis, a classification model was built that achieved 100% separation accuracy between the two investigated years. Although not directly linked to authenticity, differences in variety-specific stress responses were also observed, demonstrating the broader applicability of the approach for selecting stress-resilient varieties in the future.
