content: Bu kitabın, basım, yayın ve satış hakları Akademisyen Yayınevi'ne aittir.Anılan kuruluşun izni alınmadan kitabın tümü ya da bölümleri mekanik, elektronik, fotokopi, manyetik kağıt ve/veya başka yöntemlerle çoğaltılamaz, basılamaz, dağıtılamaz.

title: EPISTEMIC EXCLUSION AND INEQUALITY IN FRONTIER ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
summary: Social inequality is no longer only a matter of income, schooling, or access to devices. It now includes who may inspect the systems that draft public texts, rank information, and assist administrative work. This article analyses large lang
content: Social inequality is no longer only a matter of income, schooling, or access to devices. It now includes who may inspect the systems that draft public texts, rank information, and assist administrative work. This article analyses large language models as a mechanism of epistemic exclusion: publicly produced knowledge is enclosed, and most universities and publics lose the standing to audit the result. The study is qualitative and documentary. It is not an engineering benchmark. Thematic content analysis covered 23 peer-reviewed articles (2015-2024) and 13 corporate reports. A comparative case study then read GPT-4, Claude, Gemini, and LLaMA. Three findings follow. First, core methods circulated in academic and publicly funded research before commercial enclosure. Second, academic ethics is framed as justice, labour, and public accountability; corporate ethics is recoded as trust, safety, and product risk. Third, closed model parameters, hidden training data, and concentrated computing capacity block independent audit, with special force for public universities in Ibero-America. Public computing infrastructure, audit rights, and multilingual evaluation are therefore instruments of social policy, not laboratory upgrades. The study reports no new regional survey.

title: Retention During Turbulent Times of Higher Education: Modeling Intent to Leave Academia for Research University Faculty
summary: University faculty operate as the lifeblood of any institution given that their job requires a “double duty” to develop both scholarly research and student minds. Due in large part to these expectations, research shows a long history of poo
content: University faculty operate as the lifeblood of any institution given that their job requires a “double duty” to develop both scholarly research and student minds. Due in large part to these expectations, research shows a long history of poor mental health for faculty, which ultimately results in faculty turnover. One model of faculty work motivation (Padilla et al., 2023) details the way in which the faculty work environment influences their mental health, and subsequently informs their job satisfaction, organizational commitment, and intent to leave academia, which serves as a proxy for turnover. Retention related issues have not been a pressing concern for higher education institutions, but the current social environment may bring these issues to the forefront. Following the COVID-19 pandemic and leading into the demographic cliff (Grawe, 2018), higher education institutions will need to retain both students and faculty alike. To equip institutions to retain their faculty members, this manuscript seeks to confirm and build upon the aforementioned model. Since the data for the original model were collected prior to COVID-19, it is important to collect data from a more current sample to determine if the model holds true. Additionally, the inclusion of new variables will only help to strengthen the predictive validity of the model. The findings from this manuscript will advance our understanding of faculty mental health and potentially prepare institutions to better provide for their faculty in attempts to prevent turnover during the demographic cliff.

title: From academic integrity to credential integrity: What does management education certify once artificial intelligence can produce the work?
source: The International Journal of Management Education
summary: The debate on generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) in management education has centered on whether students may use AI, yet the larger question is what student work can still prove. Once AI can draft and polish a case analysi
content: The debate on generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) in management education has centered on whether students may use AI, yet the larger question is what student work can still prove. Once AI can draft and polish a case analysis, an essay, or slides, polished work stops being strong evidence of what a student can do. This article calls the resulting problem credential integrity (i.e., whether a business school can defend what its degree certifies when AI may have produced the graded work). Policies on detection, disclosure, and originality cannot solve this problem, given that all three ask who produced the work and leave intact the assumption that good work proves a capable student. In response, this article draws on assessment scholarship, policy research, and validity theory to propose a verified-judgment architecture in which high-stakes certification rests on unaided command of core concepts and methods, reasoning defended when questioned, positions reconsidered when challenged, learning transferred to changed conditions, and accountable decision making. The architecture is translated into program-level responsibilities for school leaders and redesigned assessments for teachers, neither of which requires a ban on AI or the false belief that an AI-free submission proves learning. A reality check of 84 business schools shows how far practice is from this standard, given that schools describe AI access, curriculum integration, and faculty development more fully than any proof of what the degree certifies and only one school in seven reports a safeguard (e.g., a defended capstone or work kept free of AI).

title: How can we innovate residential care building design? Insights from an Australian e-Delphi study of procurement processes
summary: The procurement of residential care facilities presents opportunities for design innovation, yet is challenged by various contextual factors, including country-specific policies, regulations, research, care models, organisational practices,
content: The procurement of residential care facilities presents opportunities for design innovation, yet is challenged by various contextual factors, including country-specific policies, regulations, research, care models, organisational practices, and socioeconomic influences. Despite the impact of these factors on built quality, little research has explored the extent to which they enable or constrain design innovation. Defining procurement as four phases (Planning, Design, Construction, and Occupancy), this study provides a cross-stakeholder understanding by integrating diverse perspectives on how these processes and their dynamics shape opportunities for design innovation in residential care environments. Objectives are: (1) to create a diagrammatic representation of the procurement process for new residential care facilities, highlighting key stakeholders and interdependent components; (2) to define what innovation means in residential care building design; (3) to identify and provide a hierarchy of contextual factors (opportunities and barriers) that influence this innovation; and (4) to explore how these factors influence innovation across the procurement process. A multi-method qualitative approach included a rapid review, analysis of 38 case studies, and a two-round national e-Delphi study with 32 experts from 4 stakeholder groups. The findings offer a foundation for policymakers to assess the influence of various factors, reframe power dynamics between key stakeholders, and explore transdisciplinary collaboration models to foster innovation. The study reveals that many challenges are not unique to residential care facilities, but reflect broader systemic issues across sectors and building typologies.

title: The performance inference gap in talent management: A critical integrative review
source: Journal of Economics and Business Letters
summary: Talent management is frequently justified by its expected contribution to organizational performance, yet a reported performance relationship can represent different constructs, measurement sources, and levels of inference. This critical in
content: Talent management is frequently justified by its expected contribution to organizational performance, yet a reported performance relationship can represent different constructs, measurement sources, and levels of inference. This critical integrative review examines the correspondence between talent management exposures, organizational outcomes, and the designs used to connect them. A new public-source search on October 7, 2026, retrieved 4,899 OpenAlex records, all retained after DOI and Unicode-preserving title checks. A purposive, full-text case corpus was then assembled to contrast outcome definitions, information sources, analytical levels, temporal structures, and reporting credibility. The inventory is not presented as an exhaustively screened systematic review. The cases reveal several distinct inference problems: performance items that already attribute success to talent management; financial labels attached to managerial perceptions; retrospective comparisons presented as evidence across time; capability chains without formal indirect-effect estimates; and mediation coefficients whose causal interpretation exceeds the design. A temporally separated study and a qualitative skills-matching study provide useful contrasts while retaining their own identification limits. Reporting contradictions and probable dataset overlap further constrain some estimates. The review develops a framework that distinguishes construct correspondence, measurement independence, and causal identification, and specifies what evidence is needed to connect talent practices to realised organizational returns. Its contribution is a transparent audit of performance inference, rather than a representative effect estimate or a universal endorsement of talent management.

title: Penguatan UMKM Halal dan Ramah Lingkungan: Integrasi Sertifikasi Halal dengan Praktik Ekonomi Hijau untuk Daya Saing Global
summary: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) face increasingly complex market demands encompassing product quality, pricing, halal assurance, product safety, environmental sustainability, and compliance with global market standards. Halal c
content: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) face increasingly complex market demands encompassing product quality, pricing, halal assurance, product safety, environmental sustainability, and compliance with global market standards. Halal certification and green economy practices are commonly positioned as separate agendas, although they have strong potential for integration as a strategy to strengthen MSME competitiveness and sustainability. This community engagement program aimed to enhance the capacity of the MSME community to understand the integration of halal certification and green economy practices as a foundation for sustainable business development and global market orientation. The program was conducted online on September 26, 2026, in collaboration with the SSQ Holistik Internasional–Malang MSME Community and involved 40 participants. The program employed a participatory capacity-building approach through needs assessment, education, mentoring, applied discussions, and evaluation using pre-test and post-test assessments. The results indicated an increase in participants’ average understanding from 69 to 87, representing an 18-point improvement (26.09%), with a normalized gain score of 0.58, categorized as moderate. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the educational intervention in enhancing participants’ knowledge capacity. However, increased knowledge does not necessarily represent actual changes in halal certification ownership or the implementation of environmental practices. Therefore, further assistance is required through halal certification support, halal traceability, resource-efficiency measurement, waste reduction, and green product development.

title: Financial Viability of Red Sea Urchin (Mesocentrotus franciscanus) Aquaculture: A Comprehensive Analysis of Risk, Production Costs, and Market Dynamics under Macroeconomic Scenarios
summary: This study investigates the financial viability of red sea urchin (Mesocentrotus franciscanus) aquaculture, addressing key economic factors such as production costs (CAPEX and OPEX), larval prices, and market dynamics. Through a comprehensi
content: This study investigates the financial viability of red sea urchin (Mesocentrotus franciscanus) aquaculture, addressing key economic factors such as production costs (CAPEX and OPEX), larval prices, and market dynamics. Through a comprehensive literature review and the development of a dual financial model (deterministic and stochastic), critical parameters influencing profitability are identified. While a baseline deterministic model suggests an Internal Rate of Return (IRR) of 22.4%, the incorporation of stochastic variables based on historical inflation and Mexican CETES rates reveals significant vulnerability (negative NPV given a 6.14% discount rate). The results demonstrate that optimizing the larval phase and reducing initial investment (CAPEX) are crucial for mitigating macroeconomic risk. This study provides a robust risk assessment framework for investors and policymakers.

title: The formalization trap explains why sustainability education policy displaces informal knowledge systems
summary: Global sustainability education has expanded rapidly since UNESCO adopted its 2030 framework. Informal sustainability knowledge has eroded across the same decade. This Perspective article asks whether exactly those two trends might turn out
content: Global sustainability education has expanded rapidly since UNESCO adopted its 2030 framework. Informal sustainability knowledge has eroded across the same decade. This Perspective article asks whether exactly those two trends might turn out structurally connected. It reports no primary fieldwork, building instead upon published studies and on official policy documents. Three contributions follow directly from that question. Embedded Sustainability Knowledge denotes understanding whose validity rests on three constitutive properties. Place, practice and relation together constitute it. The Formalization Trap then explains that observed displacement. Formal provision competes for funding, abstracts practice into portable curricula, and reserves recognition for those holders carrying documented credentials. A Recognition-First framework proposes sequencing recognition before any curricular transfer. Three institutional moves follow, and each one uses instruments that Bangladesh already operates. Heritage inscription confers standing without certification, geographical indication carries income to practitioners, and community organisations sustain transmission where curricular alignment is refused. Bangladesh serves here as critical case. Its knowledge systems remain intact, formal provision is expanding, and public money flows almost entirely through certification. This argument names conditions rather than countries, letting others test it. Formal education is not opposed here, and no withdrawal is being recommended. Only the policy sequence itself is being contested here.

title: The Tools Factor
summary: The Tools Factor is about to dominate what people write and read, know and believe to know. In this book, we explain how digital tools and agentive AI shape – and are shaped by – text production, ethics, and creativity in the newsroom. Base
content: The Tools Factor is about to dominate what people write and read, know and believe to know. In this book, we explain how digital tools and agentive AI shape – and are shaped by – text production, ethics, and creativity in the newsroom. Based on thirty years of longitudinal ethnographies in research frameworks of transdisciplinarity and applied linguistics, we discuss what this means for researching and integrating AI in professional newswriting. Key topics include: How has tools development interacted with professional writing? What does the case of implementing AI in a multilingual newsroom reveal? Why can applied linguists contribute to a sustainable AI shift of public discourse? Tracing the future of digital newswriting has resulted in three key learnings from empirical evidence. First, tools make a change that can scale up from practices to professions and society at large. Second, in seemingly unstoppable grand movements, counterchange often starts bottom-up, from positive deviants. Third, as applied linguists and transdisciplinary researchers, we are to identify the creative practices that can disrupt mainstream disruption.

title: Postcolonial perspectives on neoliberal humanitarian governance and the Rohingya refugee crisis in Bangladesh
summary: The global refugee crisis situation is increasingly being subsumed under the humanitarian-development nexus (HDN), which, otherwise, informs humanitarian interventions within the normative framework of northern stakeholders including develo
content: The global refugee crisis situation is increasingly being subsumed under the humanitarian-development nexus (HDN), which, otherwise, informs humanitarian interventions within the normative framework of northern stakeholders including development agencies. While refugee studies have already explored HDN, there is still a lack of critical research on HDN, especially in the context of neoliberal governance. And therefore, the article inquires why and how has neoliberal HDN been implemented in the event of refugee crises? To answer the research question, this study employs a qualitative method and relies on postcolonial and dependency theories towards analyzing neoliberal HDN. Also, the study argues that neoliberal shift to a humanitarian-development agenda by northern aid and development agencies serves and benefits from global to local actors in the refugee governance system. As evident from the case of the Rohingya refugee crisis in Bangladesh, neoliberal HDN is responsible for the long-term plight and protracted displacement of Rohingyas. The study findings inform that there must be a shift away from this agenda in responding to humanitarian crisis. In particular, the refugee host country needs to be enabled, towards tackling the refugee crisis in real humanitarian terms.

title: BUILDING A GREEN DIGITAL ECONOMY: HOW FINTECH STRENGTHENS GREEN FINANCE AND FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE
summary: The research methodology used in this study was quantitative research design, which aimed at studying the role of fintech in strengthening the financial performance of green finance in the framework of a green digital economy. The study emp
content: The research methodology used in this study was quantitative research design, which aimed at studying the role of fintech in strengthening the financial performance of green finance in the framework of a green digital economy. The study employed panel data of 30 countries in developing and emerging economies from 2015 to 2024, data was drawn from World Bank and IEA, financial and environmental databases. The indicators used to assess the development of fintech were digital financial services, digital payments and the adoption of financial technology, while green finance indicators were green investment, green credit and financial flows oriented towards the environment. Return on assets (ROA) and return on equity (ROE) were used to determine financial performance. The concept of green finance was considered as a potential intervening variable that affects the financial performance of financial institutions. The controlled variables were the economic growth, inflation, foreign direct investment, financial development, and renewable energy consumption. Descriptive statistics and correlation analysis were conducted followed by panel regression analysis to evaluate the direct connection between fintech development and financial performance, while a mediation analysis was used to test whether green finance was a mediator to enhance the direct relationship. The diagnostic tests for multicollinearity, heteroskedasticity, cross sectional dependence and serial correlation were performed and robust standard errors were used as appropriate. The results showed that the relationship between fintech development and financial performance was positive and significant, while green finance played the role of a mediator, but it did not completely mediate the relationship between fintech development and financial performance. Green finance was shown to be a significant and partial mediation variable, and fintech development was significantly and positively associated with green finance. These results were validated in robustness tests based on alternative indicators of financial performance and fintech. These findings highlight that fintech can have an impact on the financial performance, but also through greater access to green finance channels via the allocation of funds to green activities, making green finance a potential meaningful supplement to fintech-related financial development. Policy implications are discussed.

title: The impact of R&D innovation strategy on labor productivity in intelligent manufacturing enterprises: evidence from a quasi-natural experiment in China
summary: This study explores whether the additional tax deduction policy for R&D expenses raises firms’ R&D investment and advances industrial upgrading. Based on a sample of Chinese listed intelligent manufacturing firms, we empirically analyse the
content: This study explores whether the additional tax deduction policy for R&D expenses raises firms’ R&D investment and advances industrial upgrading. Based on a sample of Chinese listed intelligent manufacturing firms, we empirically analyse the policy’s effect on corporate labour productivity. Results indicate that the policy significantly improves labour productivity, and the conclusion holds after parallel trend, placebo and propensity score matching robustness tests. Mechanism tests show the policy mitigates financing constraints, encourages R&D engagement and lifts capital investment to boost labour productivity. Heterogeneity analysis suggests stronger effects for eastern/central-region firms, large enterprises and firms in industries with slow technological renewal. This paper reveals the policy’s influencing channels and provides empirical evidence for improving labour productivity in intelligent manufacturing.

title: γZ box at low energy
summary: A bstract We calculate the 1-loop γZ box-graph correction to electron-quark scattering at low energy and low momentum transfer. Both electron and quark masses are kept non-zero. We express our result in terms of low-energy couplings for 4-f
content: A bstract We calculate the 1-loop γZ box-graph correction to electron-quark scattering at low energy and low momentum transfer. Both electron and quark masses are kept non-zero. We express our result in terms of low-energy couplings for 4-fermion interaction including parity-violating couplings. We study the zero-mass limits and show that a non-zero electron mass is sufficient to obtain finite, well-defined couplings which are insensitive to a hadronic mass cutoff. We finally discuss the impact of our results on the determination of the weak charge of the proton from polarized electron-proton scattering.

title: Access, Affordability, and Willingness to Undergo Screening Colonoscopy in a Low‐ and Middle‐Income Country—A Cross‐sectional Study From Sri Lanka
summary: BACKGROUND: Colorectal cancer (CRC) incidence is rising rapidly across low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet most lack organised screening programmes. While colonoscopy is the diagnostic gold standard, its uptake depends not only on
content: BACKGROUND: Colorectal cancer (CRC) incidence is rising rapidly across low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet most lack organised screening programmes. While colonoscopy is the diagnostic gold standard, its uptake depends not only on service availability but also on behavioural perceptions and health system design. Sri Lanka, an LMIC with a strong public health system but no national CRC screening programme, provides a relevant policy setting to examine these dynamics. METHODS: A cross-sectional survey of 500 adults at the National Hospital of Sri Lanka assessed willingness to undergo screening colonoscopy. Sociodemographics, CRC-related knowledge, perceptions of benefit/harm, and cost considerations were evaluated using non-parametric tests and multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: Overall, 69.7% of participants were willing to undergo colonoscopy if recommended by a doctor; however, 42.7% would do so only if the procedure were free. Willingness was independently associated with belief that early detection improves outcomes (adjusted Odds Rate (aOR) 2.96, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.94-4.53, p < 0.001) and fear of CRC (aOR 1.72, 95% CI 1.13-2.61, p = 0.012). Misconceptions about colonoscopy-related harm and fear of cancer diagnosis significantly reduced acceptance. Sociodemographic variables, education level, prior colonoscopy experience, and insurance status were not independently associated with willingness. Cost-related conditional willingness highlights substantial access barriers despite high stated acceptability. CONCLUSIONS: Among the variables examined, perceived benefit and affordability were important correlates of stated screening acceptability, while sociodemographic characteristics were not independently associated. Implementation requires strategies addressing affordability, capacity, and perceptions. A phased, publicly financed programme incorporating non-invasive testing and targeted communication may provide a feasible pathway for LMICs.

title: Penalty‐Based Discrete Particle Swarm Optimization for Coordinating Relays in a Brazilian 138 kV Real Power System
summary: ABSTRACT In this paper, an original approach to deal with the coordination of instantaneous and time‐overcurrent directional protection is proposed. Such problem is mathematically modelled as a nonlinear programming problem with continuous
content: ABSTRACT In this paper, an original approach to deal with the coordination of instantaneous and time‐overcurrent directional protection is proposed. Such problem is mathematically modelled as a nonlinear programming problem with continuous and discrete variables, whose proposed resolution approach is based on the minimization of the relays' operation time by using penalty‐based discrete particle swarm optimization. In this new technique, discrete variables are treated as continuous by using sinusoidal, quadratic or polynomial functions and inequality constraints are transformed into equality constraints. The effectiveness of the model and the robustness of this approach for coordinating directional overcurrent relays were verified with a Brazilian 138 kV real power system, considering both electromechanical and digital relays, mutual impedances and network contingencies. The method has shown success in handling discrete variables and inequality constraints, which results in the decreasing of the protection engineer's workload.

title: ‘Ways of attending’: using arts-based learning to explore social work students’ identities
summary: Identity development is a central component of social work education, underpinning reflective practice and relational engagement. While existing literature emphasizes professional identity formation, less attention has been given to the int
content: Identity development is a central component of social work education, underpinning reflective practice and relational engagement. While existing literature emphasizes professional identity formation, less attention has been given to the integration of personal identities into professional selves. This research project addresses this gap, by examining how arts-based learning can support identity exploration. A qualitative research design was employed within an Erasmus+ Blended Intensive Programme comprising a series of creative workshops for 38 international students. Data were generated through a post-programme written survey, with 33 of the participants providing comments, which were examined using reflexive thematic analysis. Findings reveal that arts-based engagement facilitated shifts in perception, cognition, emotional awareness, and relational understanding. Participants described deeper self-reflection, increased self-acceptance, and developing more holistic views of themselves, while also considering applications for practice. These results are discussed with reference to theoretical perspectives on ‘attending,’ drawing on McGilchrist’s distinction between analytic and holistic modes of engagement. The study concludes that arts-based learning supports the examination of students’ identities by enabling alternative ways of attending. This contributes to students’ reflexivity with interesting and important consequences, not only for social work education but also for the students’ future social work practice.

title: AI in supply chain risk assessment: a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis
summary: Abstract Supply chain risk assessment (SCRA) is pivotal for ensuring resilience in increasingly complex global supply networks. While existing reviews have explored traditional methodologies, they often neglect emerging artificial intellige
content: Abstract Supply chain risk assessment (SCRA) is pivotal for ensuring resilience in increasingly complex global supply networks. While existing reviews have explored traditional methodologies, they often neglect emerging artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) applications and mostly lack combined systematic and bibliometric analyses. This study addresses these gaps by integrating a systematic literature review with bibliometric analysis, examining 1,903 articles (2015-2025), with 54 studies selected through PRISMA guidelines. Our findings reveal that ML models, including Random Forest, XGBoost, and hybrid approaches, significantly improve risk prediction accuracy and adaptability in post-pandemic contexts. The bibliometric analysis identifies key trends, influential authors, and institutional contributions, highlighting China and the United States as leading research hubs. Practical insights emphasize the integration of explainable AI (XAI) for transparent decision-making, real-time data utilization, and blockchain for traceability. The study underscores the necessity of dynamic strategies, interdisciplinary collaboration, and continuous model evaluation to address challenges such as data quality and interpretability. By synthesizing AI-driven methodologies with resilience frameworks, this review provides actionable guidance for optimizing supply chain risk management, fostering adaptability, and informing future research in evolving risk landscapes.

title: Explainable NLP in the Era of Large Language Models: A Unified Taxonomy, Evaluation Frameworks, and Decision Guidance
summary: Explanation methods for natural language processing (NLP) come from two literatures that rarely meet: feature attribution and probing for task models, and the interpretability of large language models (LLMs), from chain-of-thought reasoning
content: Explanation methods for natural language processing (NLP) come from two literatures that rarely meet: feature attribution and probing for task models, and the interpretability of large language models (LLMs), from chain-of-thought reasoning to sparse autoencoder features and circuit tracing. We place both in a unified taxonomy with four dimensions: scope (local vs. global), mechanism (how the explanation is computed), model access (model-agnostic vs. model-specific), and output form (importance scores, rules, examples, counterfactuals, rationale spans, concepts, natural language). Faithfulness and plausibility come apart, and the erasure tests built for extracted rationales do not apply to a chain of thought, which is an output rather than part of the input, so chains of thought need intervention tests of their own. The access a deployment allows settles which mechanisms are usable before scope or audience matter; our practical decision frameworks start from that question and are traced through three worked deployments. In our synthesis of LLM-era interpretability, a lineage table shows that most current techniques rebuild or extend older ideas under new constraints of scale and access, while two problems are new: keeping reasoning traces monitorable under training pressure, and testing whether models can introspect. Faithfulness metrics disagree with one another, and sparse autoencoders do not yet beat simple baselines on standardized benchmarks, so evaluations should name the tests they ran instead of reporting one score. We also survey applications across healthcare, legal and financial services, social science research, content moderation, and education, and close with six open problems.

title: The “Digital Moral Economy” of Care: Institutional Logics and the Legitimation of AI-Based Algorithmic Management
summary: Research on platform work has largely focused on algorithmic management in sectors such as delivery and ride-hailing, paying limited attention to care and domestic services. This article theorizes how platforms integrate technology-mediated
content: Research on platform work has largely focused on algorithmic management in sectors such as delivery and ride-hailing, paying limited attention to care and domestic services. This article theorizes how platforms integrate technology-mediated economic activities with moral principles of care. Drawing on ethnographic data from 64 narrative interviews in Belgium and France, the authors show how platforms legitimate AI-based and technologically embedded forms of management by aligning them with institutional care logics. They conceptualize this as a “digital moral economy” of care, structured around three key dimensions: efficiency, civic contribution, and transactional relationships. Through these, platforms frame algorithmic coordination as socially valuable, morally acceptable, and practically enabling forms of care exchange. While these justificatory logics partly converge across national contexts, the article also highlights important cross-national differences in justificatory logics. Findings advance debates on algorithmic management by demonstrating how moral narratives are central to the legitimation of platform-mediated care services.

title: A thorium-229 optical nuclear clock with feedback loop
summary: Abstract The laser-accessible nuclear transition in the thorium-229 isotope has been identified as a candidate for realizing an optical nuclear clock 1 that might outperform current optical clocks based on electron-shell transitions in atom
content: Abstract The laser-accessible nuclear transition in the thorium-229 isotope has been identified as a candidate for realizing an optical nuclear clock 1 that might outperform current optical clocks based on electron-shell transitions in atoms or ions 2 . It is expected to be more robust against external perturbations 3,4 and to provide enhanced sensitivity in clock-based tests of the fundamental principles of physics 5,6 . Here we realize a thorium-229 nuclear clock by stabilizing a continuous-wave laser to the 148-nm nuclear transition with rapid feedback based on absorption spectroscopy 7 . The thorium-229 nuclei are embedded in a millimetre-sized, room-temperature calcium fluoride crystal. A subharmonic of the 148-nm radiation is continuously compared with a Yb + single-ion clock. The nuclear clock shows a shot-noise-limited fractional frequency instability of $$3\times 1{0}^{-12}/\sqrt{\tau /{\rm{s}}}$$ 3 × 1 0 − 12 / τ / s where τ is the averaging time, approaching 10 −15 instabilities over 1 day of operation. Improvements to the instability by several orders of magnitude are projected for future devices. We use the nuclear clock to constrain models of ultralight dark matter by searching for periodic fluctuations and slow drifts in the nuclear transition energy, on timescales between 20 s and 1 day. Benefitting from the enhanced sensitivity of the thorium-229 transition, these constraints compete with the best atomic clocks concerning dark matter coupling to photons and go beyond previous measurements regarding coupling to the strong force.

title: Collective defence of the territorio: vernacular concepts and practices of security in Colombia’s Pacific South-West
source: White Rose Research Online (University of Leeds, The University of Sheffield, University of York)
summary: This article examines the ways in which three communities in South-West Colombia understand ‘security’, and the practices they adopt in pursuit of it. Building on the burgeoning literature on vernacular security, we show the centrality of ‘
content: This article examines the ways in which three communities in South-West Colombia understand ‘security’, and the practices they adopt in pursuit of it. Building on the burgeoning literature on vernacular security, we show the centrality of ‘territorio’ as the key referent object of security in the region, and a wide variety of collective efforts adopted by communities in pursuit of securing their territorios. Through this, we make three contributions to the vernacular security literature. Methodologically, we show that Participatory Action Research (PAR) can be a powerful tool for identifying and understanding vernacular concepts and practices of security. But more than this, PAR can also play a role in helping to build and sustain community-level collective security practices, bridging research and action. Empirically, we bring vernacular security analysis to a region that has to date not been examined, documenting discourses and practices of security that are radically different from those that have dominated (western) security studies. Conceptually, we show how understandings and practices of security in the region draw directly upon indigenous, mestizo and Afro-Colombian cultures, histories, and epistemologies - and in many respects do not conform with western security registers that are too often assumed to be universal. This reiterates the importance of PAR, which can help researchers avoid (unwittingly) perpetuating western-centric assumptions about what visions of security communities are trying to achieve, and how they pursue those objectives.

title: On Vivisection, Interest Groups and Influence
summary: The year 2022 marked the 10th anniversary of the course Critical Animal Studies: Animals in Society, Culture and the Media at the Department of Communication and Media at Lund University. As the first initiative of its kind in Sweden, the c
content: The year 2022 marked the 10th anniversary of the course Critical Animal Studies: Animals in Society, Culture and the Media at the Department of Communication and Media at Lund University. As the first initiative of its kind in Sweden, the course explores the shifting roles and positions of non-human animals in today’s complex societies. It aims to equip students with analytical tools to critically assess norms and structures that organise human-animal relations, along with their ethical, cultural, and social consequences. What started as a one-course offering driven by an idea has evolved into a decade-long project of education and emancipation for non- human animals. This anthology stands as a testament to the course’s impact, aiming to extend the rich discussions, debates, and insights cultivated beyond the classroom walls. This celebratory collection assembles writings from former students, instructors, and guest lecturers, delving into themes ranging from critical media analysis over activist strategies to pedagogical reflections. The anthology’s scope not only reflects the diverse facets of the course but also unveils the myriad, often subtle intersections between human-centered society and the lives of non-human animals.

title: Built for bulk: posture, microanatomy and soft tissue shaped gigantism in Sauropoda
summary: Abstract Sauropodomorph dinosaurs show how appendicular skeletal architecture accommodated extreme increases in body mass. Although sauropod gigantism has been linked to columnar limbs, wide-gauge posture, thick articular cartilage and tubu
content: Abstract Sauropodomorph dinosaurs show how appendicular skeletal architecture accommodated extreme increases in body mass. Although sauropod gigantism has been linked to columnar limbs, wide-gauge posture, thick articular cartilage and tubular long-bone organization, the biomechanical interaction among these components is poorly understood. Here, we examine how femo ral shape, internal bone architecture and articular soft tissues influenced mechanical scaling across Sauropodomorpha. We generated three-dimensional femoral models spanning early sauropodomorphs, narrow-gauge diplodocoids, intermediate-gauge titanosauriforms, wide-gauge titanosaurs and an African elephant control. Finite element analyses compared theoretical solid models with taxon-specific native configurations, incorporating medullary cavities and articular cartilage caps. Mechanical performance was assessed using 95th-percentile von Mises stress, strain energy density and structural stiffness. Femoral performance did not scale uniformly with body mass. The two sampled narrow-gauge taxa, Diplodocus and Amargasaurus, defined steeper scaling trajectories for stress and strain energy density, whereas wide-gauge titanosaurs generally displayed flatter trajectories, comparatively lower stress and strain energy density, and elevated stiffness in several large-bodied forms. Targeted sensitivity analyses further showed that the mechanical effects of medullary architecture and cartilage depended on their interaction with taxon-specific femoral geometry. These findings suggest that sauropod gigantism was sustained by lineage-specific combinations of femoral geometry, internal architecture and articular soft tissues.

title: Indigenous Women’s Wisdom in Sustainable Natural Resource Management: A Participatory Environmental Justice Perspective
summary: Sustainable natural resource management has yet to adequately recognize and integrate indigenous women’s traditional knowledge. This article examines its legal status, the challenges to its recognition, and the legal reforms needed to stren
content: Sustainable natural resource management has yet to adequately recognize and integrate indigenous women’s traditional knowledge. This article examines its legal status, the challenges to its recognition, and the legal reforms needed to strengthen it from a participatory environmental justice perspective. Using normative legal research with statutory, conceptual, and participatory environmental justice approaches, the study finds that indigenous women’s traditional knowledge is vital to sustainable natural resource management but remains constrained by limited legal recognition, structural and patriarchal biases, and inadequate integration into governance frameworks. The study recommends strengthening legal recognition, reconstructing gender-inclusive laws, and integrating indigenous women’s traditional knowledge into sustainable natural resource management frameworks to advance participatory environmental justice.

title: Role of digitalization and environmental policy stringency in the relationship between financial development and environmental sustainability
summary: Financial development is often viewed as a cornerstone of economic progress, yet its expansion may come with an environmental cost. This raises a critical question of whether digitalization and environmental policy stringency can weaken the
content: Financial development is often viewed as a cornerstone of economic progress, yet its expansion may come with an environmental cost. This raises a critical question of whether digitalization and environmental policy stringency can weaken the link between financial development and ecological degradation. Grounded in the STIRPAT theoretical framework, this study examines the effects of financial development, digitalization, environmental policy stringency, economic globalization, economic growth, and urbanization on ecological footprint (EF) across 27 OECD countries from 1990 to 2020. It further investigates the moderating roles of digitalization and environmental policy stringency in the relationship between financial development and EF. The results from the Method of Moments Quantile Regression (MM-QR) show that financial development increases EF, and the effect is more pronounced at higher quantiles. In contrast, digitalization and environmental policy stringency are associated with lower EF across the conditional distribution. Importantly, the interaction results indicate that both digitalization and environmental policy stringency significantly moderate the relationship between financial development and EF. This suggests that greater digitalization and stronger environmental policy stringency can mitigate the environmental pressure associated with financial development. Economic globalization also increases EF across all quantiles, while economic growth and urbanization are positively associated with EF, indicating that these factors contribute to greater ecological pressure. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of coordinating financial, digital, and environmental policies to limit the ecological costs of financial development and promote environmental sustainability in OECD economies.

title: Turning Waste into Action: Stakeholder Mapping for Extended Producer Responsibility in Sustainable Packaging`
source: RSF Conference Series Business Management and Social Sciences
summary: Packaging waste has become an increasingly urgent urban environmental problem. However, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) implementation remains constrained by unclear stakeholder roles, weak coordination, and unequal stakeholder power
content: Packaging waste has become an increasingly urgent urban environmental problem. However, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) implementation remains constrained by unclear stakeholder roles, weak coordination, and unequal stakeholder power. Research on stakeholder roles in local sustainable packaging governance also remains limited. This study examines stakeholder power, legitimacy, and urgency in EPR implementation. A qualitative case study was conducted in Yogyakarta from April to August 2026. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with seven informants representing government institutions and businesses that had or had not adopted sustainable packaging, supported by document review and field observations. The data were analyzed using thematic coding, stakeholder mapping, and triangulation. The findings identify government institutions and businesses as key stakeholders, while technical institutions facilitate the transition of micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises toward sustainable packaging. Communities have legitimate and urgent environmental interests but limited formal authority. Stakeholder salience is dynamic and context-dependent. Effective EPR implementation therefore requires clear roles, stronger coordination, business support, community participation, transparent communication, and periodic evaluation.

title: ESG Rating Disagreement and Its Relationship with Financial Risk and Firm Value: Evidence from the United Kingdom and the United States
source: Journal of Business Social and Technology
summary: Background: The growing prominence of sustainable investing has amplified reliance on Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) ratings for guiding investment choices. Nevertheless, assessments of the same firm frequently vary among ratin
content: Background: The growing prominence of sustainable investing has amplified reliance on Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) ratings for guiding investment choices. Nevertheless, assessments of the same firm frequently vary among rating providers, generating uncertainty and informational imbalances. Objective: This study investigates the association between ESG rating disagreement, financial risk, and firm value, addressing the scarcity of evidence regarding how divergence in ratings concurrently relates to market-based risk indicators and corporate valuation. Methods: The analysis encompasses 60 firms listed in the United Kingdom and the United States over the 2019–2023 period. ESG scores obtained from Refinitiv Eikon, Bloomberg, and S&P Global are standardized through percentile rank transformation, and disagreement is quantified using the standard deviation of these standardized scores. Panel data regression models are applied to assess firm value proxied by Tobin’s Q, total risk proxied by stock return volatility, and systematic risk proxied by market beta. Results: ESG rating disagreement exhibits a positive and statistically significant relationship with both firm value and systematic risk, whereas its link with total risk lacks statistical significance. These outcomes suggest that heightened rating divergence may correspond to elevated corporate valuation and increased sensitivity to broad market fluctuations, without necessarily amplifying overall stock return volatility. Conclusion: The findings reveal ESG rating disagreement does not uniformly correspond to unfavorable market outcomes. The results lend support to the relevance of signalling and information asymmetry frameworks, offering practical insights for investors who consult multiple ESG rating sources and for corporate managers striving toward more coherent ESG communication.

title: Kepastian Hukum sebagai Instrumen Perlindungan Foreign Investment dalam Pengembangan Waste-to-Energy Berdasarkan Perpres Nomor 109 Tahun 2025
source: Mutiara Jurnal Penelitian dan Karya Ilmiah
summary: Waste-to-Energy (WtE) development in Indonesia requires not only technological and financial capacity but also a predictable legal framework capable of protecting long-term investment. This study aims to analyze legal certainty as an instru
content: Waste-to-Energy (WtE) development in Indonesia requires not only technological and financial capacity but also a predictable legal framework capable of protecting long-term investment. This study aims to analyze legal certainty as an instrument for protecting foreign investment under Presidential Regulation No. 109 of 2025 and to evaluate its implications for project bankability and the State’s regulatory authority. The research employs normative legal research using statutory, conceptual, and limited comparative approaches, with Presidential Regulation No. 35 of 2018 used as a historical comparator. The findings show that Presidential Regulation No. 109 of 2025 establishes a more integrated regulatory architecture through a uniform electricity tariff, mandatory PLN offtake, must-dispatch priority, a 30-year Power Purchase Agreement, waste-supply and land arrangements, and a more structured project selection mechanism. These provisions strengthen predictability, contractual certainty, and development-side certainty while reducing regulatory, revenue, market, and feedstock risks. However, they do not constitute an absolute investment guarantee because effective protection still depends on implementation, enforceable project documents, financing arrangements, licensing, and balanced application of legitimate expectations and the State’s right to regulate. The study implies that future regulatory strengthening should focus on clearer tariff-review parameters, curtailment rules, compensation mechanisms, and consistent contractual implementation.

title: Strategies to Strengthen the Global Competitiveness of Master of Management Graduates: A SWOT Analysis of X University
source: RSF Conference Series Business Management and Social Sciences
summary: Competition among higher education institutions and rising demands regarding graduate competencies have positioned global competitiveness as a strategic priority for master's degree programs. The Master of Management (MM) Study Program at t
content: Competition among higher education institutions and rising demands regarding graduate competencies have positioned global competitiveness as a strategic priority for master's degree programs. The Master of Management (MM) Study Program at the Faculty of Economics and Business (FEB), X University aims to enhance the competitiveness of its graduates at the regional (ASEAN) level and achieve global recognition. This study aims to identify the internal and external factors influencing the enhancement of graduate global competitiveness and to formulate strategic alternatives using the SWOT matrix within a strategic management framework. A qualitative descriptive approach utilizing document analysis was employed, using 2024 Self-Evaluation Documents (DED) of the MM Study Program as main source of data. The results indicate that basically, the MM Study Program possesses a strong internal foundation, particularly regarding faculty quality, a responsive curriculum, academic-practitioner learning, networking, and international capabilities. However, certain areas require strengthening – specifically English language proficiency, international support, the integration of internationalization efforts, and the measurement of global graduate outcomes. These strengths and weaknesses, combined with opportunities and threats, were analyzed using a SWOT matrix to generate various strategic alternatives, that were synthesized into four priority strategies: global learning internationalization, global graduate competitiveness measurement, academic-industry differentiation, and efficient internationalization and learning pathways.

title: Empirical Mapping of Investor Attention Across LQ45 Stocks on The Indonesia Stock Exchange, 2022–2025
source: RSF Conference Series Business Management and Social Sciences
summary: Digitalization has transformed how retail investors discover and evaluate listed companies, making online search activity a potentially observable component of investor attention. This study maps the level, volatility, and temporal dynamics
content: Digitalization has transformed how retail investors discover and evaluate listed companies, making online search activity a potentially observable component of investor attention. This study maps the level, volatility, and temporal dynamics of investor attention across stocks in the LQ45 index from 2022 to 2025. Using a longitudinal quantitative-descriptive design, the study analyzes 68 unique securities observed over 16 quarters, yielding 1,088 stock-quarter observations. The Quarterly Google Trends Index (GTI) is used as a search-based proxy for attention. Stocks are ranked by mean GTI and by the standard deviation of quarterly GTI, while annual changes and sectoral patterns are examined descriptively. MIKA (81.53), SIDO (66.22), ARTO (57.07), WIKA (52.13), and BUKA (49.29) have the highest mean attention. Attention volatility is highest for BUKA (25.07), GOTO (16.65), WIKA (15.46), PTBA (14.26), and WSKT (13.39). Aggregate attention declines from 23.58 in 2022 to 19.29 in 2024 and rebounds to 20.72 in 2025. The study confirms that attention varies across firms and sectors and changes over time. Its main contribution is a longitudinal descriptive baseline for Indonesian LQ45 stocks that distinguishes persistent attention from episodic attention and clarifies the methodological limits of Google search data. The results provide a basis for future causal tests linking attention with trading activity, returns, and volatility.

title: AI‐Based PV Fault Detection: Benchmarking Indicators and Feature Selection Methods
source: Progress in Photovoltaics Research and Applications
summary: ABSTRACT This article presents a benchmarking of indicators for automated defect detection in photovoltaic modules based on I‐V curves. The methodology is structured in three stages. First, an ideal defect‐free I‐V curve is generated throug
content: ABSTRACT This article presents a benchmarking of indicators for automated defect detection in photovoltaic modules based on I‐V curves. The methodology is structured in three stages. First, an ideal defect‐free I‐V curve is generated through simulation to provide a reference for comparison with experimentally measured I‐V data under standard test conditions. Second, several electrical and curve‐shape indicators are computed to quantify the deviation between simulated and measured curves. Electrical parameters are expressed as ratios between experimental and simulated values, whereas curve‐shape descriptors integrate the comparison directly into their formulation. Finally, a comprehensive feature selection strategy is applied; filter (Pearson correlation and Mutual Information) and wrapper methods (Recursive Feature Elimination, Permutation Importance, and Boruta) are tested across several machine learning classifiers, including Decision Trees, Support Vector Classifiers, K‐nearest neighbors, Random Forests, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, and LightGBM. The approach is evaluated using an experimental I‐V curve database generated by the GdS‐Optronlab research group. Results consistently discard indicators such as the open‐circuit voltage ratio and short‐circuit current ratio, while highlighting the current at the maximum power point ratio, the fill factor, and the mutual information of the maximum power point.

title: Carbohydrate-to-fat ratio is positively associated with comprehensive frailty across protein-intake levels in older adults
summary: PURPOSE: Diet influences frailty, and protein intake has been a prime focus of prevention. However, frailty remains prevalent, even among older adults with relatively high protein intake, suggesting the influence of remaining energy distrib
content: PURPOSE: Diet influences frailty, and protein intake has been a prime focus of prevention. However, frailty remains prevalent, even among older adults with relatively high protein intake, suggesting the influence of remaining energy distribution between carbohydrates and fats. We investigated the association between the carbohydrate-to-fat energy ratio (CFr) and comprehensive frailty in older Japanese adults and whether this association differed by protein intake. METHODS: Cross-sectional baseline data from 5679 community-dwelling adults aged ≥ 65 years in the Kyoto-Kameoka Study were analyzed. Diet was assessed using a validated 46-item food-frequency questionnaire. Percent energy from carbohydrates, fats, and protein was calculated. CFr was defined as the ratio of percent energy from carbohydrates to that from fat. Frailty was defined as a Kihon Checklist score ≥ 7. Multivariable logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for frailty across CFr quartiles, adjusting for sociodemographic, lifestyle, and health-related factors. Restricted cubic splines assessed dose-response associations overall and within sex-specific tertiles of protein intake. RESULTS: Among the 5679 participants, 1705 (30.0%) had comprehensive frailty. Compared with the lowest CFr quartile, the adjusted ORs were 1.12 (95% CI, 0.92-1.36) for Q2, 1.44 (1.18-1.76) for Q3, and 1.92 (1.55-2.38) for Q4 (P for trend < 0.001). Positive associations were also observed across sex-specific protein-intake tertiles, with no evidence of effect modification by protein intake. CONCLUSION: A higher CFr is associated with a higher prevalence of comprehensive frailty in older Japanese adults, with broadly similar associations across protein-intake levels.

title: The Effect Of Accounting Digitization On Environmental Accounting Disclosure Through Human Resource Capacity In Msmes In Ambon City
source: Journal of Creative Power and Ambition
summary: This study aims to analyze the influence of accounting digitization on environmental accounting disclosure in MSMEs in Ambon City with human resource capacity as a mediation variable. The study uses a quantitative approach with an explanato
content: This study aims to analyze the influence of accounting digitization on environmental accounting disclosure in MSMEs in Ambon City with human resource capacity as a mediation variable. The study uses a quantitative approach with an explanatory survey of 113 respondents. Data was analyzed using statistical tests and Macro Hayes mediation analysis. The results of the study show that accounting digitization has a significant effect on human resource capacity, and human resource capacity has a significant effect on environmental accounting disclosure. However, accounting digitization does not have a direct effect on environmental accounting disclosure. Accounting digitization has an effect on environmental accounting disclosure through human resource capacity. This finding shows that human resource capacity is an important link between accounting digitization and environmental accounting disclosure in MSMEs in Ambon City.

title: Mapping the Economic and Fiscal Burden of Illicit Medicines: A Systematic Literature Review and Bibliometric Analysis Using VOSviewer
source: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
summary: Illicit medicines, including counterfeit and substandard pharmaceutical products, pose a growing threat to global health systems and economic stability, particularly in both developed and developing countries. This study conducts a systemat
content: Illicit medicines, including counterfeit and substandard pharmaceutical products, pose a growing threat to global health systems and economic stability, particularly in both developed and developing countries. This study conducts a systematic literature review combined with bibliometric mapping using VOSviewer to analyse the economic and fiscal implications of illicit medicine markets. A comprehensive search of peer-reviewed articles published between 1995 and 2025 was conducted from Scopus, following PRISMA guidelines. A total of eligible studies was analysed to identify key research trends, thematic clusters, and knowledge gaps. Bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer 16.20 revealed dominant research themes, including pharmaceutical regulation, supply chain vulnerabilities, public health risks, and economic burden. The findings indicate that illicit medicines contribute to significant tax revenue losses, increased healthcare costs due to treatment failure, and reduced productivity. Additionally, the expansion of informal pharmaceutical markets undermines formal sector employment and weakens regulatory systems. The review highlights the fragmented nature of existing research and the limited integration of fiscal and employment perspectives in current literature. It concludes that stronger regulatory frameworks, improved surveillance systems, and coordinated policy responses are essential to mitigate the economic and health impacts of illicit medicines. This study contributes to the literature by providing a comprehensive evidence synthesis and visual mapping of research trends to inform policy and future research.

title: Landscapes of Hybrid Activism
summary: The year 2022 marked the 10th anniversary of the course Critical Animal Studies: Animals in Society, Culture and the Media at the Department of Communication and Media at Lund University. As the first initiative of its kind in Sweden, the c
content: The year 2022 marked the 10th anniversary of the course Critical Animal Studies: Animals in Society, Culture and the Media at the Department of Communication and Media at Lund University. As the first initiative of its kind in Sweden, the course explores the shifting roles and positions of non-human animals in today’s complex societies. It aims to equip students with analytical tools to critically assess norms and structures that organise human-animal relations, along with their ethical, cultural, and social consequences. What started as a one-course offering driven by an idea has evolved into a decade-long project of education and emancipation for non- human animals. This anthology stands as a testament to the course’s impact, aiming to extend the rich discussions, debates, and insights cultivated beyond the classroom walls. This celebratory collection assembles writings from former students, instructors, and guest lecturers, delving into themes ranging from critical media analysis over activist strategies to pedagogical reflections. The anthology’s scope not only reflects the diverse facets of the course but also unveils the myriad, often subtle intersections between human-centered society and the lives of non-human animals.

title: Mass Protest and Civil Society Positioning in Romania
summary: Romania's contentious politics has been undergoing significant change in recent times, most visibly marked by repeated cycles of mass protest. Based on political ethnographic research conducted in Romania, this study conceptualises this pro
content: Romania's contentious politics has been undergoing significant change in recent times, most visibly marked by repeated cycles of mass protest. Based on political ethnographic research conducted in Romania, this study conceptualises this process by exploring activists’ meaning-making practices, using association/dissociation terminology from political difference theory. After a contextually determined momentum for mobilisation around 2010, outbreaks of spontaneous, self-organised and multi-thematic protests in the years since 2012 led to a liminal phase of civil society transformation, creating new networks of active people and enabling the appearance of political alternatives to the status quo. Since this disruption, the formation of a new, explicitly oppositional, branch of political civil society can be observed.

title: Comparative policy analysis of urban microplastic pollution and water quality management toward sustainable environmental governance in Malaysian cities
summary: Rapid urbanization in Southeast Asia has intensified microplastic (MP) pollution in city water bodies, urban drainage systems, and coastal environments, posing significant threats to urban water quality and public health. This study employs
content: Rapid urbanization in Southeast Asia has intensified microplastic (MP) pollution in city water bodies, urban drainage systems, and coastal environments, posing significant threats to urban water quality and public health. This study employs a comparative policy analysis to evaluate how global, regional, and national legislative frameworks address MP pollution as a critical urban water management challenge, with emphasis on ASEAN member states and Malaysia’s cities. Malaysian urban centres, particularly densely populated coastal cities such as Penang, Kuala Lumpur, and Johor Bahru, exhibit alarming MP contamination across urban water bodies, with reported concentrations ranging from 0.14 particles/L in coastal surface waters to 29,174 pieces/kg in urban sediments — values that reflect two different environmental media (water column versus sediment) and are therefore not directly comparable in magnitude, but together illustrate the pervasiveness of MP contamination across compartments driven by inadequate urban waste management infrastructure and insufficient stormwater governance. Despite Malaysia ranking third globally in marine plastic pollution contributions (73,098 metric tons annually), cities lack dedicated MP-specific urban water management legislation. This governance gap is particularly critical given MP contamination documented across urban Malaysian water bodies and sediments. The study identifies four critical urban governance challenges: (1) legislative fragmentation and weak enforcement in urban environmental management, (2) economic-environmental trade-offs in plastic-dependent urban economies, (3) insufficient municipal solid waste and wastewater infrastructure addressing MP sources, and (4) limited urban public awareness and multi-stakeholder engagement. Through systematic analysis of international regulatory models and ASEAN city-level initiatives, this research proposes an integrated urban environmental governance framework encompassing legislative amendments to the Environmental Quality Act 1974, establishment of city-scale MP monitoring protocols aligned with Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 11, implementation of Extended Producer Responsibility schemes for urban plastic waste, and enhancement of regional cooperation mechanisms. The findings offer actionable policy recommendations to improve urban water quality, strengthen sustainable municipal solid waste management, and promote resilient and sustainable cities, providing a replicable model for rapidly urbanizing developing nations facing similar urban environmental governance challenges.

title: Upstream land-use change and transboundary river water redistribution: a global mapping
source: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
summary: Transboundary river basins sustain over three billion people across 150 + nations; however, upstream land-use and land-cover change (LULCC) remains absent from the codified text of international water treaties. In this study, we present a g
content: Transboundary river basins sustain over three billion people across 150 + nations; however, upstream land-use and land-cover change (LULCC) remains absent from the codified text of international water treaties. In this study, we present a global, spatially explicit quantification of this governance blind spot, to our knowledge the first at treaty-comparable resolution. Using a basin-country-unit (BCU) framework spanning 313 transboundary basins, we mapped five upstream land-use transition types using MODIS satellite data (2001–2023), quantified their water consumption through climate-corrected evapotranspiration attribution, and expressed the result as a Silent Water Redistribution Index (SWRI) for all downstream territories. We find that upstream land use silently removes −31.66 km 3 yr. −1 from downstream water budgets, dominated by irrigation expansion (−36.37 km 3 yr. −1 ) and reforestation (−23.76 km 3 yr. −1 ), a signal corroborated by GRACE satellite gravity in 62% of the 13 basins in which the redistributed volume reaches at least 1% of the receiving country’s renewable water resources. Systematic comparison with water treaty records reveals that international water agreements leave 78.5% of the global signal ungoverned, exposing millions of people in downstream territories to unrecognized hydrological impacts. The reforestation paradox, wherein climate finance incentivizes upstream afforestation that reduces downstream water availability, warrants institutional attention. Our SWRI framework provides the quantitative foundation for integrating land-use governance into institutional water law.
